Zoomed out below the window size, the slide is centred. On main the point moved from (768, 378) to (384, 191) on the first pinch.

title: Charts: value axes start above zero when the values sit high, as in Office
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Related to #144.

## Context
This PR first fixed #144: the issue's data (42.1, 18.7, 6.3) drew 0–50 in steps of 10, where PowerPoint and LibreOffice draw 0–45 in steps of 5. Upstream ce1c7b7 ("Charts: axis number formats, automatic major unit, hidden axes") has since rewritten the value-axis scaling, and `main` now draws the issue's chart as 0–45 in steps of 5. So the branch now merges `main` and keeps upstream's structure and API as they are: `axis_scale(lo, hi, fmin, fmax, major, max_intervals, headroom)`, `Chart::axis_scale(secondary, max_intervals)`, `axis_range`, combo charts with a secondary axis, the room-based major unit, number formats and hidden axes. This PR's own `auto_scale` and its fixed "at most 10 intervals" unit rule are gone.

## What this adds on top of upstream
These are the documented rules for automatic axis limits (Microsoft's "How chart axis limits are determined", summarised by Jon Peltier) that `main` doesn't follow yet:

- **Automatic minimum:** `main` always starts the axis at zero. Office starts at zero only when every value is ≥ 0 and the smallest is below 5/6 of the largest. Otherwise the axis starts at the first major unit at or below `min − (max − min)/20`. Values of 85, 92 and 97 now get an 84–98 axis instead of bars that all look the same height.
- **All-negative data mirrors it:** the axis ends at zero only when the largest value is above 5/6 of the smallest. Otherwise it ends at the first major unit at or above `max + (max − min)/20`. (`main` didn't pad the top of an all-negative axis.) Mixed signs keep headroom at both ends, as on `main`.
- **Headroom** is 5 % of the data range (`max − min`), as documented, not of the range from zero. A single value is measured from zero, so it still gets headroom.
- **Values outside the axis limits stop at the plot edge** (`to_v` and `to_axis` in the renderer). This covers values past a fixed `<c:max>`/`<c:min>`, and bars that start at zero on an axis that now starts above zero. On `main` they …

title: Notes: speaker notes show their formatting and keep it when edited
author: Mathiasko
body:
Speaker notes with formatting (a bold first line, indented points with bullets) showed as plain lines in the notes pane and in Notes Page. Editing them there also dropped all of that formatting from the notes, and from the saved .pptx.

**Cause:** import and export were fine (`read_notes` keeps the full text body, `notes_xml` writes it back). The UI was the problem: both editors were a plain `egui::TextEdit` over `Slide::notes_text()` (`status.rs`, `sorter.rs`), and on blur they saved through `slide.notes {text}`, which did `TextBody::from_text` and wiped every bold run, level, indent and bullet of the slide's notes.

**What changed:**
- ui-egui: new `notes.rs`, one notes editor shared by the notes pane and Notes Page.
  - Draws bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and size from the runs, and each paragraph's margin, hanging indent and bullet or number. Symbol-font bullets (Wingdings `§` etc.) are mapped the same way as on slides.

  - Each edit is applied to a formatted draft, so typed text takes the formatting where it lands (Enter in a bulleted point starts another). The draft is saved when the field loses focus or the slide changes. This also fixes an older case where an edit could be dropped if the field lost focus between frames.
- engine: `slide.notes` takes `body` (formatted notes), and `slide.inspect` returns `notesBody`. `slide.notes {text}` now changes only the retyped text (new `deckcraft_model::edit::replace_text`); text that shares nothing with the old notes still comes in as plain text.

title: Bidi: auto-detect RTL paragraph direction when typing Kurdish, Arabic and Hebrew
author: Hevarh1
body:
### Problem
When typing in Kurdish, Arabic, Hebrew or other right-to-left scripts in a new presentation, shape, or paragraph, the base direction was defaulting to Left-to-Right (`props.rtl: None` resolved to LTR, and paragraph alignment defaulted to `Align::Left`).
Under LTR base direction:
- The line was anchored at the left margin.
- Visual reordering placed each newly typed RTL character at the left edge of the run.
- The caret jumped back to the start of the line (left margin) on every keystroke, and jumped to the far right on space keys (due to UAX #9 rule L1).

### Solution
1. **UAX #9 Rule P2/P3 Auto-Detection**: Added `deckcraft_model::bidi::first_strong_is_rtl` to determine if a paragraph's first strong directional character belongs to an RTL script (Arabic, Kurdish, Hebrew, Syriac, Thaana, etc., or directional marks `\u{200F}`).
2. **Layout Fallback**: In `crates/text/src/lib.rs` (`shape_para`), unassigned paragraph direction (`props.rtl.is_none()`) resolves to `rtl = true` if the text starts with an RTL script, and defaults unassigned alignment to `Align::Right` (anchoring to the right margin and advancing leftwards). Explicit user alignment overrides (`Align::Left`, `Align::Center`, etc.) remain preserved.
3. **Interactive Typing Promotion**: In `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs` (`insert_text`, `paste_body`, `set`), when inserting text into a paragraph with unassigned direction (`props.rtl.is_none()`), if the paragraph starts with an RTL character, it is automatically promoted to RTL (`props.rtl = Some(true)` and `props.align = Some(Align::Right)`), matching PowerPoint / Word behavior and persisting to PPTX/JSON. Explicit user overrides (`props.rtl = Some(false)`) are never overwritten.
4. **Regression Tests**:
   - Added unit tests in `crates/model/src/bidi.rs` for `first_strong_is_rtl`.
   - Added layout auto-detection test in `crates/text/src/tests.rs`.
   - Added end-to-end typing regression test in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` verifying sequential cha…

title: Slide show: the arrow keys work while Presenter View has the focus (#17)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Part of #17 ("Arrow buttons (Left-Right) do not work when presenting"). #17 lists other unrelated problems too, so this doesn't close it.

**Cause.** Presenter View is on by default and opens a second window with `show_viewport_immediate`. winit focuses a new window by default, and keys go only to the focused window. The show's key handler reads only the main window's input (`ctx.input` in `show::ui`), so every key pressed after the show started went to Presenter View and was ignored. Clicking the slide gives the show window the focus back, which is why the keys sometimes seemed to work.

Evidence: I logged `viewport().focused` for both windows during a real show on macOS. The main window had the focus for the first frame only, and Presenter View had it for every frame after that (`root=Some(false) presenter=Some(true)`).

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs`)
- The key mapping moves unchanged into `Show::key`, with `pressed_keys` collecting the frame's key presses.
- Presenter View passes its own key presses to the same handler, so ←/→, Space, Page Up/Down, B/W, Home/End, number + Enter and Esc work whichever window has the focus (as in PowerPoint's Presenter View).
- An embedded Presenter View (web, tests) shares the show's input, which the show already reads, so it's skipped there and each key is handled once.

**Tests**
- New `show_keys_move_one_slide_with_presenter_view_open` (kittest): with Presenter View open, → → ← lands on slides 1, 2, 1. Removing the embedded-viewport guard makes it fail (each key moves two slides), so it checks that guard.
- The focused-Presenter-View path can't be driven from the control port (synthetic input only reaches the main window). It still needs a check with a real key press in a packaged build.
- In the running app over `--control`: →, →, ←, ←, End, Home still step through builds and slides from the main window.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.

title: macOS: build the DMG with hdiutil create so the app passes codesign --strict
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #50.

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` puts a `com.apple.FinderInfo` on every file it writes into the image. The app is signed before that, so DeckCraft.app inside the released DMG, and any `ditto` copy of it, fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` with "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed". The script only re-checked the DMG's own signature after imaging, so this went unnoticed.

This is the fix PdfCraft and LightCraft already shipped (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/823, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/959), ported to `packaging/macos/package.sh`:

- The image is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies and can hit "Resource busy" on CI runners, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses.
- `xattr -cr` on the bundle before signing, so nothing picked up during the build ends up under the signature.
- After the DMG is signed, the script mounts it read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside and on a `ditto` copy of it, plus `spctl --assess` on the copy when notarizing. Any failure stops the release and prints the app's xattrs.
- The volume name stays `DeckCraft` and `.DS_Store` / `.background` are copied as before, so the window layout is unchanged.
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` no longer says the DMG is built with `makehybrid`.

Testing: I don't have a Mac, so this was not run. I checked the script with `bash -n` and shellcheck 0.11 (clean) and compared it line by line with the PdfCraft change, which was verified on macOS (the new gate passes, and fails with the old `makehybrid` lines put back). The release workflow's macOS job is what will actually exercise it; the new check after imaging makes that job fail loudly if something is off.

title: Windows: compile DX12 shaders with FXC
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Windows the app quit right after the window appeared with "Parent device is lost". wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` it finds on the DLL search path. DeckCraft ships none, and without a matching `dxil.dll` DXC warns that the DXIL is unsigned. wgpu treats that warning as a compile error, its indirect-validation pipeline fails and the device is lost.

The fix sets the DX12 compiler to FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) in `graphics::configure`, next to the existing DX12-only backend default. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still overrides it for troubleshooting, the same way `WGPU_BACKEND` overrides the backends. This is the same change as storytold/cadcraft#613 (and storytold/lightcraft#484, storytold/gridcraft#382). The README's Windows troubleshooting section mentions it.

Tested with a unit test in graphics.rs that starts from `Auto` and checks `configure` leaves FXC. It failed before the change and passes now, and a second test checks an explicit compiler choice is kept. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 6 steps).

Not verified: I built on Linux only, where the `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` call in main.rs isn't compiled (no Windows target installed here), so Windows CI is what checks that line. Nobody ran it on a Windows machine.

author: Mathiasko
body:
Fixes #171.

## Problem
There was no way to turn a presentation into an animated GIF: `docs/file-format-parity.md` listed "Animated GIF of the deck" as export: no, `docs/gaps.md` had it under "No video or animated GIF export", and the checklist row was M. PowerPoint's Export ▸ Create an Animated GIF is a common way to share a short deck.

## What changed
- `file.export` writes an animated GIF (format `gif`, or a `.gif` path): one frame per slide from the slide renderer, shown for `secondsPerSlide`, through the `image` crate's GIF encoder (already a dependency; no new crates). Each frame gets its own 256-colour palette: exact when the slide has 256 colours or fewer, NeuQuant otherwise. Slides are composited onto white.

- Never crash: wrong types, out-of-range values, NaN and infinities are parameter errors; at most 500 frames and 200 million pixels in total, checked before anything is rendered.
- The Export… dialog gets "Animated GIF (.gif)" with Size, Seconds per slide, From/To slide, Loop forever and Include hidden slides; an invalid range or value keeps the dialog open with a message. The web build downloads the GIF.

title: PDF: map each glyph to its shaping cluster's text in ToUnicode (#164)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #164.

The PDF text layer gave each glyph its text range by position. That worked only when a run had exactly one glyph per character. When a run had fewer or more glyphs than characters (for example a ligature such as "fl"), glyph 0 got the whole run's text and every other glyph got nothing. The ToUnicode CMap then mapped one glyph to a whole sentence and left codes like `<0002>` with no mapping. poppler rejected the long entries, and text extraction came out garbled.

The cluster data the issue asks for is already available: `GlyphRun.cells` holds, for each glyph, the paragraph character that heads its shaping cluster. The new helper `glyph_text_ranges` uses it:

- A cluster runs from its head to the next cluster head in the run, or to the end of the run. A ligature glyph therefore maps to all of its characters ("fl" maps to `f` and `l`), and every other glyph maps to its own character.
- All glyphs of one cluster (for example a base letter and a combining mark, or kashida fill) share the cluster's range. krilla treats glyphs with the same range as one cluster and writes the text only once.
- Ranges are computed from cluster heads, not from glyph order, so right-to-left runs (glyphs in visual order) get the correct characters too. krilla then marks them as reversed.
- A glyph with no cell gets an empty range, the same as the old code gave it. Every range stays inside the run's text, so krilla's `text[range]` cannot panic.

Rendering does not change, because the text layer is invisible.

Test: `glyph_ranges_follow_shaping_clusters` in `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs` covers an "fl" ligature, a two-glyph cluster, and a right-to-left run that starts mid-paragraph and uses multi-byte characters. With the old logic, the ligature case maps the whole word to glyph 0.

title: CLI: --help prints usage and unknown render flags are rejected (#163)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #163.

`deckcraft-cli render --help` wrote a PNG named `--help`, because `render()` sent every unrecognised `--flag` to its catch-all arm, which made it the output path. A misspelled flag such as `--scael` was handled the same way.

Each point of the issue:

- **`render --help` / `-h`** now print the usage and exit 0 without touching the filesystem.
- **Unknown `render` options** (anything starting with `-` that is not a known flag) now fail with ``unknown option `--scael` ``, the same error `run` already gives for its unknown options.
- **`info`, `convert`, `run`, `commands`** print the usage and exit 0 on `--help` / `-h`, instead of opening a file called `--help`, complaining about missing arguments, or filtering the command list by "--help".
- **Top-level `deckcraft-cli --help` / `-h` / `help`** print the usage to stdout and exit 0. Running with no arguments or an unknown subcommand still prints it to stderr and exits 1.
- **`describe`, `app`, `mcp`** had the same problem (`describe --help` said "unknown command", `app --help` tried to reach the app, `mcp --help` said "unknown mcp option"), so they now take `--help` / `-h` too.

All of them print the full usage block, which is the only help text the CLI has.

Tests in `apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs`:

- `render_help_prints_usage_and_writes_nothing`: `render --help` and `render -h` succeed and no `--help` file is created.
- `render_rejects_unknown_flag`: `render --sample --scael 2 out.png` returns the unknown-option error and writes nothing.
- `other_subcommands_accept_help`: `info`, `convert`, `run`, `describe` and `mcp` accept `--help` / `-h`.

All three fail on `main`.

title: control server: bound request lines and concurrent connections
author: SteamSmith

## Summary

`apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs` (the opt-in `--control` loopback channel) read request lines with `BufRead::lines`, which buffers an entire line before anything checks its size, and spawned one thread per accepted connection with no limit.

- **Bounded line reads:** each line is read with `take(MAX_LINE + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`. A line longer than `MAX_LINE` = 256 MiB (generous, since requests can carry documents or media as base64) gets an error reply and the connection is closed, without buffering the rest. Previously there was no line limit at all.
- **Connection cap:** at most `MAX_CONNECTIONS` = 16 connections are served at once; further ones get `{"ok": false, "error": "too many control connections"}` and are closed. A slot is released when its connection ends, including if its thread can't start or panics (`Drop` guard).

Everything else in request handling is unchanged (blank lines skipped, same replies, same timeouts). The approach mirrors DesignCraft's control server.

## Tests

New tests in `control_server.rs`:
- `lines_are_read_up_to_the_limit`: line at the limit accepted, CRLF stripped, final line without newline read, then end of stream
- `an_overlong_line_is_refused_without_reading_the_rest`: at most limit+1 bytes buffered, remainder left unread
- `requests_are_answered_with_their_ids`: end to end over a loopback socket with a stand-in UI
- `extra_connections_are_refused`: the 17th concurrent connection gets the error line

## How this was verified

On my Windows machine, Smart App Control blocks a dependency's build script (`parking_lot_core`), so I couldn't build the full app locally. Instead I compiled **this exact file**, unmodified, as a module of a small harness crate with stand-ins for `egui::Context` and `ControlRequest`. All four new tests pass there, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic` is clean on it. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes in the repo. The repo's …

title: Slides: Ctrl+A in the slide pane selects every slide (#188)
author: isaac-levine
body:
Clicking in the slide thumbnails and pressing Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac) now selects every slide, like PowerPoint does. Before this the shortcut always ran `edit.selectAll`, which selects the shapes on the current slide no matter where you clicked.

`edit.selectAll` now takes an optional `scope: "slides"`, the same convention `edit.cut`, `edit.copy`, `edit.paste` and `edit.delete` already use. With it, every slide is selected (hidden ones too), shape and text selection is cleared, and the current slide stays where it is so the canvas doesn't jump. Any other scope value is an error, and so is calling it while a master or layout is being edited. Without a scope nothing changes.

I didn't reuse the `slides_scope` heuristic from `edit.delete`. The selection normally contains the current slide, so that heuristic would have hijacked Ctrl+A on the canvas too. Since the engine can't see which pane has focus, the UI tracks it: `SlideApp::slides_focused` follows the last primary click (inside the thumbnail pane or not), the sorter always counts, and `menus::ui_shortcut` sends the scoped command in that case.

Tests: engine tests for one slide, several slides with one hidden, the current slide staying put, the unscoped path being unchanged, and a bad scope returning an error. An egui_kittest test clicks a thumbnail, presses Cmd+A and checks all three slides are selected, then clicks the canvas and checks Cmd+A selects shapes again.

fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass, and `cargo xtask parity` produced no changes. I haven't taken a screenshot of the running app, the kittest harness is the only UI coverage.

Fixes #188

title: Equations on slides: laid out and edited in place with equaSHion
author: shuff57
body:
## Summary

Typeset equations on slides, edited in place with the equaSHion editor (a pure-Rust equation editor).

- **Layout:** equations on a slide are laid out by equaSHion, in the style the slide draws them in.
- **Editing:** click an equation to edit it in place (the same gesture as in WordCraft); Alt+= opens the editor. The widget draws only the caret and selection, over the slide's own text.
- **Ribbon:** an Equation tab with equaSHion's galleries, symbol sets and ready-made equations, laid out as WordCraft's (Tools, Symbols, Structures, Equation Options). Insert > Equation is a split button with the ready-made equations.
- **Import and paste:** PPTX import keeps self-contained OMML, linear text and run formatting. Pasting one OMML, MathML or delimited-LaTeX equation inserts it.
- **Commands:** `insert.equation`, `equation.update`, `equation.get`, `equation.fromLinear`; equation runs are atoms in the text model.
- **Hosting:** `ui-egui` gains `context_changed()` so a host shell (OfficeCraft) can re-install fonts and visuals when it brings this app's tab back.

## Relation to #55

#55 is the earlier attempt at the same feature (its own `deckcraft-math` crate). This branch replaces
that approach with equaSHion and is based on the current `main` with no conflicts. If this is the
direction you prefer, #55 can be closed in its favour; if not, this can be dropped.

The equaSHion crates are **git dependencies pinned to a revision of `shuff57/equaSHion`** (see
`Cargo.toml`), the repo they live in today. Before this merges they should come from a repo the org
owns (or be vendored), and the pin updated.

## Testing

Built and exercised as a tab inside OfficeCraft (https://github.com/shuff57/officecraft). I have not
run this repo's full CI on this branch.

title: Animation effects: follow the system's reduced-motion setting
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

With animation effects switched off in the OS (Windows 11: Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visual effects ▸ Animation effects), DeckCraft still animated its own interface: wheel scrolling and Ctrl+wheel zooming eased in over several frames, and menus, tooltips and dialogs faded in.

## What this changes

DeckCraft's own motion now follows the system setting by default, with an override in Preferences.

With effects off:

- A wheel notch scrolls the slide, the thumbnails, the Slide Sorter and every list by the whole notch at once.
- Ctrl/⌘+wheel zooms the slide and the Slide once.
- Menus, tooltips and dialogs don't fade in, and scroll areas don't glide to a target.
- A setting changed while DeckCraft is running is followed without a restart.

Where the setting is read:

| Platform | Source |
|---|---|
| Windows | Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visua (`UISettings.AnimationsEnabled`) |
| macOS | Accessibility ▸ Display ▸ Reduce motion (`NSWorkspace`) |
| Linux / BSD | XDG settings portal (`reduced-motion`, GNOME `enable-animations`, KDE `AnimationDurationFactor`), falling back to `kdeglobals` and GTK `settings.ini` where no portal answers |
| Web | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query |

Where the system reports nothing, animations

## Interface

- **Preferences ▸ Animation effects:** Use system setting (default), On, Off. While it follows the system, the dialog  shows what was detected.
- **Command:** `view.animationEffects` takes `{mode: "system"|"on"|"off"}` or `{on: bool}` (toggles without either) and answers `{mode, on, system}`.
- **Control channel:** `ui.set` accepts `animationEffects`; `ui.inspect` reports `animationsOn` and `systemAnimations`.
- **Saved state:** `animationEffects` in `ui.json`. An older file, or an unreadable value, loads as Use system setting without losing the other preferences.

## Not affected

What a presentation plays — transitions, slide animations, animated GIFs, video — is its content and runs as authored. Set Up Slide Show ▸ Show…

title: Portable mode: portable.txt beside the exe keeps settings there (#200)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #200.

If a `portable.txt` sits beside the DeckCraft executable, `ui.json`, `prefs.json`, `logs/` and the AutoRecover files go to `<exe dir>/DeckCraftData` instead of `%APPDATA%\DeckCraft` (or the macOS/Linux equivalents) — the same trigger file PhotoCraft uses.

title: PPTX: SmartArt and OLE objects we can't draw keep their parts on save (#203)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes the data loss in #203 (both reproductions).

**Cause**: an object DeckCraft doesn't model (`ShapeKind::Opaque`) kept its `graphicFrame` XML, but not the parts that XML references. On save, any frame with relationship references was written as its preview picture or an empty rectangle — so `ppt/diagrams/*` and `ppt/embeddings/oleObject*.bin` were dropped.

**Fix**
- `Opaque` gets `parts: Vec<(rel id, relationship type, MediaId)>` (serde default, so existing `.deckcraft` files load unchanged). The reader fills it with every part the frame's XML references.
- The writer re-adds those parts under fresh slide relationship ids and rewrites the ids in the kept XML. If any reference can't be satisfied it falls back exactly as before (preview + `log::warn!`).
- `opc::Rel` now also keeps the full relationship type URI, so non-`officeDocument` types are written back correctly.
- **SmartArt**: a diagram's data part names its cached drawing by a *slide* relationship id (`dsp:dataModelExt relId`), which a save renumbers. That link is dropped from the kept data part. Only diagrams whose drawing is missing or empty reach this path (otherwise the drawing is already imported as a group).
- **Legacy OLE**: these objects find their preview in the slide's VML drawing through `spid`. DeckCraft doesn't write that drawing, and PowerPoint refuses to open a file with a dangling `spid`. The reader now takes the preview from the VML drawing (so DeckCraft shows it too), and the writer emits PowerPoint's own fallback form: no `spid`, preview as `p:pic`.
- Still falls back to the preview: a referenced part with relationships of its own, or an external link.

**Verified in PowerPoint (Microsoft 365, via COM)** with the issue's files, saved by `deckcraft-cli run --in … --save …` once, twice in a row, and via `.deckcraft` and back:
- `smartart-org-chart.pptx`: opens; the frame is real SmartArt with 5 nodes (Manager/Second para, Employee, Employee2, Assistant, Manager2) and draws as the org cha…

title: Outlines: Markdown headings make slides, list items are their bullets (#211)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #211.

**Cause**: `.md` outlines went through the plain outline rules (unindented line = slide, indentation = bullet level), so `# Intro` kept its `#` and every top-level `- item` became a slide.

**Fix** (`outline_to_slides`, `crates/format/src/lib.rs`): when the text contains any ATX heading (`#`…`######` followed by a space), each heading is a slide title (closing `#`s trimmed) and every line under it is a bullet nested by its list indentation (`- a` level 0, `  - b` level 1). Text without headings reads exactly as before.

Detecting by content rather than by extension means the same fix applies to every path into the parser: File ▸ Open of a `.md`, a dropped `.md`, and Insert ▸ Slides from Outline with pasted Markdown. A `#hashtag` (no space) is not a heading.

**Verified**
- The issue's `outline.md`: `deckcraft-cli info` reports 2 slides, *Intro* and *Second*; rendered slide 1 shows *Point one*, *Point two* and the nested *Sub point*.
- New `markdown_outline` test (headings, `##` with closing hashes, `*` items, nested item, `#hashtag`); existing `outline_roundtrip` unchanged; `cargo test -p deckcraft-format -p deckcraft-engine`; clippy `-D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check`.

Not handled: numbered list markers (`1.`) keep their number in the bullet text.

title: CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents in words
author: hoblin
body:
An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` reads its answers as is. Many of them didn't say what happened: a wrong command name was reported as broken JSON, a missing shape didn't say which or where, `null` didn't say what changed, and unknown parameter keys were silently ignored. Each one cost the agent extra turns on every deck.

Now every answer reads like a sentence written for a person. An error says how the CLI read the input, what is wrong with it, and the form that works, taken from the command's own params doc. It never guesses what the agent meant.

## Before and after

Real calls; "before" is `main`, "after" is this branch.

### 1. The command name

The agent wants a new blank presentation. It read `ID` in the help, `--cmd ID=JSON`, as a label of its own.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'new=file.new={"blank":true}'
right:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"blank":true}'

before: deckcraft-cli: new: bad JSON: expected ident at line 1 column 2
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 1 of 1 was read as command `new` with parameters `file.new={"blank":true}`.
        `new` is not a command: --cmd takes COMMAND=PARAMS, a command id, then `=`, then a JSON object,
        e.g. --cmd 'slide.new={"title":"Q3"}'. Nothing ran.
```

### 2. A shape on another slide

The agent resizes a shape it drew on slide 0 after `slide.new` moved it to slide 1. Shape ids are looked up on the slide being edited.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'shape.insert={…}' --cmd slide.new --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' --save deck.deckcraft
right:  … --cmd 'slide.go={"index":0}' --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' …

before: deckcraft-cli: invalid parameters for `shape.resize`: no such shape
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 3 of 3: shape 260 is on slide index 0, but shape ids are looked up on slide index 1,
        the one being edited; slide.go {"index": 0} switches to slide index 0. Nothing was saved or exported.
```

`edit.select`, `edit.delete`, `arrange.*` and every other command…

title: Animations: nine PowerPoint exit effects import as themselves (#147)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #147: PowerPoint exit animations losing their motion and direction on import.

**What the issue's video shows** (frames checked): the buildings use **Float In** to enter and a **Float Out** with the *Float Down* option to leave. In DeckCraft's show they fade out in place instead of sinking. Re-picking the option in DeckCraft fixes it, because then DeckCraft writes its own form.

**Cause**: PowerPoint writes *Float Down* as its own preset, **47** ("Descend"), not as Float (42) with a direction. DeckCraft only knew 42, so a Float Down entrance or exit imported as a plain Fade. Black-box probing of every PowerPoint effect also turned up 9 more exit effects with the same problem.

**How I checked** (PowerPoint via COM): every animation effect id, as entrance and exit, in every direction PowerPoint accepts, saved and compared with what DeckCraft imports.

**Fix**
- **Float Down (47)** imports as `float` / `floatOut` with option `d`, and is written back as preset 47 (subtype 0).
- **9 exits** that mirror an entrance DeckCraft already plays now import as themselves, with their direction. The show plays each as its entrance in reverse:

| PowerPoint exit (preset) | DeckCraft effect | directions |
|---|---|---|
| Float Out, Float Down (47) | `floatOut` + `d` | — |
| Blinds (3) | `blindsOut` | horz / vert |
| Box (4) | `boxOut` | in / out |
| Checkerboard (5) | `checkerboardOut` | across / down |
| Diamond (8) | `diamondOut` | in / out |
| Peek Out (12) | `peekOut` | b / l / t / r |
| Strips (18) | `stripsOut` | lu / ru / ld / rd |
| Sink Down (37) | `sinkDown` | — (plays as Rise Up leaving downward) |
| Spinner (49) | `spinnerOut` | — |
| Contract (55) | `contract` | — |

- Saving writes matching filters, plus up/down motion for Float Out and Sink Down (Float Out previously wrote only a fade).
- The other 22 exits (Crawl Out, Collapse, Pinwheel, …) have no DeckCraft entrance to mirror and still fade.

**Verified**
- PowerPoint probe decks re-imported: Float Down import…

title: Title bar: on macOS the window buttons sit centred in it (#71)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #71.

On macOS the window extends into the title bar and AppKit draws the traffic lights itself; moving them would need AppKit calls (`unsafe`), so the title bar has to fit them instead. DeckCraft's bar was 38 pt tall, so the lights sat 3 pt above its centre line. On macOS the bar is now 32 pt, centred on the lights, the quick-access buttons start after the three lights with the same gap the lights keep from the top (78 pt, was a fixed 84), and the Present button drops from 26 to 22 pt to keep a margin. Linux, Windows and web are unchanged (`TITLE_H` stays 38 pt).

The approach is the one from wordcraft #255 and gridcraft #323, but the constants were measured on a real macOS 27 window: lights 14 pt across, 23 pt centre to centre, the first at x = 9 pt, centred 16 pt from the top. Those PRs use 12 / 20 / 10 (a 28 pt band), which matches macOS 15 and earlier; on macOS 26+ that leaves the lights about 2 pt below the bar's centre and the first button about 1 pt from the green light. Happy to send the same follow-up to both. With this PR, on macOS 15 and earlier (12 pt lights centred at 14 pt) the lights would sit about 2 pt above the bar's centre, with a wider gap before the first button.

Validation:
- Ran the app on macOS 27 (Apple silicon) and captured the real window before and after (attached). After: 32 pt bar, lights centred on it, quick-access icons centred within 0.5 pt of them, 9 pt between the green light and the Home button.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib title_bar_tests`: a geometry test that fails if the macOS bar goes back to 38 pt, the content inset back to 84 pt or the Present button back to 26 pt.
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask wasm` (macOS 27, Apple silicon).

I have before/after captures of the real window if they help; happy to attach them.

title: Notes and Presenter View: long notes scroll, presenter controls show (#221)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes the two bugs in #221; likely also what #202 ("presenter view doesn't work") ran into.

**1. Long speaker notes spill over the slide.** The notes `TextEdit` wasn't in a scroll area, so a long note drew above its pane and over the slide (and stretched the pane, whose height is saved). It now scrolls inside the pane at the pane's height.

**2. Presenter View "has no buttons".** The buttons were there but invisible: the default (light-theme) button text is dark grey on the presenter window's near-black background. They now draw light text on a visible fill. The issue also asks to pause and restart the timer, so the timer gets **Pause / Resume** and **Reset**.

Not in this PR: rearranging the presenter layout (moving the notes relative to the next-slide preview).

**Verified in the running app** (Windows, `--sample`, control channel + real mouse clicks on the presenter window):
- 40 lines of notes: before, they covered the bottom of the slide; after, they scroll inside the default-height pane and the slide is untouched.
- Presenter View: before, the controls were barely visible top-right; after, they are clearly drawn. Clicking **Next** builds the next bullet / slide, **Pause** freezes the timer (same value 4 s later) and turns into **Resume**, and **Reset** sets it to 00:00:00.
- New `presenter_timer_pauses_resumes_and_resets` test; `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.

On a single monitor the full-screen show covers the presenter window (it has to be brought forward). Putting the show on the second monitor for #202 isn't covered here; I only have one monitor to test with.

author: xmaks82

title: Text: draw shrink-on-overflow at the scale the file was saved with
author: xmaks82
body:
PowerPoint draws `<a:normAutofit fontScale=… lnSpcReduction=…/>` text at the saved scale; we read those values but ignored them in `layout()` and only shrank when our own layout overflowed. Saved decks showed larger text and wider line spacing than PowerPoint, with text running past its placeholder.

- `layout()` starts from the saved scale and reduction (non-finite/out-of-range values ignored) and still shrinks further when the text doesn't fit at it.
- `edit_text` resets the saved scale after an edit, so changed text is fitted afresh (PowerPoint refits on edit); otherwise shortened text would stay shrunk.

**Checked** against PowerPoint's PDF export of 31 real decks (597 slides), together with the glow fix: 59 slides closer to PowerPoint, 1 slightly further (line breaks moved by font-width differences); slide count matches on all decks.

Tests: `saved_shrink_scale_is_drawn` (text), `editing_text_refits_a_saved_shrink` (engine). `cargo test --workspace` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Charts: draw combo charts with columns, lines and a secondary axis
author: xmaks82
body:
A combo chart (columns plus lines, the lines often on a second value axis) was read with each series' type but drawn as lines only, on one scale: a weekly spend-and-clicks chart showed the clicks as a flat line along the bottom and no columns at all.

- **Reading** (`read/chart.rs`): a plot group whose value axis isn't the first group's is on the secondary axis — `Series::secondary_axis` existed but was never set.
- **Model**: `Chart::series_kind`, `on_secondary`, `axis_range(secondary)` (a combo stacks only its stacked series; `y_min`/`y_max` apply to the primary axis). `value_range` unchanged for single-type charts.
- **Rendering** (`render/chart.rs`): bar-like series drawn as bars (clustered or stacked among themselves), the others as lines/areas over them, each against its own axis; the secondary axis' labels on the right. Line series take their line's colour and width (`c:spPr/a:ln`), also in the legend. Long category labels (date ranges) wrap onto two lines.

Writing is unchanged (an unmodified chart round-trips through `Chart.raw`).

**Checked** against PowerPoint's PDF export: the combo chart in a real deck now has its columns, both lines on the right-hand scale and their colours as in PowerPoint; on 31 decks / 597 slides nothing else changed (3 slides slightly closer). Remaining differences are axis number formats (`#,##0 ₽`) and major-unit choice.

Tests: `combo_axis_ranges` (model), `combo_chart_with_a_secondary_axis` (pptx), `combo_chart_draws_columns_and_a_line_on_its_own_axis` (render; fails before). `cargo test --workspace` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: deckcraft-cli help explains the CLI to an agent
author: hoblin
body:
**Stacked on #219.** Its change arrives here as one squashed commit ("CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents in words"); the rest is this PR. Once #219 merges, this diff shrinks to the help change alone.

An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` learns the input language from its help. The help described the CLI in its own grammar: `--cmd ID[=JSON]`, which an agent read as "a label of my own, then `=`". Nothing said that shape ids are looked up on the current slide, or what `format.*` acts on. Agents learned those by trial. Now the help explains the CLI the way the answers already do: in sentences written for a reader, with a full example.

This PR changes the help only. The input language is unchanged.

## Before and after

### `deckcraft-cli --help`

before: it is not a subcommand.
```
deckcraft-cli: unknown subcommand `--help`
usage: deckcraft-cli info FILE
       deckcraft-cli render (FILE | --sample) [--slide N | --all] [--scale S] [--edit] OUT

       …

title: "Not available" names only the keys a command takes
author: hoblin
body:
**Stacked on #228, which is stacked on #219.** Their changes arrive here as two squashed commits; the last commit is this PR. Once they merge, this diff shrinks to the fix alone.

When a command that needs selected shapes runs with nothing selected, its error told the agent to use `ids`, whatever the command takes. `shape.setDefault` takes no parameters, and `table.*` and `chart.*` take `id`, so an agent following the hint was refused. The hint now names only the key the command takes.

## Before and after

```
$ deckcraft-cli run --cmd shape.setDefault
before: command `shape.setDefault` is not available right now: nothing selected. It acts on `ids` or on the selected shapes; edit.select {"ids": […]} selects shapes.
after:  command `shape.setDefault` is not available right now: nothing selected. Acts on the selected shapes. edit.select {"ids": […]} selects shapes.

$ deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'shape.setDefault={"ids":[2]}'      (following the old hint)
        `shape.setDefault` was given `ids`, which it doesn't take. `shape.setDefault` takes no parameters.

$ deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'table.style={"style":"grid"}'
before: command `table.style` is not available right now: nothing selected. It acts on `ids` or on the selected shapes; edit.select {"ids": […]} selects shapes.
after:  command `table.style` is not available right now: nothing selected. Acts on the shape in `id`, else on the selected shapes. edit.select {"ids": […]} selects shapes.

$ deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'shape.resize={"w":5}'
after:  command `shape.resize` is not available right now: nothing selected. Acts on the shapes in `ids`, else on the selected shapes. edit.select {"ids": […]} selects shapes.
```

`how_to_enable` takes the command id, and for "nothing selected" and "select two or more objects" uses `CommandSpec::acts_on_for(reason)`. That is the sentence `describe` prints, worded from the gate and the `id`/`ids` keys the command takes. `acts_on()` is now built on it. The other hints are un…

title: Tables: caret in the edited cell, click-to-place, drag borders to resize
author: pierrevbc
body:
Tables: caret in the edited cell, click-to-place, drag borders to resize

## Problem

Editing a table felt broken even though the engine supported it:

- Double-clicking a cell entered cell editing (`TextSel.cell`) and outlined the cell, but no caret
  and no text selection were drawn (the canvas skipped them when `cell` was set and
  `text::layout_for` returned `None` for cells), so typing looked like it went nowhere. Up/Down/
  Home/End had no line layout in a cell, and the caret always started at the end of the cell.
- A click elsewhere in the table while editing a cell left editing instead of moving the caret.
- Row heights and column widths could only be changed through commands, not with the mouse.

## Changes

1. **Caret and selection in cells.** `cmd::text::text_frame(st, sel) -> (TextLayout, Affine)`
   covers shapes and cells; `layout_for`, hit testing (`tools::text_pos`) and the canvas go through

   `cmd::text::caret_line` (empty placeholders, end-of-line affinity), now extended to cells, and
   IME composition underlines (#101) use `text_frame` too, so they sit right in a cell.
   Up/Down/Home/End move by line inside a cell.
2. **Clicks.** Double-click puts the caret where clicked and selects the word; while a cell is

   after a double-click collapsing the word just selected (shapes too).
3. **Resize by dragging borders.** New hit kinds `TableColumn` / `TableRow` with resize cursors.
   An inner column border moves the two neighbouring columns and keeps the table width; the right

title: Charts: axis number formats, automatic major unit, hidden axes
author: xmaks82
body:
Value axes showed raw numbers (`800000`) on a fixed ~5-interval scale with fixed label gutters, deleted axes (`<c:delete val="1"/>`) were still drawn, and data labels ignored their number format — Russian business charts read `516600000` where PowerPoint shows `516 600 000 ₽`.

**Builds on #227** (combo charts); its commit is the first here — review the last commit.

- **`deckcraft_model::numfmt`** — Excel number format codes: positive/negative/zero sections, quoted and `\`-escaped literals, `_x` padding, `*x` fill, `[$sym-lcid]` currency, `[colour]`/conditions dropped, `0 # ?` placeholders, grouping by `,` or the locale's literal space (`# ##0`), trailing-comma scaling, `%`, `General`; digit grouping and decimal mark from the chart's `c:lang` (`ru-RU` → `800 000`, `12,5%`). Never panics (fuzz-ish test over malformed codes and non-finite values).
- **Reading** — per value axis: `numFmt`, `delete`, `scaling/min|max`, `majorUnit`, for the primary and a combo's secondary axis; data labels' `numFmt` (series, then group, else the source `numCache/formatCode`); `c:lang`. The primary value axis is now the one on the left/bottom and the secondary the one on the right/top or crossing at max, regardless of plot-group order (#227 took the first group's axis, which put columns on the wrong scale when the bar group sat on the right axis).
- **Scale** (`Chart::axis_scale`, `chart::axis_scale`) — fixed bounds/unit where given, else data + 5 % headroom rounded out to the smallest 1-2-5 unit leaving as many intervals as the axis has room for labels.
- **Rendering** — axis labels in their format, gutters sized to the longest label, deleted axes take no room, data labels in their format.

title: PPTX export: a workbook for edited and new charts, updated in place when the data changes
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

Since #355, an unchanged chart keeps the embedded workbook it was read with (and the other parts
its relationships reach, in `Chart.kept`) when the presentation is saved as PPTX. What is still
lost:

- **Any edit drops the workbook.** Every chart command (`chart.type`, `chart.data`,
  `chart.options`) clears `Chart.raw`, so after a title change, a new legend or one changed value
  the chart is no longer "unchanged" and is saved without `c:externalData` or a workbook. Edit Data
  in other presentation apps has nothing to open, and the workbook's other sheets, formulas and
  formatting are gone.
- **Charts made in DeckCraft have no workbook at all.**

Reproduce on `main` with a public file, not for committing:

1. `features/steps/test_files/cht-charts.pptx` from scanny/python-pptx (commit `278b47b`), or
   `test-data/slideshow/aascu.org_hbcu_leadershipsummit_cooper_.pptx` from apache/poi (slides 6
   and 7, one chart each).
2. `deckcraft-cli run --in cht-charts.pptx --cmd 'chart.options={"title":"New"}' --export out.pptx`
   (any chart command), or insert a chart and export.
3. `unzip -l out.pptx | grep embeddings` prints nothing for that chart; its `chartN.xml` has no
   `c:externalData`.

## Design

The workbook stays where #355 put it: in `Chart.kept`, the package parts an imported chart points
at. No new media item, no new field for it in the model. `ChartKept::workbook()` finds the kept
workbook part (the internal `package` or `oleObject` target of the chart's relationships).

On export, `Exp::chart_rel`:

1. **Unchanged chart** (its kept part still describes the model): #355's path, untouched. The

2. **Edited chart whose data still fits its original ranges** (`Chart.source`, commit 2): the
   chart part is written from the model with its original formulas, and the kept workbook is

title: SmartArt: text is laid out on its text rectangle (dsp:txXfrm), not in columns
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

In SmartArt imported from PPTX, the text of a pre-drawn shape is laid out inside the shape's own
box. SmartArt drawings give each shape a separate text rectangle, `dsp:txXfrm`, which DeckCraft
does not read. In list layouts the shape is a tall, narrow rounded rectangle turned by 90°, with a
text rectangle turned back by -90°: the text should run in wide horizontal lines, but it comes out
as narrow vertical columns of a few words each. The exported PPTX keeps the columns, since the
SmartArt is written back as a group of shapes.

Reproduce on `main` (0.6.0) with a public file, not for committing:

1. `2017/OWASP Top 10-2017 (en).pptx` from OWASP/Top10 (commit `3a31f35`), slides 20 ("What's Next
   for Organizations") and 21 ("What's Next for Application Managers").
2. `deckcraft-cli render "OWASP Top 10-2017 (en).pptx" --slide 19 --scale 1 out.png` (the CLI
   index starts at 0).
3. The bullet text of each row is split into vertical columns. Same after

The simple SmartArt of apache/poi (`test-data/slideshow/SmartArt.pptx`) renders fine: its text
rectangles match its shapes.

functions). After the drawing's shapes are read, each `dsp:sp` with a `dsp:txXfrm` gets its text
placed on that rectangle, read in the shape's coordinate space and turned by the shape's rotation

title: Canvas: drag the frame of a text box being edited to move it
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

Once a text box or placeholder is in text editing, it can't be dragged: every press inside its
box, border included, places the caret or starts a text selection. A click on an unselected text
box or placeholder enters editing straight away (like PowerPoint), so moving a text box takes an
extra step: click outside, then drag it before the click turns into editing. In PowerPoint,
grabbing the border of a box being edited moves it, with the move cursor on hover.

Reproduce on `main` (0.6.0):

1. `deckcraft --sample`, click into the title of slide 1: the caret appears.
2. Press on the title's dashed border and drag: the caret moves or text gets selected; the title
   doesn't move. The cursor over the border is the text cursor.

Cause: `Session::down` (`crates/engine/src/tools.rs`) sends any press inside the edited box's
axis-aligned bounds, inflated by the hit tolerance, to the caret. Only the resize, rotate and
adjust handles are checked first. The canvas shows the text cursor over the whole box while
editing (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`).

## What changes

Two commits: the change, and the progress docs.

- **Engine.** New `Hit::Frame { id }`: `hit_test` returns it, after the handles of the selection,
  when the point lies in a band the hit tolerance wide on either side of the edge of the box being
  edited. The test runs in the shape's own frame (`Xfrm::affine().inverse()`), so it follows
  rotation and flips; in very small boxes the inner half of the band shrinks to a quarter of the
  box so text stays reachable. Lines (connectors with text) and locked shapes have no frame.
- **Press on the frame** (`Session::down`): leaves text editing, selects the box and starts the
  usual `Drag::Move` (smart guides, snapping, Shift to constrain, Alt to duplicate), committed as
  one undo step ("Move"). A click without a drag only selects the box, with no undo step, as in
  PowerPoint.
- **Inside the box**, caret and text selection are unchanged. The zone now follow…

title: Canvas: right click selects the shape under the pointer
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

A right click on an unselected shape opens the slide's context menu (Layout, Reset Slide, Format
Background...), not the shape's: the shape has to be left-clicked first. In PowerPoint, the
right-button press selects what's under the pointer, then the menu matches it.

Reproduce on `main` (0.6.0): `deckcraft --sample`, right-click the title of slide 1 without
selecting it first: slide menu, title not selected.

Cause: the canvas only sends the primary button to `Session::pointer`
(`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `pointer`), and `context_menu` picks the shape or slide menu from
the current selection.

Expected (as in PowerPoint):

- unselected shape: selected alone (a text box or placeholder is not put into editing, nothing is
  dragged), shape menu;
- shape already selected, multiple selection included: selection kept;
- empty slide: selection cleared, slide menu;
- inside the text being edited: caret and text selection kept, and the menu acts on the text.

## What changes

Two commits: the change, and the progress docs.

- **Engine.** New `PointerKind::ContextClick` (`contextclick`, or `rightclick`, in `ui.pointer`
  and the MCP `pointer` tool). It selects as listed above and returns `{hit, selected, editing}`.
  It never edits text, starts a drag or adds an undo step, and does nothing while a drawing tool
  or a gesture is active. In the box being edited it uses the same zone as a left press that
  places the caret (the box's bounds inflated by the hit tolerance).
- **Canvas.** The secondary-button press goes through `Session::pointer` before egui opens the
  context menu (on release). While text is being edited, the menu shows text items: Cut, Copy and
  Paste (which already act on the selected text in text mode), Paragraph..., Bullets, Numbering,
  Link..., Format Shape....
- `docs/control-protocol.md` lists the new pointer kind; the MCP `pointer` tool describes it.
- **Progress docs.** The context-menu row of `docs/ui-parity.md` (status line, history…

title: PDF export: vector slides with real text; effects rasterize per element
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

`docs/gaps.md` lists "PDF export rasterizes slide artwork" as a beta blocker: each slide is one
raster image at print resolution under an invisible text layer. Files are large (0.1 to 2 MB a
slide at the default 200 dpi) and blurry when zoomed or printed.

## What changes

Four commits, rebased on `main` at 9859da3 (after the shared PDF writer, #708): the export, the
progress docs, tests for the drawing `main` gained since this PR was opened (pattern fills,
rectangle and shape path gradients, fill overlays, compound outlines, text shadows and glows,
gradient text, colour emoji, WMF/EMF pictures, WordArt warps), and tests for the newer bevels,
lit faces, group shadows, circle gradients, picture tiles and upright vertical text.

Slides are drawn by the same renderer through a vector canvas, so shapes, outlines (width, dashes,
caps, joins, arrowheads), solid and linear/radial gradient fills, transparency, rotation, flips,
groups, tables and charts become PDF paths and paints, and text is real text in the embedded font
subsets (searchable, selectable, mapped back to Unicode cluster by cluster). JPEG and PNG pictures
are embedded as they are (JPEG stays DCT), others as lossless pixels; crops and picture
transparency are kept. Backgrounds (solid, gradient, picture) are vector too.

and tables with file-defined styles are vector. Pictures the renderer can't decode show the

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`deckcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps. It is the same change as storytold/gridcraft#480 and storytold/wordcraft#798.

    deckcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

**How it works**

The engine only ever opens a user-named file in three places: `file.open`, the media read behind `insert.picture`, `insert.audio`, `insert.video` and `picture.change`, and the writer behind `file.save`, `file.saveAs` and `file.export`. Those now go through two small helpers, `io::read_file` and `io::write_file`, and the checks sit there. The new `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` holds the roots and the path logic: make the path absolute, follow symlinks (for a file that doesn't exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and require the rest to be plain names), then compare with the root by whole path components. On Windows the comparison ignores case, handles `\\?\` and UNC prefixes, and refuses device names like `CON` and `NUL`. Refusals come back as ordinary tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

A test walks every file under `crates/engine/src` and fails if one other than `io.rs`, `file_access.rs`, `recovery.rs` and the test files calls `std::fs`, `File::open`, `File::create` or `OpenOptions`.

`Headless::with_automation_roots` in deckcraft-mcp puts the roots in force for every call. The CLI accepts `--flag DIR` or `--flag=DIR`, refuses a flag given twice, and refuses a root that is missing or not a folder. A root left out grants none of its access, so `--automation-read-root` alone makes the server read-only. The flags only make sense for the in-process server, so combining them with `--connect` is an error. `docs/mcp.md…

title: `.deck` folder format: a presentation as one JSON file per slide, for Git
author: pierrevbc
body:
Closes #220.

## Problem

A `.deckcraft` file is a zip whose `presentation.json` is one compact line. In Git it is an opaque
binary: no readable diff, no review, and two branches that touch the same deck conflict on the
whole file. Decks edited by agents through the CLI or MCP leave changes nobody can review.

## What changes

A second on-disk form of the same document, a folder that DeckCraft opens and saves directly
(spec: `docs/deck-folder-format.md`):

```text
talk.deck/
├── deck.json             format, version, the presentation fields not stored elsewhere
├── slides.order          slide order and sections, one slide key per line
├── slides/<ULID>.json    one slide per file
├── masters/<id>.json     one master with its layouts and theme (+ notes.json, handout.json)
├── media-meta/<id>.json  {"id", "name", "contentType", "link"?, "sha256"}
└── media/<sha256>.<ext>  media bytes, named by content
```

Five commits, rebased on `main` at 9859da3:

1. **Format** (`crates/format/src/folder/`): `to_folder(&Presentation, previous) -> FileMap` and
   `from_folder(&FileMap) -> Result<Presentation>`, pure functions over an in-memory file map, so
   the crate stays free of I/O and wasm is unaffected.
   - Canonical JSON: 2-space indent, LF, final newline, unescaped UTF-8, keys in the order the
     model writes them. A small ordered JSON value (`folder/json.rs`) keeps that order without
     turning on serde_json's `preserve_order` for the whole workspace.
   - `key: null` pairs are dropped only when reloading without them gives the same model; the
     check found `Chart.title` and `Chart.legend` (defaults aren't null) and keeps those.
   - Keys the model doesn't know (a newer DeckCraft, another tool) are kept from the previous
     version of each file, in place.
   - Slide files are named by ULID keys given on first save and found again by slide id, so
     reordering only touches `slides.order` and two branches adding slides never collide. Clock
     and randomness are …

title: Text: exact line spacing ends at the last line's descent
author: xmaks82
body:
With exact line spacing (`<a:lnSpc><a:spcPts/>`) PowerPoint puts the baseline at 80 % of the line pitch and ends the text at the last line's descent rather than a full pitch below it. We laid every line out a full pitch tall, so cells and text boxes using exact spacing came out taller than PowerPoint's: a table of 12 pt rows at 26.59 pt exact spacing (common in decks built from Excel tables) grew to 35.6 pt rows where PowerPoint draws 33 pt, pushing the table down and making shrink-on-overflow kick in early.

`layout_scaled`: under `Spacing::Pts` the baseline is at `0.8 × pitch` and `content_height` ends at the last line's descent (proportional and single spacing unchanged).

**Measured** against PowerPoint's own PDF of a real deck (`pdftotext -bbox`): rows now 33.5 pt vs PowerPoint's 32.9–33.8 pt (were 35.6). Across 31 decks / 597 slides the change touches 7 slides, all within ±1.5 of 255 per pixel.

Test: `exact_line_spacing_ends_at_the_last_descent` (fails before). `cargo test` for text/render/pptx/model and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

Side note while testing: `engine::tests::clicks_in_flipped_shapes_hit_the_text_where_it_is_drawn` fails ~3 in 10 full `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine` runs on `main` here (Linux, without craft-fonts, Liberation Sans): the click at x=240 lands on a character boundary and resolves to char 1 or char 2 between the plain and the flipped measurement, with the same face both times.

title: Pictures: the black-and-white (bi-level) recolour is read, drawn and saved (#234)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #234.

`a:biLevel` on a picture's blip is now read into a new `PictureAdjust::bilevel` threshold (0–1, from `thresh` in 1/1000 of a percent, so `25000` = 25%), written back on save, and applied when the picture is decoded: each pixel whose luminance (Rec. 601 weights, the same ones the grayscale adjustment already uses) is below the threshold becomes black, the rest white, and alpha is left untouched, as ECMA-376 Part 1 describes the effect. It is applied after brightness/contrast/saturation and is part of the decoded-image cache key, so the same picture with and without the effect does not share a cached pixmap. The cyan-on-transparent logo from the issue now renders white over its cyan background.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-render --lib images` — new pixel test (cyan with alpha → white at a 25% threshold and black at 70%, dark blue → black, grey just above/below the threshold, alpha kept) and a cache-key test
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-pptx --test roundtrip` — the round-trip picture now carries `bilevel: Some(0.25)`
- each new test fails with the fix reverted and passes with it
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-model -p deckcraft-pptx -p deckcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Render: a group's child-coordinate scale no longer scales line widths (#233)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #233

## Cause

A group's children are drawn under `parent * group_child_affine(group, child_frame)`, which maps the group's child coordinate space onto its box. A deck from the old master-unit era uses a tiny child space (here `chExt` 3721 x 1910 against an `ext` of 5907087 x 3032125, a scale of about 1587), so that mapping scales by ~1587. `stroke()`, `arrowheads()` and the ink strokes in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` set that full transform on the context and give the line width in points, so a 0.75 pt line was stroked about 1200 pt wide and covered the slide. PowerPoint keeps line widths absolute: only the slide/view scale changes them.

## Fix

The renderer remembers the transform a top-level shape is drawn under (the slide-to-pixels view). For a shape inside a group, the outline is first carried through the rest of the chain (`view⁻¹ · m`) and then stroked under the view itself. So the group's child-coordinate scale moves and sizes the outline but never the line width, dash lengths (they are multiples of the width) or arrowhead size, also for groups scaled unevenly (100 across, 50 down). Shapes outside groups take exactly the code path they had (`m` itself, outline untouched).

## Verified

Offscreen with `deckcraft-cli render`: a deck made with the sample deck plus a group with the issue's child space (`off 284957,2284419`, `ext 5907087 x 3032125`, `chOff 1111,1899`, `chExt 3721 x 1910`) holding a 0.75 pt red line with an arrowhead and a 0.75 pt blue dashed rectangle.

| | rendered slide |
|---|---|
| `main` | covered by a huge red and blue shape |
| this branch | thin red diagonal line with its arrowhead and a thin dashed rectangle over the normal slide |

New test `tests::group_child_scale_does_not_scale_line_widths` in `crates/render/src/tests.rs`. It draws the same group (dashed 4 pt rectangle, 3 pt arrowed line, 5 pt ink stroke) with children laid out 1:1, in a child space of scale 100, and in one scaled unevenly, and requires the same number of inked…

title: Fonts: a family loaded by another thread is still found
author: xmaks82
body:
Two threads resolving the same installed family at once raced in `FontDb`:

1. The thread that lost found every face already added by the other, so `load_cataloged` returned "nothing added", `try_family` treated the family as missing, and the lookup fell through the substitutes to the last-resort face — the text was then drawn in whatever system font covered it (Ubuntu, here, instead of Liberation Sans).
2. Faces were pushed one at a time, so a lookup could see a family half-loaded (Bold before Regular, in path order) and take the wrong face.

**Fix** (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`): `try_family` looks again after loading whenever the family is installed, whoever loaded it; a file's (and a family's) faces are parsed first and added under one write lock, skipping duplicates.

**Why it matters beyond tests:** the app renders thumbnails/slides on several threads, so a deck opened right after start-up could lay out a text box in a fallback font (different widths, wraps and autofit) depending on timing.

**Flaky tests it explains:** `engine::tests::clicks_in_flipped_shapes_hit_the_text_where_it_is_drawn` failed 3 in 10 full `cargo test -p deckcraft-engine` runs on `main` here (Linux, no craft-fonts) — now 0 in 20; text-layout tests comparing two layouts in one test were affected the same way.

**Test:** `a_family_loaded_by_another_thread_is_still_found` copies an installed multi-face family to a temp folder and resolves it from 8 threads on a fresh `FontDb` 30 times (skips on a machine without such a family): fails 5/5 before, passes 10/10 after. `cargo test --workspace` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Text: line spacing reduction comes off the percentage, not the spacing
author: xmaks82
body:
PowerPoint's `lnSpcReduction` takes percentage points off a paragraph's line spacing (90 % less 20 % is 70 %) and leaves the space before/after paragraphs alone. We multiplied (90 % × 0.8 = 72 %) and shrank the paragraph spacing too, so shrunk text had different line and paragraph pitches from PowerPoint's.

**Measured** on PowerPoint's own PDF of a real deck (`pdftotext -bbox`): a body at 90 % spacing, 10 pt before paragraphs, `fontScale=85%`, `lnSpcReduction=20%` runs at 20.2 pt lines (23.8 pt × ~1.2 × 0.70) with 9.9 pt between paragraphs.

`layout_scaled`: `Pct(f)` lines are `natural × (f − reduce)` (floored at 10 % of f); `spacing_pts` no longer applies the reduction. With #226 (saved scale), 10 of 12 affected slides across 31 decks get closer to PowerPoint.

Test: `line_spacing_reduction_comes_off_the_percentage` (fails before). `cargo test` for text and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: Text: honour spcFirstLastPara (space before the first paragraph)
author: xmaks82
body:
`<a:bodyPr spcFirstLastPara="1">` makes the first paragraph's space before and the last paragraph's space after count. PowerPoint honours it (and Google Slides exports set it on every body); we always dropped both, so such text sat one paragraph gap too high — 9.5 pt on a real deck, measured against PowerPoint's PDF.

- Model: `BodyProps::space_first_last`, inherited like the other body properties (default false in `resolve::body`).
- Read/write `spcFirstLastPara`.
- Layout: the first paragraph's space before and the last one's space after count when it's set.

Across 31 real decks this (with the other text fixes) moved 47 slides closer to PowerPoint's rendering.

Tests: `space_before_the_first_paragraph_with_spc_first_last_para` (text), `body_props` extended (pptx). `cargo test` for text/pptx/model/render and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

title: DeckCraft can author a real PowerPoint template
author: hoblin
body:
**Stacked on #229, which is stacked on #228 and #219.** Their changes arrive here as three squashed commits; the last two commits are this PR. Once they merge, this diff shrinks to the template work alone.

An agent building a company's PowerPoint template with `deckcraft-cli` could set the theme, put a logo on the slide master and add layouts, but couldn't finish the template. Formatting a master placeholder changed only its prompt text, a layout couldn't hide the master's graphics, there were no subtitle, footer, slide number or date placeholders, `.potx` was saved as a plain presentation, and a font family named per weight fell back to Inter. Each of these now works through the CLI, in PowerPoint's terms.


## Before and after

Before is `main` with #219, #228 and #229, after is this branch. All calls are `deckcraft-cli run --print --cmd …` on a new blank presentation (`file.new={"blank":true}`).

**Master text styles.** Set the title style on the slide master, then add a slide:
```
view.slideMaster={"master":0}  edit.select={"ids":[2]}  format.size={"size":40}  format.font={"family":"Supera Gothic"}
before: format.size → changed the slide masters, their layouts or the theme     (only the prompt text changed)
after:  format.size → changed the title text style of slide master 0

slide.new={"layout":"titleAndContent","title":"Q3"}, then format.state on its title
before: "font":"Inter" "size":44.0
after:  "font":"Supera Gothic" "size":40.0
```

**Layout placeholder styles:**
```
view.slideMaster={"layout":1}  edit.select={"ids":[14]}  format.bold={"on":true}
before: format.bold → nothing changed
after:  format.bold → changed shape 14 on layout 1 of slide master 0
```

**Hide background graphics, dark layouts:**
```
view.slideMaster={"layout":2}  design.hideBackgroundGraphics={"hide":true}
before: nothing changed
after:  changed the background graphics of layout 2 of slide master 0

design.background={"style":4}
after:  changed the background, colour map of layout 2 …

title: fix(cli): render refuses an unknown option instead of writing it as a file (#235)
author: RCShoemaker
body:
## What was wrong
`deckcraft-cli render` treated any argument it didn't recognise as the output path. So `render deck.pptx --help` rendered the slide into a PNG named `--help` (#235), and a mistyped option such as `--bogus` was silently ignored.

Reproduced on `main` at `688c7ef`:
```
$ deckcraft-cli render --sample --help
--help (1920×1080)            # and a 111 KB file named --help
$ deckcraft-cli render --sample --bogus out.png
out.png (1920×1080)           # --bogus ignored, exit 0
```

## Fix
In `render`'s argument loop, an argument that starts with `-` and isn't a known option is now an error: `deckcraft-cli: unknown render option `--bogus``. A lone `-` still reaches the existing path handling.

## Relation to #228
#228 makes `--help` / `-h` print help for every subcommand, which covers the other half of #235. This PR only touches the render argument loop, which #228 leaves alone, so the two shouldn't conflict. With both merged, #235 is fully fixed. I've left #236 to #228, which documents that `--slide` counts from 0.

## Tests
- New `render_refuses_an_unknown_option_instead_of_writing_it_as_a_file` covers `--bogus`, `-x` and `--help` and checks that no file is written. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) on Windows 11.

The second commit adds my own entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

Refs #235

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built deckcraft and deckcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#deckcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: Text: single-spaced lines are 1.2 times the font size apart, as in PowerPoint
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: single-spaced lines were as tall as each font's own ascent plus descent, so they ran tighter or looser than in PowerPoint depending on the font. Calibri lines were 15% too close together (18 pt instead of 21.6 pt at 18 pt), Segoe UI lines too far apart, and every multi-line text box drifted from PowerPoint's layout.

After: lines are 1.2 times the font size apart in every font, with the baseline where PowerPoint puts it, so line positions match PowerPoint to within half a point on all twenty fonts I measured.

How: I built decks in PowerPoint with three lines of "HHH" in twenty fonts (Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman, Georgia, Courier New, Aptos, Segoe UI, Verdana, Cambria, Tahoma, Yu Gothic, MS Gothic, Microsoft YaHei, SimSun, Malgun Gothic, Leelawadee UI, Nirmala UI, Gabriola, Cambria Math) at 18 and 40 pt, exported them with PowerPoint at 2 px/pt and measured the ink rows. The pitch is always 1.2 × size. The baseline sits at `usWinAscent / (usWinAscent + usWinDescent)` of that pitch for every font except the two with a huge Windows extent (Gabriola, Cambria Math, over 1.5 em), where it sits at 0.81. `FontFace` gains `line_split`, and `line_metrics` in the text crate uses it with `LINE_PITCH = 1.2`. Percent spacing, exact spacing and autofit all build on `line_metrics`, so they follow.

On 446 slides from the Apache POI test decks, the mean pixel difference from PowerPoint's own export dropped from 14.2 to 10.7. 304 slides got closer and 18 moved by about a pixel.

Tests:
- `single_spaced_lines_are_1_2_times_the_size_apart_whatever_the_font` (text): every line is 1.2 × size tall at 18 and 40 pt, and the first baseline sits at the face's split. Fails without the change.
- `line_split_follows_the_windows_ascent_and_descent` (fonts): the split is read from OS/2.

title: Themes: background pictures are recoloured, and dark layouts stay dark
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: decks using the Office 2007-era built-in themes (Treck and its relatives, still common in real-world decks) showed grey backgrounds where PowerPoint shows warm tinted ones. Their dark "section header" slides came out light, with dark title text instead of light.

After: theme background pictures are recoloured like PowerPoint does, and slides on a dark layout are dark with light text. On the Apache POI `themes.pptx` deck, slide 9's pixel difference from PowerPoint's own export drops from 131 to 3, and slide 8's from 27 to 2.

Two missing pieces:
- **Duotone** (`a:blip/a:duotone`): read, but the picture was drawn unchanged. The painter now resolves its two colours against the slide's colours and the placeholder colour (`phClr`), and the image cache maps each pixel's luminance between the dark and the light colour (keyed on them, so different recolours don't collide). This also covers duotone set on ordinary pictures.
- **Colour map overrides** (`p:clrMapOvr/a:overrideClrMapping`) on layouts and slides were ignored, so a layout mapping `bg1→dk1, tx1→lt1` still drew light. `Layout` and `Slide` now carry an optional colour map, `resolve::Ctx` uses slide › layout › master (a slide with `masterClrMapping` follows its layout, as PowerPoint draws it), and the PPTX writer writes them back.

Tests:
- `duotone_maps_luminance_between_its_two_colours` (render): black, mid grey and white map to dark, the mix and light, alpha is kept, and duotones key the cache separately.
- `a_layout_colour_map_override_applies_to_its_slides` (model): layout override applies to its slides and the layout, the slide's own override wins, and the master keeps its map.
- `colour_map_overrides_round_trip`, `a_picture_duotone_round_trips` (pptx).

title: Shapes: preset adjust guide names follow the ECMA-376 definition (#214)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #214.

title: Render: two-colour gradients ramp like PowerPoint's
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: a two-colour gradient (black to white, or any two theme colours) was blended linearly in sRGB, so it looked darker and muddier through the middle than in PowerPoint. Red to green went through brown.

After: two-colour gradients ramp like PowerPoint's, lighter and smoother through the middle. Gradients with three or more stops, or with a stop moved off an end, still blend linearly, because that is what PowerPoint does with them.

How: I built gradient probes in PowerPoint (five colour pairs, both directions, on shapes and on a slide background, three stops, a stop at 20 %) and read PowerPoint's exported pixels. A gradient of exactly two stops at 0 % and 100 % mixes the colours in linear light, with the second colour's share following an S-shaped curve: black to white is 105, 186 and 238 at a quarter, half and three quarters, against 64, 128 and 191 linearly. Anything else is linear in sRGB (black to red to white gives 64, 128, 191 per segment). The new `ramp` module holds the measured curve (symmetric, 17 points) and expands a two-colour gradient into 16 pieces, so vello's sRGB interpolation draws PowerPoint's ramp. Fills use it for linear and path gradients alike.

On 446 Apache POI slides, 6 got closer to PowerPoint's export (Office theme backgrounds: `backgrounds` slide 2 went from 11.2 to 4.7, `themes` slide 3 from 10.2 to 2.9) and one SmartArt slide moved by under a point.

Tests:
- `ramp::tests`: black to white and two colour pairs match PowerPoint's pixels within 3, the ends are the stops, the weight is symmetric and monotonic, and only two-colour gradients are expanded.
- `a_linear_gradient_ramps_like_powerpoint`, `a_gradient_with_a_stop_off_the_end_stays_linear` (render): rendered pixels at 25/50/75 % match PowerPoint.
