title: Text: wrap URLs, Korean and CJK punctuation where PowerPoint does
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: DeckCraft wrapped text at different points than PowerPoint in three common cases.
- URLs and paths broke after every `/` or `\`.
- Korean broke between syllables, splitting words ("안녕하 | 세요").
- A line of Japanese or Chinese ending in "。" or "，" pulled the previous character down with it, so the line was one character short.

After: these wrap exactly where PowerPoint wraps them. A URL fills the line and breaks at the edge, Korean wraps between words, and closing East Asian punctuation hangs past the edge of the line.

How: I built a deck in PowerPoint with ten narrow boxes (hyphens, slashes, backslashes, an unbreakable word, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, dots, punctuation, brackets) and compared PowerPoint's export with DeckCraft's render. All ten now break at the same characters.
- `break_opportunities` removes Unicode's break after `/` and `\` unless `latinLnBrk` is on (PowerPoint's default text styles set it off), and removes breaks between two Hangul characters.
- `break_lines` lets a closing East Asian punctuation mark hang when `hangingPunct` is on (PowerPoint's default text styles set it on; the spec's default is off).
- `ParaProps` gains `latin_line_break` and `hanging_punct`, inherited like the other paragraph properties and read and written as `latinLnBrk` and `hangingPunct`.

Hyphens, spaces, dots and brackets were already right and are unchanged. No Apache POI slide changed by more than 0.3.

title: Emoji: drawn in colour, with families, skin tones and flags joined
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: emoji were drawn as black outlines from a symbol font. Sequences fell apart into their parts: a family (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦) was four separate people, the rainbow flag a white flag and a rainbow, and a thumbs-up with a skin tone was a thumb and a colour square.

After: emoji are drawn in colour from the installed colour emoji font, with their sequences, skin tones and flags joined, as PowerPoint draws them. An emoji forced to text style (U+FE0E) stays a plain glyph.

How:
- **Font choice** (`fonts::fallback`): `is_emoji_cluster` recognises emoji (default emoji presentation, U+FE0F, ZWJ between pictographs, skin tones, regional indicators, keycaps). Such a cluster takes a colour font (`FontFace::is_color`: a `COLR`, `CBDT`, `sbix` or `SVG ` table, cached per face) before the document's fonts. If none is loaded, an installed one covering it is loaded from the system catalog (misses remembered, not on wasm). No vendor font is named: the choice is by capability. In the text crate, emoji and U+FE0E clusters no longer reuse the previous cluster's face.
- **Colour glyphs** (`render::colr`): a `skrifa` `ColorPainter` over vello paints COLR v0 and v1 glyphs in their `CPAL` colours, with solid fills, linear, radial and sweep gradients, transforms, clip boxes and composite modes. Palette index 0xFFFF takes the text colour, and nesting is capped for hostile fonts. `draw_glyph` uses it for colour faces and otherwise draws the outline as before.

Checked with PowerPoint: in the wild-text deck's emoji line, the family, thumbs-up, rainbow flag, heart, person and laptop now match PowerPoint's export glyph for glyph (flags stay letters, as in PowerPoint on Windows). No Apache POI slide changed, and rendering the 95 POI decks took the same time (15.0 s against 15.4 s, within noise).

title: Comments: threads and resolved state survive a .pptx round trip (#70)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #70.

**What was wrong.** The writer emitted the legacy comment part only, so replies were flattened into sibling comments and the resolved flag was dropped. Modern PowerPoint decks carry a second, threaded part (`p188`) as well — and the reader took both, importing every comment twice.

**Export** (`crates/pptx/src/write/mod.rs`): a slide with comments now also writes the modern threaded part `ppt/comments/modernCommentN.xml` — `p188:cmLst` with nested `p188:replyLst`, `status="resolved"`, EMU `p188:pos`, the slide's `commentRel` anchor ext and the modern `ppt/authors.xml` with GUID author ids — next to the flattened legacy part, the same pair of parts PowerPoint itself writes. Older readers keep the legacy view; PowerPoint 2021+ and DeckCraft read threads and resolved state.

**Import** (`crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs`): when a slide carries both parts, the modern one wins and the flattened legacy copy is skipped (the dedup also covers packages that type the modern part through a `Default` entry — the `p188` root is recognized too). Modern positions scale as EMU; they were read as legacy 1/8 pt, ~1587× off, so markers from real PowerPoint decks land in the right place now.

Comment ids are deterministic GUIDs from the existing `tables::guid`, so exports stay reproducible with no new dependency.

**Known limitation for a follow-up:** comments anchor with `p188:unknownAnchor` (schema-valid) rather than a slide moniker, which needs part identity the model does not have yet.

**Format facts verified** against the Open XML SDK part registry and schema files (`PowerPointCommentPart.json`, `PowerPointAuthorsPart.json`, the 2018/8 schema), ONLYOFFICE's PPTX writer and Microsoft's add-comment sample: content types, rel type URIs, `CT_Comment` child order (anchor → pos → replyLst → txBody), required attributes, braced-GUID ids, `userId=""`/`providerId` handling, and the anchor ext URI.

**Tests:** new `crates/pptx/tests/comments.rs` — threads plus resolved state round-t…

title: Text: gradient fills draw, starting over on every line as in PowerPoint
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

**Stacked on #273** (two-colour gradient ramp). Only the last commit is new here.

Before: text with a gradient fill (WordArt-style headings, common in real decks) was drawn in one solid colour, the gradient's first.

After: gradient text is drawn with its gradient, the way PowerPoint draws it. Each line is filled with the whole gradient, spanning that line's text: a top-to-bottom gradient runs top to bottom on every line, and a left-to-right one runs from the line's first character to its last, wherever the line sits in the box.

How: I made a probe deck in PowerPoint (a three-line vertical gradient, a short left-aligned word and a centred word with horizontal gradients) and compared it with PowerPoint's export. It showed the per-line behaviour, and DeckCraft now draws the same.
- `paint::gradient` is the gradient builder moved out of `fill_path`, so shape fills and text share it, including PowerPoint's two-colour ramp.
- `draw_layout_with` builds one gradient per line, from the line's top and bottom and its first and last caret, and fills each glyph with it through a paint transform.
- The text crate resolves the gradient's colours when it builds the run's style, so the renderer needs no colour scheme.

Test: `a_text_gradient_starts_over_on_every_line` (render). In two lines of black-to-white text, each line starts dark and ends light. It fails without the change.

title: Text: shadows and glows are drawn, with PowerPoint's glow spread
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: text shadows and glows (Format Text Effects, or the legacy Shadow button) were read from the file but never drawn. Headings that rely on a glow or shadow to stand out from a busy background came out flat.

After: text shadows and glows are drawn under the text. The glow's spread matches PowerPoint's export pixel for pixel on a measured profile: solid to about a third of the radius past the letters, faded out by about two thirds.

How:
- The text layout carries a run's outer shadow and glow on each glyph run (`GlyphRun::effects`: colours resolved, sizes scaled with autofit). Bullets don't take them.
- `draw_layout_with` draws every run's shadow, then every run's glow, each in one blurred layer per run, before any text. The shadow's offset is in slide space, like shape shadows.
- `needs_filters` also looks at text effects in runs, list styles and the master's text styles, so a slide with only text glow renders with the blur filter.

I measured the glow on the wild-text deck built in PowerPoint (an 8 pt green glow on bold 40 pt text). Before the calibration DeckCraft's glow spread twice as far.

_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: pattern fills (Format Shape ▸ Fill ▸ Pattern, common in older decks and charts) were approximated. Every preset was drawn as dots, bars or a grid on an 8-point cell, so "30%" looked like sparse dots, "wave" like a dot grid, and "trellis", "plaid" and "sphere" bore no resemblance to PowerPoint's.

After: all 54 preset patterns draw the same tile as PowerPoint, at the same size (one 96-dpi pixel per cell, 0.75 pt) and lined up from the slide's top-left corner, so neighbouring shapes' patterns join seamlessly. A deck with all 48 patterns PowerPoint offers, rendered at two pixels per cell, matches PowerPoint's export to a mean pixel difference of 0.2, down from 62.

How: I exported every preset from PowerPoint, black on white, at exactly two output pixels per pattern cell. That gives 48 from its pattern gallery plus the 6 the gallery doesn't offer (`horz`, `vert`, `cross`, `dnDiag`, `upDiag`, `diagCross`), which I set in the XML. I read each 8×8 tile and its phase from the pixels: black-box observation of output, no PowerPoint files or assets in the repo. The new `render::pattern` module holds the tiles and fills a path with an 8×8 two-colour pixmap repeated with nearest sampling.

Tests:
- `every_drawingml_preset_has_a_tile`: all 54 values of `ST_PresetPatternVal`.
- `percent_presets_get_denser`: the percentage presets set more cells as the percentage grows.
- `pattern_fills_draw_powerpoints_tiles` (render): dkVert's columns and pct50's checkerboard appear pixel for pixel at one output pixel per cell.

title: Render: compound outlines (double, thick-thin, thin-thick, triple)
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: double, thick-thin, thin-thick and triple outlines (Format Shape ▸ Line ▸ Compound type) were drawn as one solid band, so framed shapes, certificate-style borders and divider lines lost their look.

After: each kind is drawn as its separate lines, in the same proportions and on the same sides as PowerPoint, on shapes and on lines. The probe deck (all five kinds at 24 pt, on rectangles and lines) matches PowerPoint's export at 4 px/pt to a mean pixel difference of 0.03, down from 8.8.

How: I measured PowerPoint's export of 24 pt lines of each kind. Double is 1/3 line, 1/3 gap, 1/3 line. Thin-thick is 1/5, 1/5, 3/5 and thick-thin its mirror. Triple is 1/6, 1/6, 1/3, 1/6, 1/6. The first band sits on the left of travel, which is the outside of a shape, since presets run clockwise. The new `render::compound` module holds these bands and moves a path sideways: lines meet at their miter points (so inner corners don't loop), curves are offset with `kurbo::offset::offset_cubic`, and hostile coordinates are skipped. `stroke` then draws each band with the line's own caps, joins and dashes.

Tests:
- `compound::tests`: the band tables, offsetting a rectangle outward and inward (exact miter corners), a circle's radius, and a hostile path.
- `compound_lines_draw_their_bands` (render): each kind's dark bands down a rectangle's top edge match PowerPoint's widths within a point.

title: Render: rectangle and outline path gradients
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

**Stacked on #273** (two-colour gradient ramp). Only the last commit is new here.

Before: "from centre" gradients that follow a rectangle or the shape's outline (path gradients `rect` and `shape`, PowerPoint's Rectangular and Path gradient types) were drawn as circles. A rectangle filled from its centre showed a round glow instead of PowerPoint's X-shaped bevel look, and a triangle or rounded rectangle lost the shape of its shading.

After: these gradients follow the rectangle or the outline as PowerPoint draws them. Two probe decks built in PowerPoint (circle, rect and shape paths from the centre and from a corner, on rectangles, an ellipse, a triangle and a rounded rectangle) match its export to a mean pixel difference of 1.7 and 0.6, down from 15.6 and 22.

How: I measured PowerPoint's export with linear three-stop gradients.
- For `rect`, the colour position is the larger of the horizontal and vertical distances from the focus, each as a share of the room to that side's edge.
- For `shape`, it's the share of the way from the focus to the outline along the same ray.
- `circle` was already right and stays a vello radial gradient.

The new `render::pathgrad` module computes the position per pixel into an image of the bounds (at most 384 px on the long side, bilinear-sampled). It handles focus rects (`fillToRect`), uses the shape's flattened outline for `shape`, and applies the same colour ramp as other gradients.

Tests:
- `pathgrad::tests`: `rect` axis shares from the centre and from a corner, `shape` positions on an ellipse and a triangle, and the colour ramp.
- `rect_path_gradients_draw_x_shaped_contours` (render): rendered pixels at PowerPoint's measured positions.

title: Render: soft edges fade to the shape's outline
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: the soft-edge effect faded a box-shaped mask, not the shape. Ovals and other curved shapes kept hard edges wherever their bounding box was wider than they were, and the fade on a rectangle began outside it, leaving a pale fringe.

After: soft edges fade along the shape's own outline, transparent right at the edge and fully opaque about one radius inside, matching PowerPoint's export of a 12 pt soft edge to within half a pixel across the fade.

title: Start screen: a missing Recent file is marked, its error shows, and entries can be removed (#172)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #172.

**What was wrong.** The start screen reported errors through `set_status`, but the status bar is only drawn while a presentation is open (`SlideApp::ui`): clicking a Recent entry whose file had moved or been deleted did nothing visible, and the same went for every other start-screen error, like a failed **Open the sample deck**.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui`):

- The start screen now draws the transient status message itself, right under the Open row — a real `Label`, not painted text, so screen readers see it too, and wrapped so a long OS error doesn't clip at the panel edge. Shared with the status bar through a new `SlideApp::fresh_status()` (peek-with-expiry), replacing the inline 6 s check there.
- Recent entries whose file no longer exists are dimmed with a `(missing)` mark and hover text **before** anything is clicked.
- Each Recent row gets a remove button (`SlideApp::forget_recent`), persisting with the usual prefs save.
- A successful open clears a stale error, so an old failure no longer lingers next to a document that just opened.

**Deliberate limits:** existence is probed once per path per session — a stat on a dead network share can block for the OS timeout, so UNC paths and URLs are never probed (they stay unmarked and are judged when opened); a disconnected mapped drive would still stall once, accepted. The remove button is a plain `×` because U+2715 has no glyph in the UI font stack (egui would draw the replacement character — visible in a first draft).

**Tests:** three kittest UI tests driving the real start screen — the missing mark and the drawn error (asserted through the accessibility tree, so a fix that paints the message invisibly would fail), removal from the list, and the negative case (an existing file is never marked). Visually verified via snapshot against both the broken and fixed rendering. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Tables: styles the file defines are read, drawn and kept
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: tables drew in the wrong colours whenever their style wasn't one of a handful DeckCraft knows. Every unknown style (Themed, Light, Dark and most Medium variants) was drawn as Medium Style 2, so gradient-banded themed tables came out pale blue and white, and saving dropped the style definitions the file carried.

After: tables are drawn from the style definitions in the file. PowerPoint writes the definition of every table style a deck uses into `ppt/tableStyles.xml`, so this covers the whole gallery and custom styles. LibreOffice's `bnc480256` (two themed tables) went from a pixel difference of 27.6 to 1.6 against PowerPoint's export. Across the 202 table slides in the corpus the mean difference fell from 10.2 to 10.0, with 7 better and 2 moved by half a point.

How:
- **Model**: `TableStyleDef` covers each part (whole table, bands, first and last rows and columns, corner cells) and the table background. A part has fills, theme fill and line references, per-side and inside borders, and text colour and bold. Definitions keep their raw XML. They live in `Presentation::table_styles`.
- **Reader**: parses `tableStyles.xml`. A table whose style the file defines keeps its GUID, except DeckCraft's own generated styles, which still map back to their ids.
- **Renderer**: `look_def` applies the parts that cover a cell in the spec's order. Each part's edge borders go on its region's edges and its inside borders between cells within it. Fills are painted as real fills, so gradients and see-through colours work, and the table background goes under every cell.
- **Writer**: puts definitions back exactly as read.

Tests:
- `table_styles_the_file_defines_are_read_used_and_kept` (new `pptx/tests/table_styles.rs`): a probe definition with a table background, a bold coloured whole table, a 2 pt left border, no inside lines and a see-through band is read, used by the table, and survives…

title: Bullets: an installed symbol font draws its own glyph

After: when the deck's symbol font is installed on the machine, its own glyph is drawn, so the bullet is exactly PowerPoint's. When it isn't, Wingdings 2 and 3 codes get their own look-alikes (stars, triangles, arrows) instead of Wingdings' table.

Nothing is bundled: the font is used only if it is installed, like any other system font.

Found on a real-world deck (`dese-presentation-0.pptx` from mass.gov, slide 16) compared with PowerPoint's export. The bullet star now matches.

title: Chart legend: honour legendPos and overlay in the renderer (#262)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #262.

The reader kept `c:legend/c:legendPos` (default `r`) and the writer wrote it back, but `crates/render/src/chart.rs` always drew the legend as one row under the plot. Now the renderer places the legend by `legendPos`. The layout is in a small `legend_layout` function so that it can be tested:

- `r` (the OOXML default; unknown values fall back to it) and `l`: a vertical stack, centred vertically, and the plot area is narrowed on that side.
- `t` / `b`: a centred row, and the plot area gets shorter. `b` gives the same layout as before.
- `tr`: a vertical stack in the top-right corner, and the plot area is narrowed.
- `c:overlay val="1"`: the legend is drawn in the same place, but the plot area keeps its full size. The reader now reads `c:overlay` into a new `Chart::legend_overlay` field (default `false`), and the writer writes it back instead of always writing `0`.

Not in this PR: `c:legend/c:layout/c:manualLayout`. DeckCraft does not read `c:layout` for any chart element yet (the plot area's manual layout is also ignored). Handling it needs both `edge` and `factor` modes and a write-back, so it should be a separate change.

Tests:
- `render::chart::tests` checks the legend origin and the remaining plot area for `r`, `l`, `t`, `tr`, `b` (unchanged from before) and overlay.
- `read::chart::tests::legend_position_and_overlay_are_read` checks `legendPos`/`overlay`, and the defaults when they are missing (`r`, no overlay).

Neither test compiles on `main`: `legend_layout` and `legend_overlay` do not exist there.

title: PPTX: a placeholder without geometry takes its layout's
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: a slide placeholder drawn with its layout's shape (a picture placeholder cut into a circle, a frame with holes, any non-rectangular placeholder) came out as a plain rectangle covering whatever the layout puts under it. PowerPoint leaves the geometry out of such a placeholder and draws it with its layout's.

After: placeholders without their own geometry take their layout placeholder's (or the master's), as in PowerPoint. Three LibreOffice test decks now match PowerPoint's export: `custgeom-placeholder` from a pixel difference of 11.1 to 0.4, `custgeom-nofill-path` from 17.2 to 0.2, and `custgeom-overlapping-contours` from 16.6 to 5.0. No other slide in the 966 compared got worse.

How: the reader marks a placeholder whose `spPr` has no `prstGeom` or `custGeom`, then fills its geometry from its parents once the masters and layouts are read (`inherit_placeholder_geometry`). Anything without a parent becomes a rectangle. DeckCraft's writer already leaves the geometry out for inheriting placeholders, so DeckCraft's own files now also open the way PowerPoint shows them.

Test: `a_placeholder_without_geometry_takes_its_layouts` (new `pptx/tests/placeholders.rs`). Slide placeholders with their geometry stripped get the layout's ellipse, and ones with their own geometry keep it.

title: CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents in words
author: hoblin
body:
Closes #298.

Based on `main` and stands on its own. It replaces #219, and folds in #229's fix to this PR's own "not available" hint.

An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` reads its answers as is. Many of them didn't say what happened: a wrong command name was reported as broken JSON, a missing shape didn't say which or where, `null` didn't say what changed, and unknown parameter keys were silently ignored. Each one cost the agent extra turns on every deck.

Now every answer reads like a sentence written for a person. An error says how the CLI read the input, what is wrong with it, and the form that works, taken from the command's own params doc. It never guesses what the agent meant.

## Before and after

Real calls; "before" is `main`, "after" is this branch.

### 1. The command name

The agent wants a new blank presentation. It read `ID` in the help, `--cmd ID=JSON`, as a label of its own.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'new=file.new={"blank":true}'
right:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"blank":true}'

before: deckcraft-cli: new: bad JSON: expected ident at line 1 column 2
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 1 of 1 was read as command `new` with parameters `file.new={"blank":true}`.
        `new` is not a command: --cmd takes COMMAND=PARAMS, a command id, then `=`, then a JSON object,
        e.g. --cmd 'slide.new={"title":"Q3"}'. Nothing ran.
```

### 2. A shape on another slide

The agent resizes a shape it drew on slide 0 after `slide.new` moved it to slide 1. Shape ids are looked up on the slide being edited.

```
wrong:  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'shape.insert={…}' --cmd slide.new --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' --save deck.deckcraft
right:  … --cmd 'slide.go={"index":0}' --cmd 'shape.resize={"ids":[260],"w":50}' …

before: deckcraft-cli: invalid parameters for `shape.resize`: no such shape
after:  deckcraft-cli: --cmd 3 of 3: shape 260 is on slide index 0, but shape ids are looked up on slide index 1,
        the one being edited; slide.go {"inde…

title: deckcraft-cli help explains the CLI to an agent
author: hoblin
body:
Closes #299.

Based on `main` and stands on its own; it replaces #228.

An AI agent driving `deckcraft-cli` learns the input language from its help. The help described the CLI in its own grammar: `--cmd ID[=JSON]`, which an agent read as "a label of my own, then `=`". Nothing said that shape ids are looked up on the current slide, or what `format.*` acts on. Agents learned those by trial. Now the help explains the CLI in sentences written for a reader, with a full example.

This PR changes the help only. The input language is unchanged.

title: Render: shadows, inner shadows and glows spread like PowerPoint's
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->

Before: shape shadows and glows were too soft and wide. Inner shadows also fell on the wrong edges: an "Inside: Bottom Right" shadow darkened the top and left of the shape.

title: macOS: end the process in on_exit so closing the window doesn't crash
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #279.

Same crash and same fix as storytold/gridcraft#117 (PR storytold/gridcraft#316, c1d293296), which followed storytold/vectorcraft#670. eframe runs with `run_and_return`, so it drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still going. AccessKit's macOS adapter gives the content view back its original class on teardown, and AppKit's Touch Bar support still has a KVO observation on it, so the next display cycle throws "not registered" and the app aborts. On macOS, `App::on_exit` now ends the process right after saving the preferences, before eframe tears the window down. eframe calls `on_exit` on every way out (close button, ⌘Q, `app.quit`), and only after the unsaved-changes prompt has let the window close, so Save / Don't Save still work as before. Nothing after it is needed: prefs are written and the log file is unbuffered. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

WordCraft (#539) and PhotoCraft (#1624) went a different way, quitting through `-[NSApplication terminate:]`. That needs objc2/dispatch2 in the app, so I kept GridCraft's one-liner. Happy to switch.

Validation:
- `on_exit_ends_the_process_on_macos` (new, in `apps/deckcraft/src/main.rs`): runs `on_exit` in a child copy of the test binary and checks the process ends inside it on macOS (and returns elsewhere). Fails on main (`on_exit returned` is printed), passes here
- I couldn't reproduce the crash itself on an M1 Pro with no Touch Bar: on main, the close button (AX `AXCloseButton`) and `app.quit` both exit 0 with no crash report. With the fix, both still exit 0, and `ui.json`, `prefs.json` and the log are still written
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS 27, Apple silicon)

title: Text: no Latin ligatures, and kerning only from the run's kern size
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: Latin text was shaped with the font's default features, so Calibri drew "ti" (in "Autism", "Transformation"), "fi" and "ffi" as joined ligatures, and every run was pair-kerned even when the file turns kerning off (`kern="0"`) or the text is below the `kern` size.

After: Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text draws no standard or contextual ligatures, and pairs are kerned only when the run's `kern` size is set and the text reaches it, as PowerPoint does. On a test deck built in PowerPoint (Calibri, Cambria and Arial at 40 pt, kerning off and on), line widths now match PowerPoint's exactly; before, kerning-off lines were narrower and ligatures were visible.

How: `make_style` records whether the run kerns; items split on it; `shaping_features` turns off `kern` where the run doesn't kern, and `liga`/`clig` for alphabetic scripts. Arabic and other scripts keep their ligatures, and items with emoji sequences keep them too (they're joined by ligatures in some fonts). Tests cover the feature choice per script, a font with an ffi ligature drawing one glyph per letter, and kerning switching on at exactly the `kern` size (the font tests pick any installed font that has the ligature or kerns AVATAR).

title: fix(security): require a token on the control channel
author: mendy-cohen
body:
Fixes #263.

- New `deckcraft_mcp::auth` module. The token is `DECKCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` if set, otherwise 32 random bytes from the OS. The app writes it to `deckcraft-control-<port>.token` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or the per-user temp folder. The file is created fresh each start (never through an existing symlink) and is mode 0600 on Unix.
- The first request on a connection must be `auth` with the right token, compared in constant time. Anything else gets an error and the connection is closed, including a non-JSON first line like an HTTP request from a browser. A repeated `auth` after that is answered without reaching the UI.
- `Remote` (used by `deckcraft-cli app` and `mcp --connect`) sends the token on every connection. It looks the token up again on reconnect, so a restarted app still works.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the handshake.

This is the same approach as storytold/gridcraft#834, and it lines up with what PhotoCraft and PdfCraft already do.

### Testing
- New unit tests: token generation and matching, token file permissions, and a real-socket test showing requests reach the UI only after `auth`.
- `cargo test -p deckcraft-mcp -p deckcraft`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on the touched crates, `cargo fmt` and `cargo xtask layers` all pass.
- Manual run on macOS with `deckcraft --control 7990`. A request with no token is refused, an HTTP-style request is refused, the token file is `-rw-------`, and `deckcraft-cli app --port 7990 --method ui.inspect` works.

title: fix(macos): open .pptx and .deckcraft files from Finder
author: mendy-cohen
body:
On macOS, DeckCraft can't be chosen as the default app for presentations, and double-clicking a file can't open it in DeckCraft.

**Why:** `Info.plist.in` declares the `.deckcraft` and `.pptx` UTIs but has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so LaunchServices doesn't know DeckCraft opens them. And Finder sends files as a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, not as command-line arguments. winit 0.30 doesn't handle that event, so even with the plist fixed, the file never reached the app.

**Changes**
- `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`: adds `CFBundleDocumentTypes` for DeckCraft Presentation (`Owner`) and PowerPoint Presentation (`Alternate`, so existing apps stay preferred until the user picks DeckCraft).
- `apps/deckcraft/src/apple_events.rs`: the same approach as GridCraft's `apple_events.rs`. It registers the handler with `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"` before the event loop starts and opens the paths on the next frame. Errors are logged and shown in the status bar. The dependency is the same pinned version and checksum as in GridCraft's `Cargo.lock`, and the workspace stays `forbid(unsafe_code)`.
- Ignores the `-psn_` argument older macOS adds on a Finder launch. It used to be treated as a file to open.

I only declared `.pptx` and `.deckcraft`. `file.open` sniffs content, so `.potx`/`.ppsx` might work too, but I didn't verify them.

### Testing
- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy -p deckcraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask layers` and `plutil -lint` all pass.
- On macOS 26 (arm64) I built a throwaway bundle from the debug binary and this `Info.plist.in`, registered it with `lsregister`, and ran `open -a <bundle> "Test Deck.pptx"`, using a `.pptx` saved by `deckcraft-cli run --sample`. `ui.inspect` showed the deck open. `lsregister -dump` lists the claimed UTIs as `org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation, ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation`.
- I didn't run the full `packaging/macos/package.sh` (signing and notarization).

title: Text: WordArt transforms (prstTxWarp) draw, and their adjusts round-trip
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: WordArt text with a transform (`a:prstTxWarp`, such as Arch Up, Wave or Inflate) was drawn flat, and its adjust values were dropped on save.

After: all 40 PowerPoint text-warp presets are drawn, and their adjust values are read, kept and written back.

How:
- `geom::warp` holds the warp curves. They were measured from PowerPoint renders of probe decks (clean room, observation only).
- Most presets stretch each band of lines between a top and a bottom curve.
- Arch, Circle and Button set the text along an ellipse at its natural size, with extra lines stacked outwards.
- `render::warp` flattens glyph outlines and underlines and maps every point through the warp. Unwarped and rotated text draw exactly as before.

How closely it matches PowerPoint (ink overlap on probe decks):
- Most presets: 0.95 to 0.996.
- Arch and Button: about 0.9.
- Can, Cascade and Inflate/Deflate Bottom/Top: the shape matches but glyphs drift by up to about 1% of the width.
- Circle and Ring: the shape matches but the text is turned a few degrees.

Tests:
- Warp math: guides for every preset, where the curves bend, arcs, line bands, and hostile adjusts and boxes.
- Rendering: arches lift the middle of a line, Plain fills the text rect, unknown warps draw flat, and every preset renders inside the slide.
- pptx: adjust values round-trip (`adj` vs `adj1`/`adj2`, partial lists, NaN).

Not done yet: a Transform gallery and adjust handles in the editor; warped rotated or vertical text, which still draws flat.

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: Shapes: the 38 missing PowerPoint preset shapes
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: 38 of PowerPoint's preset shapes had no geometry in DeckCraft, so decks using them drew nothing (or a rectangle), and the shape gallery lacked them. They are: the curved, circular and swoosh arrows, the line and arrow callouts, gears, funnel, ellipse and left-right ribbons, corner tabs, chart markers, pie wedge, uneven trapezoid, rising line and offline storage.

Every outline is constructed independently from measurements of PowerPoint's own renders (clean room; nothing from Microsoft's shape definitions). Defaults come from PowerPoint's adjustment values on newly inserted shapes, and clamping follows what PowerPoint was observed to do.

Known gaps: the swoosh head and funnel angles are fitted constants; a very tall left-right ribbon is off by up to 1% and a circular arrow with band and head both at 40% is visibly off. Text rectangles are reasonable guesses, not measured, and only the uneven trapezoid has adjust handles.

Tests: every new preset is in the catalog and builds finite outlines inside its bounds at eight sizes (including zero) with huge, negative, NaN and infinite adjusts; outline points measured from PowerPoint are matched within 1 pt for each family.

title: Text: Tab no longer ends text entry in lists (#93)
author: FabPei
body:
Pressing Tab to indent a list item killed the keyboard: the item gained a level, but no further typing, Enter, Backspace or arrow keys reached the text. The same happened after any arrow key during text editing, so pressing Enter to add a list item appeared to do nothing and new items never joined the list. Lists looked broken even though the text and list commands themselves behaved correctly.

The cause is the slide keyboard gate in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: Tab and arrow keys that no widget claims move egui's keyboard focus onto ordinary widgets (the window's drag handle, ribbon buttons), and `SlideApp::keyboard` dropped every key while any widget held focus — the focus cycle intercepted the keys from then on. #78 reports the same symptom from the Tab side.

While text on the slide is being edited, that stray keyboard focus is now surrendered before key handling, so the edited text keeps the keyboard. Real text fields, dialogs, the command palette and open menus keep their keys exactly as before.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The new regression test `tab_in_an_edited_list_keeps_the_keyboard` drives a list through the real egui input path — type, Enter, Tab, type, Enter, type — and asserts the text and the list levels; it fails before this change because every key after Tab is swallowed.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#93

title: Text: the caret shows on dark slides and in empty placeholders
author: xc4pr
body:
Fixes #318.

### What was wrong
- The caret is stroked with `Tokens::caret`, which is black in both the light and the dark app theme. But the caret sits on the slide, so on a dark slide (the built-in Nocturne theme, for example) it is black on `#121826`.
- A placeholder nobody has typed into has a `TextBody` with no paragraphs. `cmd::text::layout_for` laid that out as zero lines, so `TextLayout::caret` returned `None` and nothing was drawn. The "Click to add …" prompt also stayed up while the placeholder was being edited.

### What this changes
- `cmd::text::caret_color` (engine): the resolved colour of text typed at the caret (`edit::props_at`, `resolve::run`, `resolve::text_color`). The canvas strokes the caret with it and falls back to the theme token when that text has no fill.
- `cmd::text::layout_for` lays an empty body out as one empty paragraph, so the caret gets a line, in the place and at the height the first typed character will have.
- The canvas passes the placeholder being typed into as `RenderOpts::skip_text` while its body is empty, so the prompt makes way for the caret. The canvas texture's cache key carries it.

### Tested
- Two engine tests: an empty title has a caret in the middle of its box, and the caret is dark on the default theme, light on Nocturne and red after `format.color`. The first one fails without the `layout_for` change.
- By hand through the control channel on Linux (GNOME, Wayland): ten screenshots over two blink periods, counting the pixels that change inside the placeholder.

author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: a font the machine doesn't have fell back to a style look-alike (Avenir Next → Montserrat, or Arial when none was installed), while PowerPoint draws it in Calibri, so lines broke in different places. Fonts that documents name by their Windows family ("Segoe UI Semibold", "Arial Black", "Calibri Light") weren't found at all when the font's typographic family differs ("Segoe UI" with a "Semibold" style), so titles in Microsoft's own decks came out in the wrong font.

After: text matches what PowerPoint draws on the same machine (measured with probe decks built in PowerPoint):
- A missing font draws in Calibri, whatever the theme, `panose` or `pitchFamily` say. Metric-compatible names keep their stand-ins (Calibri → Carlito, Arial → Liberation Sans…).
- Liberation Sans and Serif draw as Arial and Times New Roman, as PowerPoint maps them. Windows' standard aliases (Helvetica, Arial CE…) map to their base fonts.
- Windows family names find their faces. A family's installed files load together, so one name loading a single face (Segoe UI Semibold) can't make regular Segoe UI text semibold.
- Office's downloadable fonts (Aptos and the newer cloud families) keep their open substitute (Aptos → Inter), since PowerPoint downloads and draws them as themselves (relates to storytold/deckcraft#107).

Measured against PowerPoint's exports on 1,128 slides from real-world, Apache POI and LibreOffice decks: 141 slides closer, 3 slightly further (all under 2 points of mean difference).

How: `FontDb::document_face` picks the face for document text; the text crate uses it. Faces record their Windows family and style (`name` IDs 1/2), the system font catalog lists them under both names, and lookups load every cataloged file of a family once, under a lock so a concurrent lookup waits rather than falling back.

title: Keyboard shortcuts: match PowerPoint's Windows and Mac lists
author: n0mahd
body:
## Summary

This PR checks DeckCraft's default shortcuts against Microsoft's published lists: "Keyboard shortcuts in PowerPoint" (the Windows and Mac tables) and "Use keyboard shortcuts to deliver PowerPoint presentations". It binds every listed shortcut that already has a feature to run.

- **Coverage:** before this PR, 68 of the 192 listed shortcuts worked. After it, 150 work and 3 are partial.

  - **Mac:** 22 → 59 of 70.
  - **Slide show:** 10 → 20 of 35.
- **Where it is documented:** the full audit table is in `docs/ui-parity.md#shortcut-audit`.

- **Bug fix:** registry shortcuts on punctuation keys never fired from the keyboard. egui calls the key `CloseBracket` while the registry says `]`. Bring Forward, the font size keys, superscript and Next Window were affected.
  - `keys::key_token` now normalises the key name.
  - The UI maps shifted symbols back to the key they are typed on, so `{` matches Ctrl+Shift+[.
- **Paths:** the UI, the control channel (`ui.key`) and MCP all reach the same key path. `ui.key` now handles UI shortcuts first, the same way the keyboard does.

**Slides and files**
- Ctrl+M new slide (Windows only; on the Mac, Cmd+M stays Minimize).
- Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D duplicates the slide.

title: Fonts: use Office's downloaded fonts, and say which fonts a file is missing
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: decks set in Aptos (Office's default font since 2023) drew in a look-alike even on machines where Office had downloaded Aptos, and a deck whose fonts weren't installed gave no sign its text was substituted.

After:
- DeckCraft also reads the fonts Microsoft Office downloads on demand (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\FontCache\4\CloudFonts` on Windows; Office's cloud-font cache and app font folders on macOS). Aptos and Aptos Display then draw exactly as in PowerPoint. These fonts are only read where they already are; DeckCraft never ships or requires them.

How: `engine::fonts::missing_fonts` resolves every slide run's family (theme fonts included) and character-bullet font, and lists those `FontDb` doesn't have. `DocState::missing_fonts` keeps the list from opening, and `ui-egui::toast` shows it once per document.

Tests: the engine lists a missing font and not an installed one, and new documents list nothing. A kittest test opens a .pptx in a missing font, finds the toast's text, closes it and checks it stays closed. The message wording is tested for one to many fonts. title: Embedded objects draw their preview picture, including old VML previews
author: echelon
body:

author: echelon

title: Selection Pane: reorder by drag and drop, groups, Show/Hide All and Lock, as in PowerPoint (#133)
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: the Selection Pane listed objects but couldn't reorder them by drag and drop, didn't show groups with their children, and had no Show All / Hide All or arrows. Objects couldn't be locked (storytold/deckcraft#133).

After: the pane works like PowerPoint's. Its behaviour was observed in PowerPoint with a test deck.
- **List:** the front-most object is on top. Groups expand with a chevron and indented children. Each row has an eye and a padlock.

title: Text: Ctrl+arrows, Ctrl+Backspace/Delete and other text keys work like PowerPoint (#268)
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

- **Font size:** Ctrl+Shift+> / < and Ctrl+] / [ step the font size.
- **Change case:** Shift+F3 cycles lower → Each Word → UPPER.
- **End on wrapped lines:** End keeps the caret at the wrapped line's end.
- **Clicks:** double-click selects a word without its trailing space; triple-click selects the paragraph.

title: Render: text in a scaled group keeps its point size, as in PowerPoint
author: echelon
body:

title: Open: a password-protected presentation says so, and open errors show on the start screen
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #346.

A password-protected .pptx isn't a zip: PowerPoint stores it as a compound file (CFB) holding `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` streams. `open_presentation` didn't recognise it and returned the generic "not a presentation DeckCraft can read", and `pick_and_open` dropped that error with `let _ =`. Even where errors were kept (Open > Recent, files arriving through the web picker) they went to the status bar, which isn't drawn on the start screen or the File tab, so you just landed back where you were. Now the pptx crate recognises an encrypted package (a bounds-checked CFB directory walk, copied from GridCraft's `crates/xlsx/src/cfb.rs`) and the engine says "<file> is password-protected. DeckCraft can't open password-protected presentations yet.", and open failures show as a toast, which is visible over the start screen too.

What's left for #346: actually asking for the password and decrypting (ECMA-376 Agile/Standard, as WordCraft and GridCraft do). That needs AES/SHA-512 crates DeckCraft doesn't depend on yet, so I kept it out of this PR; happy to follow up with it if you want it in.

Validation:
- `cfb::tests::a_password_protected_presentation_is_named_as_such` (pptx, on a compound file built in the test): fails on main (the message says "not a presentation DeckCraft can read"), passes here
- `backstage::tests::a_file_that_cant_be_opened_says_why` (ui-egui, Open > Browse on the start screen with an unreadable file): fails on main (nothing on screen), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-pptx -p deckcraft-engine -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Fonts: the font scan leaves out faces with no outline tables
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

The font scan (`file_face_names` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`) also lists faces with none of the tables skrifa reads glyph outlines from (`glyf`, `CFF `, `CFF2`, `VARC`), such as faces whose glyphs are bitmaps only or are stored as outlines in Apple's `hvgl` table. `FontDb::outline`, which the renderer reads glyph outlines from, returns an empty path for every glyph of such a face.

On macOS 27.0.1 the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` catalogs "GB18030 Bitmap" (`Supplemental/NISC18030.ttf`), so it is in `FontDb::families()`, which the Home tab's font list shows. The face stores its glyphs as `bdat` bitmaps and has no color glyph tables. It maps 27,544 characters, `FontDb::outline` returns an empty path for all of them, and the renderer draws none of them (`crates/render/src/lib.rs:1487-1493`).

## Fix

`file_face_names` leaves out a face whose table directory has none of those four tables. vectorcraft has the same check (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/781), and the open designcraft pull request https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/443 adds it there. With the check, the scan of `/System/Library/Fonts` on the same Mac catalogs 785 faces instead of 786, and "GB18030 Bitmap" is the one left out.

## Test

`faces_without_outlines_are_not_cataloged` (`crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`) renames the `glyf` table of the `legacy-semibold.ttf` fixture in memory, writes it and a copy of `legacy-regular.ttf` to a temporary folder, and scans that folder. The Regular is listed, and the Semibold is listed under neither its typographic nor its Windows family name. On `main` the test fails (`styles("DeckCraft Legacy")` returns `["Regular", "Semibold"]`). No font file is added.

`cargo test -p deckcraft-fonts --lib` (22 passed), `cargo clippy -p deckcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean. On macOS 27.0.1 with craft-fonts at `8dcdacd5`, `cargo xtask ci` passed fmt and clippy and stopped at the test step: `ime_te…

title: Slides: Select All follows the pane - Ctrl+A over the slides pane or in the sorter takes every slide (#188)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #188.

**What was wrong.** Ctrl+A always ran the engine's `edit.selectAll`, which selects the current slide's shapes: clicking a thumbnail and pressing Ctrl+A looked like nothing happened.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui`, engine untouched): the UI keyboard path routes Cmd/Ctrl+A to `slide.selectSlides` with every slide while the pointer last worked the slides pane or in the Slide Sorter — Select All follows the pane, as in PowerPoint. On the canvas the engine keeps its shapes semantics, so MCP and the control channel are unchanged (they have no pane, and the Edit menu's Select All stays with the shapes like modern PowerPoint's Home ▸ Select).

**Design note:** an engine-level rule ("slides selected ⇒ select slides") was considered and rejected — `go_to` sets `sel.slides = [current]` on every navigation, so the ordinary canvas state would have made canvas Ctrl+A regress to selecting slides.

**Hardening against stale-flag paths** (each walked through in review):

- text being edited and slide-master context fall through to the engine (`selection.text.is_none()`, `target == Slides`);
- the flag only counts where the pane exists (Normal/Reading views);
- a canvas press collapses the pane's multi-selection back to the current slide — so pane Ctrl+A → canvas click → Delete can never sweep the deck with a second Delete;
- opening or creating a deck clears the flag.

**Known small gap:** the thumbnail pane draws its tiles with the painter (no accessibility nodes), so the flag-setting click itself isn't driven by the tests; the flag's effect, the canvas-press collapse (driven through a real `PointerButton` event on `canvas_rect`), and the sorter route are all covered. A natural follow-up, also noted in review: Delete/Backspace after a slide selection currently only honours the Delete key.

**Tests:** two kittest UI tests — the pane ⇄ canvas Select All round-trip including the real canvas press, and the sorter route. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Bump quick-xml to 0.41 (RUSTSEC-2026-0194, RUSTSEC-2026-0195)
author: natocool2
body:
Bumps quick-xml from 0.38 to 0.41, which fixes two advisories:

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0194](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html): `Attributes` with the default `with_checks(true)` takes O(N²) time on a start tag with N attributes.
- [RUSTSEC-2026-0195](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0195.html): `NsReader` allocates for every `xmlns` declaration on a tag with no limit.

**Exposure today: none that I can find.** `deckcraft-pptx` reads attributes with `with_checks(false)` and does not use `NsReader`. The bump clears `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` for anyone who ships DeckCraft, and leaves one copy of quick-xml in the lockfile instead of two.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: `quick-xml = "0.41"`.
- `crates/pptx/src/xml.rs`: `decode_and_unescape_value(decoder)` is deprecated in 0.40+ (and `clippy -D warnings` would fail). It is replaced with `decoded_and_normalized_value(XmlVersion::Implicit1_0, decoder)`, which is the call the deprecated method now makes.

## How this was checked

- The quick-xml API used here was diffed between 0.38.4 and 0.41.0 (`Reader`/`Config` fields, `Event` variants, `BytesStart`/`BytesText`/`BytesRef`, `escape`): the only changes that touch this workspace are the deprecations above. `Attribute::normalized_value*` is exactly what the deprecated methods call in 0.41, so behaviour is the same as a plain bump. One difference from 0.38 that comes with the bump itself: attribute values now get XML 1.0 normalisation (a literal tab/CR/LF inside an attribute value becomes a space; `
` is kept), as the spec requires.
- `Cargo.lock` was updated with `cargo update --workspace` only: quick-xml 0.38.4 is removed and every dependent now points at the 0.41.0 already locked for `wayland-scanner`. No other package moves.
- `rustfmt --check` passes on the changed files. I did **not** build or run `cargo xtask ci` locally; CI here is the first compile, so please treat its result as the check.

It scores worse because of separate existing issues: category labels wrap instead of rotating, and the series draws a line PowerPoint hides. Chart text also comes out larger than PowerPoint's.

title: slide.new reads leading tabs in body as bullet levels; --help prints the usage (#360)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #360

## Cause

1. `slide.new` (MCP `add_slide`) builds the body with `TextBody::from_text`, which keeps a leading tab as a literal character in a level-1 paragraph. `text.set` has its own code that turns leading tabs into the outline level, so the same text gave different results through the two commands.
2. The desktop binary's argument loop knew `--control`, `--sample`, `--show` and `--version`; everything else, `--help` included, was pushed on the list of files to open, so it logged `--help: No such file or directory` and left the editor open.

## Fix

Two commits, one per report.

- `take_tab_level` (in `cmd/text.rs`) is the one rule for a leading tab (one level per tab, up to 8, dropped from the text). `text.set` uses it as before and `slide.new` now applies it to each paragraph of `body`. The title is not touched.
- `parse_args` reads the command line, and `-h` / `--help` print the usage (`--control`, `--sample`, `--show`, `--version`, `--help`) and exit, as `--version` does. Other arguments mean what they did.

## Verified

- On `main`, the test `a_new_slides_body_takes_leading_tabs_as_bullet_levels` (the issue's body `"Install from DMG\nLaunch app\n\tCheck signing\nBuild a deck"` plus a two-tab line) fails: the paragraphs come back as `(0, "\tCheck signing")` and `(0, "\t\tDeeper")`; with the fix they are `(1, "Check signing")` and `(2, "Deeper")`, the same as `text.set` gives for the same text (the test compares both). A body without tabs is unchanged.
- `help_prints_the_usage_instead_of_opening_a_file` and `the_other_arguments_still_mean_what_they_did` cover `parse_args` (the second one pins the existing flags, the environment port and a bad `--control` value). `cargo run -p deckcraft -- --help` now prints the usage and exits without opening a window.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 753 pass, 2 fail. Both fail on an unmodified `main` (`735e16d`…

title: ui: admit stock macOS CJK faces as interface fallbacks (#101)
author: Momentum96
body:
Follow-up to #331 (#101). On macOS, Korean text in the window title, recent files, outline and
notes still drew as boxes.

Cause: `uifonts.rs` skips borrowed faces over `MAX_FACE_BYTES` (48 MB). macOS's only Hangul face,
`/System/Library/Fonts/AppleSDGothicNeo.ttc`, is 55,323,000 bytes, so it was rejected; the font
database returns one face per character, so nothing else was tried. With that fixed, Simplified
Chinese hit the same wall: the picked face is `PingFang.ttc` at 78,222,888 bytes.

Fix: raise the cap to 128 MB (same bound as PhotoCraft), with a comment naming the largest stock
faces it must admit. No fonts bundled. Windows/Linux stock CJK faces are all under 48 MB, so
behaviour there is unchanged.

Reproduced on macOS: `ime_tests::cjk_text_in_the_interface_is_drawn_with_real_glyphs` failed with
`FontId{13, Proportional} draws "한국어발표자료" of "한국어 발표 자료" as boxes`; it now passes with all
four scripts checked.

Checks: `cargo test -p deckcraft-ui-egui --lib` (45 passed), `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy -p deckcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm`.

Trade-off: egui keeps its own copy of each borrowed face, so a Mac UI showing Korean and Chinese
can hold up to ~133 MB more (only once such text is on screen).

author: echelon
body:

_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: deliberately wild text slides built in PowerPoint showed many differences from DeckCraft. Typical examples:
- Hebrew/Arabic punctuation and digits ordered differently;
- small caps drawn at full size, and transparent text drawn far too faint;

- many numbering schemes wrong;

After: each was measured in PowerPoint and fixed. One commit per fix:
- **Bidi by run language:** neutrals (punctuation, spaces, digits) follow the run's `lang` as PowerPoint orders them, not plain UAX #9 (bidi probes 12.9 → 8.3–10.1).

- **Transparent text:** alpha was applied twice (60% transparent drew at 16% opacity).
- **Tab stops:** centre, right and decimal stops align the text after them, and a tab past the line end wraps.
- **Underlines:** every style (double, heavy, dotted, dash, long dash, dot-dash, wavy) drawn at the font's `post` underline metrics. "Words" underlines spaces too, as PowerPoint does.
- **Strikethrough:** at the font's OS/2 strikeout position and thickness (exact pixel rows).

author: GhostMitra
body:

title: Slide show: the presenter window opens without taking the show's keyboard (#237)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #237 on Windows and macOS; scopes what Linux still needs.

**Diagnosis.** Starting a show also opens the presenter view — a second window (`show_viewport_immediate`) over the fullscreen one, on by default (`ui.presenter_view`). A newly mapped window takes keyboard focus (the window manager's call), so the arrow keys landed in the presenter window — which handles no keys — until a click refocused the show: exactly the report of needing one mouse click before the arrows worked. The in-harness input path was verified clean first (a show answers ArrowRight from its first frame), which is what pointed at the platform-level steal.

**The fix:** the presenter viewport opens with `with_active(false)` — it does not activate itself, matching PowerPoint's presenter window, which never takes the keyboard from the show. Checked in winit 0.30's sources: Windows shows it with `SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE` and macOS uses `orderFront` — both platforms also carried this latent steal and are fixed; the presenter's own buttons still work by mouse, and no platform regresses.

**Honest limits, stated in the code comment and progress docs:** winit honors `with_active` only on Windows and macOS. On X11 and Wayland (the reporter's Fedora/GNOME) activation belongs to the window manager and the flag is inert — there the real fixes are the presenter-placement work (gaps list #9, also #202) or forwarding the show's nav keys through the presenter viewport's input, which would make the arrows work wherever focus sits; both are sketched as follow-ups rather than smuggled into this diff, since the input refactor is untestable in our harness.

**Tests:** a guard that the show answers the arrows from its first frame — the invariant any platform fix must preserve. ROADMAP row (platform-scoped, like the DX12 entry) and the slideshow-parity presenter row updated.

title: Pptx: read password-protected presentations
author: Manaseh-debug
body:
## What this does

Opening a password-protected `.pptx` no longer fails — it asks for the password and opens the deck.

- **MS-OFFCRYPTO decryption** in `crates/pptx/src/crypt.rs`: standard encryption (Office 2007: AES-128-ECB, SHA-1, versions 2–4) and agile encryption (Office 2010+: AES-128/256-CBC, SHA-1/256/384/512, spin count), unwrapped from the CFB container's `/EncryptionInfo` and `/EncryptedPackage` streams. Key material is held in `Zeroizing`, and the spin count and info-stream size are capped (`MAX_SPIN_COUNT`, `MAX_INFO`) so a hostile file can't make the reader spin.
- **A Password dialog on open** with a working retry: a rejected password keeps the text the user typed and reports itself under the field instead of pushing a fresh prompt over it. Asking for a password is not treated as an error in the status bar.
- **Legacy binary `.ppt` is reported as unsupported**, not mistaken for a protected file — it is an OLE compound file too, but carries no encryption streams.
- **Opening a protected deck warns that saving would drop the password**, because writing an encrypted package is not implemented: `"<name>: opened decrypted — DeckCraft can't encrypt on save yet, so saving it would drop the password"`.

- `crates/pptx/tests/crypt.rs` decrypts the plain, two standard (AES-128/SHA-1, AES-256/SHA-1) and four agile (AES-128/SHA-384, AES-256/SHA-256, AES-256/SHA-512, …) fixtures. `crates/pptx/tests/fixtures/make.py` regenerates them with `msoffcrypto-tool` as the encoder only and decrypts each back with that library before it is committed; the fixtures are recorded in `ATTRIBUTION.md` as CC0 and contain no Microsoft material.

title: Colour menus: an Eyedropper that takes a colour from the slide (#367)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #367

PowerPoint's Shape Fill menu has an **Eyedropper**: choose it, click anywhere and that colour is applied. DeckCraft's colour menus had theme colours, standard colours and a hex field only, so "choose colors from the presentation" meant reading a hex code off the screen by hand.

## What changed

- **`slide.colorAt {slide?, x, y, scale?}`** (new, read-only command, `cmd/file.rs`): renders the slide and returns the colour at a point in slide units: `{color: "RRGGBB", alpha, x, y}`. A point outside the slide, a missing or non-numeric coordinate or an unknown slide is an error. This is what the Eyedropper takes, and what scripts and MCP use to read a colour off a slide. `Image::straight_at` (render crate) reads one pixel as straight RGBA.

Choosing it closes the menu; over the slide the pointer is a crosshair with the colour under it and its hex beside it, a click takes the colour, Esc, a right click, a click off the slide or a click elsewhere in the window cancels. The slide is rendered once when it starts, so the hover is cheap.
- **No changes to the callers.** There are about fifteen places that show a colour menu (Shape Fill, Shape Outline, Font Color, the Format pane, …), each applying a swatch's colour its own way. The Eyedropper hands its colour back through the same menu: `color_popup` opens it for a frame and `color_grid` returns the colour as if its swatch had been clicked, so every caller applies it as it applies a swatch.
- The canvas gives the pointer to the Eyedropper while it waits, so the click does not select, move or insert anything.

title: Opus: validate the header in Decoder::from_head (#425)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #425.

`Decoder::from_head` is public and takes an `OpusHead` whose fields are all public, but it trusted them. `Decoder::new` goes through `OpusHead::parse`, which checks the stream counts and the mapping table; a hand-built header skipped those checks. With zero streams, concealment indexed `streams[0]`; with a mapping shorter than `channels`, or a mapping or coupled-stream count out of range, `decode` indexed `mapping[c]` or `scratch[s]` out of bounds. A `Result`-returning API could panic.

`OpusHead::validate` now checks the invariants the decoder indexes by: at least one channel, `1 <= streams`, `coupled_streams <= streams`, `streams + coupled_streams <= 255`, `mapping.len() == channels`, and every mapping entry either 255 (silence) or below `streams + coupled_streams`. These are the same checks and `InvalidHeader` messages that `OpusHead::parse` / `from_dops` already apply, plus the mapping-length check that the parser gets for free from slicing. `from_head` calls it first, so `Decoder::new` and `Decoder::simple` are unchanged (their headers already pass).

Tests in `multistream.rs`:
- `from_head_rejects_inconsistent_headers`: zero streams, short mapping, out-of-range mapping index, more coupled streams than streams, and zero channels all return an error. It fails on main (zero streams is accepted).
- `from_head_accepts_valid_headers`: mono, stereo, a 3-channel multistream layout and a silent (255) mapping entry still build a decoder.

title: xtask: assets audit no longer panics on Unicode names and reads real paths from git (#424)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #424.

Both problems from the issue are in `xtask/src/assets.rs`.

**1. Wildcard matching panicked on multibyte names.** `glob()` checked `rest[..i].contains('/')` for every byte offset `i` before it checked `is_char_boundary(i)`. A `*` that crossed a character such as `ż` or `日` sliced in the middle of it and panicked. The wildcard now steps only over char boundaries (`char_indices()` plus the end of the string). The rules stay the same: `*` matches any run of characters except `/`.

**2. Git-quoted paths disappeared from the audit.** `git ls-files` without `-z` quotes paths that contain non-ASCII or special characters (with the default `core.quotePath`), for example `"assets/\305\274.png"`. Those strings never `exists()` on disk, so the file was dropped from the check and a missing attribution went unreported. The audit now runs `git ls-files ... -z` and splits the output on NUL. The names come back unquoted whatever `core.quotePath` is set to, and names with spaces or newlines stay whole.

Tests (in `xtask/src/assets.rs`):
- `glob_handles_multibyte_names`: wildcards through Polish and CJK names, `*` still stops at `/`, an attributed Unicode asset passes, and an unattributed one (`assets/é.png`) is reported. On `main` the first assertion panics with "byte index 1 is not a char boundary".
- `ls_files_output_is_nul_separated_and_unquoted`: NUL-separated output with a Unicode name and a name that contains a space and a newline parses to the exact file names.

title: CLI: render-transition refuses --t values that would share one file name (#423)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #423.

When `render-transition` is given several `--t` values, each frame is written to `<stem>-t<value>.png`, with the value rounded to three decimals. Two different values that round to the same name, such as `0.1001,0.1002`, or the same value given twice, wrote to the same file. Only the last frame was kept, but the command still printed one output line for each frame.

The output paths are now built before anything is rendered or written, by a small `frame_paths` helper. If two of them are the same, the command returns an error that names the file, and nothing is written. This is the "detect/reject collisions before any output writes" option from the issue. The file names stay the same, so scripts that read `-t0.250.png` etc. keep working. A single `--t` still writes to OUT unchanged.

Tests (`apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs`):
- `single_frame_uses_out_as_is`: one value writes to OUT.
- `frames_get_distinct_names`: ordinary separated values get the existing `-tN.NNN.png` names.
- `values_rounding_to_one_name_are_rejected`: `0.1001,0.1002` and `0.5,0.5` give an error. Without the fix, there was no check, so both pairs went to one file.

title: Info: keep a property draft when another field or the side menu is clicked (#422)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #422.

The Info page lost a property edit unless it was finished with Enter. I checked the two paths the issue describes against `main`:

- **Clicking another field (e.g. edit Author, then click Title).** Title is drawn first and takes the focus when it is clicked. When Author was drawn next, its draft had already been reset to the saved value, because the field no longer had the focus. `lost_focus` then saw nothing to commit. Now the commit check runs after the `TextEdit` is drawn, and the reset to the saved value runs only when the field has no focus and has nothing to commit.
- **Clicking a side-menu entry (Save, Home, Save As, Close, ...).** The side menu is drawn before the page, so `Save` ran `app.save()` before the field could commit. The file was written without the new value and the presentation was left dirty. Each side-menu click now commits the Info page's drafts first (`commit_props`, which runs only while Info is shown), and then runs the action.

Esc is unchanged: it still leaves the File tab before the page is drawn, and the edit is dropped. Enter still commits as before.

Tests (kittest, real pointer input):
- `info_keeps_a_property_draft_when_another_field_is_clicked`: type an Author, click Title, and check that the author is set.
- `info_saves_a_property_draft_when_save_is_clicked`: on a presentation that has a file, type an Author and click Save. The author is set and the presentation is not dirty, so the value went into the saved file.

Both tests fail on `main`. The existing Enter test (`info_shows_and_edits_the_properties`) still covers the Enter path.

title: Engine: moving the selection to another text body settles the composition (#421)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #421.

`Session::select` changed the selection without touching an active IME composition. The composition only stores an offset and a length, so after selecting another text body, the next `compose_text`/`commit_text` replaced characters at that offset in the *new* body, while the old body kept its preedit.

`Session::select` now records the text owner (slide, target, shape, table cell, notes) before running the callback and, if a composition is active and the owner changed, settles it with `end_composition()`. This is the same thing `execute` (journalled commands), `key` and pointer presses already do, so the old body keeps its composed text as one "Type Text" undo step and the new body is left untouched. Moving the caret inside the same body leaves the composition alone, as before.

Tests (`tests_keys.rs`), both failing on `main`:
- `select_into_another_body_settles_the_composition`: compose in text box A, select text box B, commit: B gets only the committed text, A keeps its composed text.
- `select_into_another_table_cell_settles_the_composition`: the same between two cells of one table.

title: Honeycomb transition: cover the bottom of the slide with new-slide cells (#420)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #420.

`honeycomb` placed row centres every `rh * 0.866` but counted rows as if they were `rh * 1.5` apart. On a 16:9 slide that gave 11 rows, so the last new-slide cells stopped at about y = 0.75 and the bottom quarter stayed black until the frame at t = 1 snapped to the full new slide.

The row count now uses the same spacing as the placement: `(1 / (rh * 0.866)).ceil() + 2`. The hex vertical radius is `0.577 * rh`, so a row spacing of `0.866 * rh` (1.5 radii) is the correct pointy-top lattice, and the last row now sits below y = 1 for every aspect. Columns already cover the full width (`0..=cols` with half-column offset), so they are unchanged.

Test: `honeycomb_new_cells_reach_the_bottom_of_the_slide` checks that at t = 0.99 the new-slide cells reach y >= 1 for 16:9 and 4:3. It fails on main (bottom about 0.75) and passes with the fix.
