title: Media: preserve video frames and EOF across seeks
author: MMexicann
body:
Fixes #416.

VideoFeed::seek could discard new-generation frames and EOF after sending a seek command. Leave queue consumption to pull(), which filters stale generations and unblocks the worker.

Adds regression coverage for queued frames and EOF, successive seeks, a full stale queue, and repeated seeks through H.264, HEVC, VP9 and AV1. Updates playback documentation and the roadmap.

Validation: all six cargo xtask ci gates passed; 892 tests passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. The deterministic queue regression failed before the fix.

Related: #449 is already open for this race. This PR offers consumption-time generation filtering and additional regression tests that can be reused with that fix.

title: Metafile: EMF+ arcs, convex clip paths, wrapped strings, nested metafiles
author: NikitkaRa
body:
**Stacked on #582, which is itself stacked on #574.** This branch contains both PRs' commits, so review only the last commit (or review this PR after they merge). No issue exists. This is PPTX fidelity (ROADMAP Upcoming, item 2) and the third EMF+ slice.

## Summary
- **Arcs and pies:** FillPie, DrawPie and DrawArc. GDI+ angles, measured along rays from the centre, are converted to the ellipse parameter, with cubics of at most 90°.
- **Real clip paths:** the canvas clip is now a convex device polygon, not a rectangle.
  - Clip rectangles stay exact under rotation.
  - Clip paths and region nodes that form one convex outline (ellipses, rounded or rotated rectangles, diamonds) clip to that outline.
  - Fills use Sutherland–Hodgman against the polygon and outlines use Cyrus–Beck. Bitmaps are cropped, then masked outside a non-rectangular clip. Text gets the polygon's bounding rectangle.
  - Non-convex clips still fall back to their bounding rectangle. Union is the rectangle around both; XOR, exclude and complement keep the left area.
- **String wrapping:** DrawString word-wraps to the layout width unless NoWrap is set. A word wider than the line breaks between characters. Widths are estimated from typical proportional character widths, because the metafile crate has no fonts.
- **Glyph-index driver strings:** for the Windows core fonts that keep the standard Macintosh glyph order (Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Verdana, Georgia, Tahoma, Trebuchet MS, Comic Sans MS, Impact), glyphs 3..=97 map back to ASCII. Other fonts, or glyphs outside that range, are still skipped.
- **Nested metafile images:** a metafile image object (WMF, placeable WMF, EMF, EMF+) is parsed with this crate and its items are stretched into the DrawImage destination. Paths, tiles, bitmaps and text are all carried over. Nesting is capped at 3 levels.

## Test plan

  - quarter pie geometry and a half-circle arc
  - a diamond clip path that cuts the square's corners
  - DrawStrin…

title: Charts: histograms, Pareto and box and whisker; Office 2016 charts save as themselves
author: NikitkaRa
body:
**Stacked on #537, which is itself stacked on #532.** This branch contains both PRs' commits, so review only the last commit (or review this PR after they merge). No issue exists. This covers the `chartex` chart types from the after-beta pool in docs/gaps.md (Charts: data grid, elements and the newer chart types).

## Summary
- **Histogram and Pareto:**
  - The model bins the first series' observations by `bin_size`, else `bin_count`, else Scott's rule (as Excel does). Bins are (lo, hi], with the minimum in the first bin, and there are at most 1000.
  - They draw as touching columns labelled `[a, b]` / `(b, c]`.
  - A Pareto sorts its bins and adds the cumulative percentage as a line on a 0–100 % secondary axis.
  - `cx:binning` (`binCount` and `binSize`) is read and written.
- **Box and whisker:**
  - Points are grouped by category label, and each series is drawn side by side in each group.
  - Quartiles use Excel's exclusive method. Whiskers run to the furthest point within 1.5 IQR, outliers are dots, and the mean is an ×.
  - The bar renderer draws the frame (value axis, gridlines, groups, legend).
- **Editing and saving:** an edited or new Office 2016 chart (waterfall, funnel, treemap, sunburst, histogram, Pareto, box) is now written as a `chartEx` part from the model, with the plain chart as the `mc:Fallback`, so it stays its own type. Before, it became a plain column chart. Unchanged imported charts still keep their original part (#532).
- **Commands and UI:**
  - The Insert › Chart and Change Chart Type menus list Pareto, Box and Whisker and Sunburst after a separator (the other four were already listed).
  - `chart.options` takes `binCount`, `binSize` (null for automatic) and `subtotals` (waterfall totals).
  - `chart.type` turns on gridlines and varied colours for these types, as their chartEx defaults do.
  - The sample data for histogram, Pareto and box charts is raw observations.
- docs/gaps.md and docs/file-format-parity.md are updated.

title: Render 3-D extrusions: sides under turned cameras (3-D slice 1)
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary
Slice 1 of the gaps.md "Edit points, text warp, 3-D" item's 3-D part: extrusion. Based on `main`.

Overlap check: #508 (w3, Format Shape 3-D controls: engine and pane), #562 (bevel round-trip in PPTX) and #578 (3-D models round-trip) don't touch `crates/render`. This PR changes only the renderer and reads the `raw3d` XML those PRs keep.

- New `render/src/extrude.rs`: reads `a:sp3d extrusionH` and `a:extrusionClr` (`srgbClr` or `schemeClr`) from the kept 3-D XML. It only applies when the deck also has an `a:scene3d`, because without a scene PowerPoint draws the shape flat.
- `camera::project3` projects points off the shape's plane, which gives the camera's view of the depth axis (`back_offset`).
- The renderer sweeps the shape's outline from the back face to the front face in the side colour before drawing the face. The side colour is the extrusion colour, or the fill's, at 62 % brightness. It uses one pixel per step, capped at 96 steps.
- Front-facing cameras show no sides, as in PowerPoint.
- Limitations: one shade for all sides (PowerPoint shades each side by its normal and light rig), and no contour. Lighting rigs and materials are the next slice.

Checked by eye in a 960×540 render: an isometric cube, a red-sided isometric ellipse, a perspective star with accent-2 sides, and a front-camera box with no sides. The sides sit behind the face on the side the camera turns away.

## Testing
- `extrude` unit tests: depth and colour parsing, no extrusion without a scene, and the back face's direction.
- `extrusions_show_their_sides_under_a_turned_camera` (render): the red sides are drawn, the cube's sides add ink, and a front camera adds none. Set `DECKCRAFT_PNG_OUT=…png` to dump the render.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: SmartArt: Text Pane, add and remove shapes, promote and demote
author: NikitkaRa
body:
First slice of SmartArt editing (after-beta pool in docs/gaps.md). Based on `main`; it doesn't depend on any open PR. #242 and #209 touch PowerPoint-read SmartArt, which this doesn't change.

## Summary
- **Model:** `Shape.diagram: Option<Diagram>`, holding the layout kind and its nodes (`{text, level}`). It is skipped when `None`, so existing files are unchanged, and it is saved in `.deckcraft`.
- **Engine:** new `crates/engine/src/cmd/smartart.rs`.
  - Every edit regenerates the group's children inside its child rectangle, so the diagram keeps its place and size. Text typed straight into a diagram shape is read back into the nodes first.
  - New commands, each targeting the SmartArt group or any shape inside it:
    - `smartArt.nodes` (query)
    - `smartArt.setNodes`: the whole outline, tab-indented lines, or one node's text
    - `smartArt.addNode`: after, before, above or below, as in PowerPoint
    - `smartArt.removeNode`: sub-points move up a level
    - `smartArt.promote` and `smartArt.demote`: they move the node's whole subtree
    - `smartArt.layout`
- **Layouts:** sub-points become bullets inside their parent's shape in list, process, cycle, pyramid and matrix. Hierarchy is now a real tree: each subtree is as wide as its leaves, with connector lines.
- **`insert.smartArt`:** accepts tab-indented `items` or `nodes`, and returns `{id}`.
- **UI:**
  - A **SmartArt Design** contextual tab with Text Pane, Add Shape (After/Before/Above/Below), Promote, Demote and Layout.
  - A **Text Pane** task pane: Enter adds a line, Tab and Shift+Tab demote and promote, Backspace on an empty line removes it, and a line's edit is committed when it loses focus.
  - Inserting a SmartArt graphic opens the Text Pane.
- **Docs:** gaps.md (SmartArt entry rewritten), parity checklist (Text pane and layout switching M → P, recomputed), file-format and target-app parity.
- **Not in this slice:** PowerPoint-authored diagrams are still read as plain groups (no outline, so no Text Pane)…

title: Native macOS menu bar
author: RiccardoTancredi
body:
## Native macOS menu bar

### What
A real macOS menu bar built from the existing **`menus::menu_tree`** (DeckCraft, File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Arrange, Slide Show, Window, Help), with **Open Recent**.

### Why
DeckCraft defined a menu tree "shared with the native macOS menu bar" but had no bar wired up; this adds it.

### How it stays safe

title: Export: MP4 and MOV video of the deck, with our own H.264 encoder
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. This is the "No video or animated GIF export" item from the after-beta list in docs/gaps.md. Animated GIF is #171/#177; this PR does the MP4/MOV half and doesn't touch GIF.

## Summary
- `file.export` with `format: mp4|mov` (or a `.mp4`/`.m4v`/`.mov` path): plays each slide's transition, then holds the slide for its "advance after" time, otherwise `secondsPerSlide` (default 5 s). Takes `height` (default 1080, from 480p to 4K; width follows the slide aspect, both even), `fps` (1–60, default 30) and `includeHidden`. The result reports bytes, frames, size and seconds.
- New `deckcraft_h264::Encoder` (`crates/h264/src/encoder.rs`), written from H.264 itself, as the inverse of our decoder:
  - Constrained Baseline, CAVLC, 4:2:0, one slice per picture, deblocking off.
  - Every coded macroblock is Intra 16x16 (V, H or DC, picked by SAD) with chroma DC prediction.
  - In P pictures, macroblocks whose source is unchanged are skipped, so a held slide costs a few bytes a frame.
  - The SPS carries BT.709 VUI and timing, and the level comes from the size and frame rate.
- `crates/engine/src/video.rs`:
  - Builds the timeline (capped at 2 h at 30 fps), renders frames through `render_slide`/`render_transition` and muxes them with `deckcraft_isobmff::Mp4Writer` (faststart, MP4 or QuickTime brand).
  - A key frame starts every slide and every transition, and at least every 2 s.
  - The file is written through a temporary sibling.
- No external tools or new third-party crates: the engine now depends directly on our own `deckcraft-h264` and `deckcraft-isobmff` (both lower layers; the layers check passes).
- Docs: the MP4/MOV row in file-format-parity.md is marked yes, and the gaps.md entry now names what's left (in-slide animations, audio, GIF in #177).

Overlap: #177 also edits `file.export` and `format_for_path` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs` (for GIF), so expect a small textual conflict in whichever lands second.

title: Review: spelling with Hunspell dictionaries, suggestions, Change and Ignore All
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Based on main. Covers the spelling part of gaps.md "Proofing" (after beta); thesaurus (#549) and AutoCorrect (#521) have their own PRs.

title: Draw: pen pressure scales ink width
author: NikitkaRa
body:
## Summary

- Ink strokes keep the pointer's pressure. Each segment is drawn at the average of its endpoint widths. A reading of 1 is the pen width, and a light touch stays at least 8% of the pen so a zero reading is still visible.
- A mouse, a missing or non-finite reading, and a stroke whose samples are all the old placeholder 0.5 still draw at the pen width, so existing decks and the PPTX ink fixture look the same.
- PPTX still writes one freeform per stroke. A pressured stroke exports at the mean sample width. A legacy flat 0.5 stroke stays at the pen width.
- `ui.pointer` on the control channel and the headless MCP server takes an optional `pressure` from 0 to 1. The editor reads touch force when a pen reports it. macOS Force Touch does not reach the app, because egui-winit drops that event.
- Tilt, pinch-zoom, and the slide-show annotation pen are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Model: legacy 0.5 stays at the pen width; pressure 1 is full width; 0.25 is a quarter; 0 is the 8% floor; NaN is full width
- [x] Engine: a pen stroke stores 0.2, 1.0, 0.4; a mouse and a NaN reading store 1.0
- [x] Render: a 1.0-to-0.12 stroke covers more of the slide on the firm half; a flat 0.5 stroke matches a flat 1.0 stroke
- [x] PPTX: the existing ink fixture still round-trips at pen width 3; a 1 / 0.5 / 0 stroke exports at the mean width
- [x] Live on macOS: `ui.pointer` stored pressure as sent; a scale-4 render measured the firm part 8 px, the light part 2 px, the mouse stroke 8 px

author: NikitkaRa
body:
**Stacked on #609** (branch `spelling`); merge that first — this diff includes its commit until then.

## Summary

The check runs on a `spelling` worker thread (`ui-egui/src/squiggles.rs`), never the UI thread: the UI sends the slide's paragraphs for one document revision, the worker drops superseded jobs and caches results per paragraph content (typing re-checks only the edited paragraph), then asks for a repaint. - **Language per run:** words take the `lang` of the run they start in (already read/written from PPTX `a:rPr@lang`); `review.spelling` reports `para/start/end/lang`; `lang` param is the default for runs without one. Hyphenated words are checked part by part.
- **Compounds:** `COMPOUNDFLAG`, `COMPOUNDBEGIN/MIDDLE/END`, `COMPOUNDMIN`, `COMPOUNDWORDMAX`, `ONLYINCOMPOUND`; last part may carry a suffix.

title: Animations: check effect options and accept direction words
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. I found this while checking #616's video frames: `animation.add {"effect":"fly","option":"fromBottom"}` was accepted, and the shape flew in diagonally from the bottom right. title: Metafile: EMF+ cardinal curves and region fills
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Stacked on #588 (EMF+ arcs, clip paths, wrapped strings), which is on #582 → #574. Review only the last commit. No issue: these EMF+ drawing records were skipped, so pictures that use them lost those shapes. GDI+ draws charts' smoothed lines and freehand outlines as cardinal splines, and fills shaded areas as regions.

## Summary
- `EmfPlusDrawCurve` (0x4018), `EmfPlusDrawClosedCurve` (0x4017) and `EmfPlusFillClosedCurve` (0x4016) draw as cubic Béziers through the points. Each segment's control points are a third of the tension along the neighbouring chords (GDI+ cardinal splines, default tension 0.5).
  - Open curves honour the record's offset and segment count, clamped to the points there are.
  - Closed curves wrap around and close.
  - Compressed (16-bit) points work, and the S flag colour brushes too.
- `EmfPlusFillRegion` (0x4013) fills the region object's area, the same convex area the region clip already uses.
- Hostile input is safe: a NaN tension, fewer than two points, an offset past the end or a missing region draws nothing and never panics.
- Not in this PR: `Clear` (it would need the picture's frame, and is normally transparent) and `StrokeFillPath`.

## Test plan

- [x] `emfplus_cardinal_curves_and_region_fill`: the closed curve is four cubics through a diamond's corners and closes, the open curve is four cubics without closing, and the region fill is its rectangle.

title: Metafile: EMF+ Clear, and the EMF+ record coverage written down
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Stacked on #633 (→ #588 → #582 → #574). Review only the last commit. No issue: this closes out the EMF+ work.

## Summary
- **`EmfPlusClear` (0x4009)** paints the whole picture frame in its ARGB colour. It ignores the world transform and the clip, as GDI+'s `Graphics::Clear` does. A transparent clear, the usual one, draws nothing, and so does a file with no frame. The EMF reader now passes the frame to the EMF+ player for this.
- **StrokeFillPath (0x4037) is not implemented, on purpose.** MS-EMFPLUS lists it in the record-type enumeration but not among the drawing records (§2.3.4), and gives it no layout. gdiplusenums.h documents it as "TBD", and GDI+ doesn't write it, so any guess at its fields could draw garbage. It stays skipped.
- **String drawing was already covered:** DrawString and DrawDriverString landed in #582/#588 (wrapping, formats, and glyph-index driver strings for the core fonts). So every drawing record of §2.3.4 is now played.
- **Docs:**
  - The `emfplus.rs` module doc now lists what is played, what is not drawn (image attributes, glyph indices of other fonts, XOR/exclude/complement regions), and what is deliberately ignored (rendering hints, rendering origin, SerializableObject image effects, SetTSGraphics/SetTSClip, StrokeFillPath).
  - file-format-parity.md (EMF/WMF row) and gaps.md no longer say "EMF+ records are not drawn".

## Test plan

title: Charts: bar widths, column/bar point fills, smoothed lines and chart text colour as the file sets them
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by rendering test decks headlessly and comparing them with LibreOffice's PNG export of the same files. The repo has no .pptx files, so the decks were: the engine sample (via `DECKCRAFT_PPTX_OUT`), a python-pptx deck (placeholders, bullets, table, four chart types, autoshapes, gradients, mixed runs), and LibreOffice's 23 bundled presentation templates saved as .pptx. Ranked by mean pixel difference, the worst real mismatch was the chart slides (e.g. Freshes slide 6 and 7):

- **Per-point fills (`c:dPt`) were ignored on column/bar charts.** They were read but only pie used them, so a series with white points drew in the accent colour. Columns and bars now take each point's own fill.
- **Chart text colour from `c:txPr` was never read.** `Chart::text_color` existed but nothing set it, so light axis labels on dark slides drew dark grey and were invisible. It is now read from the axes', legend's, or chart's text properties.
- **Clustered bars were far too thin, on every multi-series column or bar chart.** This was the largest pixel difference in the corpus (the engine sample's chart slide). Gap width and overlap are fractions of *one bar's* width, so a band holds `n − (n−1)·overlap + gap` bars. The renderer instead split `band / (1 + gap)` among the series. A bar group without `c:gapWidth`/`c:overlap` now also takes the schema's defaults (150 %, 0 %) instead of PowerPoint's new-chart 219 %/−27 %.
- **`c:smooth` lines drew as straight segments.** They now draw as a Catmull-Rom curve through every point, as PowerPoint does.

Tests: a render test (one red point's column; bar width for gap 150 %; smoothing curve shape) and a reader test (axis text colour; gap/overlap defaults). `cargo xtask ci` passed (6/6). I checked the before/after renders against LibreOffice by eye: Freshes slide 6 now has white columns and white axis labels, and slide 7 has curved lines.

Not covered here, also seen in the comparison: horizontal bar charts list the first category at the top, but Po…

title: Render: cap dash count so a tiny dash on a huge shape can't crash on open
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by fuzzing the pptx open/save round trip with mutated decks (truncated zips, missing parts, bad rels, extreme attribute values; 3000+ mutation runs plus 47 crafted extreme-value slides, each imported, exported, reimported and rendered).

**Bug:** a shape with `<a:custDash><a:ds d="1" sp="1"/></a:custDash>` and a hairline width on a 2147483647 EMU rectangle opens fine, but drawing the slide aborts the whole process with `memory allocation of 7516192768 bytes failed`. The stroker expands each dash into its own outline. That means hundreds of thousands of dashes, which is a startup crash for any deck with this slide visible.

**Fix:** `limit_dash_count` measures the path and scales the dash pattern evenly once a stroke would get more than 20,000 dashes. At that density the dashes are far below a pixel, so it looks the same. Ordinary lines keep their pattern exactly. A non-finite path length draws solid.

**Test:** `a_tiny_dash_on_a_huge_shape_draws_without_running_out_of_memory` in render/tests_wild.rs (renders the case; checks the limit leaves normal patterns unchanged and caps huge ones at the limit).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. Not stacked: from main.

title: Shapes: star4/star5 text rectangles as the standard defines them
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found while re-ranking the LibreOffice-vs-render comparison (/workspace/fid corpus: the engine sample, a python-pptx deck, LibreOffice's 23 templates as .pptx) for non-chart mismatches.

The 5-point star's text area was approximated as the box inset by ~15 % per side, about 0.69 of the width. ECMA-376's presetShapeDefinitions give star5 the inner pentagon, `sx1..sx4 × sy1..sy3`, about 0.38 of the width at the default adjust. So text that PowerPoint and LibreOffice wrap ("Shape 3" at 18 pt in a 2-inch star) stayed on one line, too wide and too high. star4 now uses its spec rectangle too: the square through the inner points at 45°. Other stars keep the old approximation.

Test: `star_text_rectangles_follow_the_standard`. `cargo xtask ci` passed (6/6). Checked by eye: the star's text now wraps and sits exactly as in LibreOffice's export.

Other differences reviewed and left alone, because LibreOffice is the one that's off or ours is tuned to PowerPoint:
- LibreOffice prints the empty placeholder prompts.
- It doesn't bold the table style's header row.
- It draws a transparent-background hatch pale.
- Its pattern tiles are at device pixels.
- Radial and rotWithShape=0 flipped gradients are drawn as deliberately tuned to PowerPoint.

Open question for someone with PowerPoint: does flipping a shape with rotWithShape=0 mirror a linear gradient? LibreOffice mirrors it; we don't (Blue Curve template).

title: Shapes: chevron text rectangle per presetShapeDefinitions
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by re-ranking the 116-slide LibreOffice comparison (see #638) for non-chart mismatches.

A chevron's text box ran from the notch to halfway along the point (`d .. w − d/2`). presetShapeDefinitions give `il = ?: dx x1 l`, `ir = ?: dx x2 r` with `dx = x2 − x1`:
- When the notch and the point's base don't meet, the text box spans the notch to the point's base (x1 .. x2).
- Once they meet or cross (any chevron as tall as it is wide at the default 50 %), the text box spans the whole width.

So a square chevron's 'Shape 4' was drawn a couple of letters per line in a sliver. Now it's set on one line across the shape, as LibreOffice (and the standard) lay it out. homePlate was already right and is now covered by the test too.

Test: `chevron_text_rectangle_follows_the_standard` (wide, square, homePlate). `cargo xtask ci` passed (6/6). Checked by eye against LibreOffice's render of a python-pptx shapes slide.

**Other non-chart differences seen (not changed here):**
- LibreOffice-only quirks: it prints placeholder prompt text, and it drops the bold first-row text of table styles. PowerPoint keeps both, and so do we.
- Unverified without PowerPoint: whether flips mirror a `rotWithShape="0"` linear gradient (LibreOffice does, our renderer deliberately doesn't), and the radius of a `path="circle"` gradient focused on an edge (Sunset template).

title: Startup: survive damaged settings, font folders, recovery folders and small texture limits
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. These are beta-priority startup crashes and hangs I reproduced on Linux.

## Summary
- **Settings (`ui.json`, `prefs.json`):**
  - New `ui_egui::settings` module. It reads regular files only, caps them at 4 MiB, and logs parse errors (they no longer fail startup).
  - `UiState::sanitized` and `Prefs::sanitized` clamp every numeric field and dedup and cap the recent files list.
  - Writes are atomic (tmp file, then rename).
  - Before this, a saved `"zoom": 1e30` killed the app at startup (abort/OOM), and `1e4` panicked in egui.
- **Canvas zoom:** the canvas and the control protocol clamp a stray zoom to `ZOOM_RANGE`. The status bar now shows the zoom actually in use.
- **Canvas texture:** the texture is cut to `max_texture_side`. At 400% zoom, a GPU or software fallback with a 2048 limit panicked ("Texture slide-canvas has size 3840x2160").
- **System font scan:**
  - It opens only regular files between 13 B and 512 MiB, and `load_cataloged` follows the same rule.
  - A FIFO named `*.ttf` in `~/.fonts` used to hang startup forever.
  - The scan is now capped at depth 12 and 200k entries, so a link to `/` can't turn into a disk crawl.
- **AutoRecover:** entries that aren't regular files are skipped, which removes another FIFO hang. At most 32 presentations reopen per start, newest first; the rest stay on disk for the next start.

## Test plan
- [x] `settings::tests`: damaged files, out-of-range values, round trip with no tmp file left behind, and the window opening with hostile saved state. I checked the harness renders by eye.

title: Text: shrink on overflow gives up at once when even 10% overflows
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by the resource-exhaustion fuzz pass: a deck whose shape has `normAutofit` and far more text than its box can hold took **~15 s to open**. The test case was a 0.1-inch box with 20,000 paragraphs, and every redraw of the slide paid that cost again.

**Cause:** `layout` binary-searches the font scale between 10% and 100% with 12 more full layouts. When even 10% overflows, none of them can fit, but the search still lays out the whole body 13 times before falling back to 10%.

**Fix:** lay out at the smallest scale first. If that overflows, return it right away; every larger scale overflows too, and the result is the one the search ended with before. Otherwise the search runs as before, seeded with the 10% layout as its fallback. Total time for the fuzz deck: 17 s → about 2 s (import + render + export).

**Test:** `shrink_gives_up_at_once_when_even_the_smallest_scale_overflows` counts layout passes with a test-only thread-local counter. It allows at most 2 passes, and was 14 before the fix (confirmed failing on main). It also checks that text which fits somewhere in the range still gets searched to a scale between 10% and 100%.

Overlaps in area with #226 and #485 (which draw the saved fontScale), but not in logic. Not stacked: from main. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: PPTX: shape text anchors at the top when the file gives no anchor; write ctr for centred shapes
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Fidelity sweep (the LibreOffice comparison, see #638), text layout.

**Mismatch.** The model centres a shape's text when it has no anchor of its own, and the writer omitted the anchor in that case. A file's `<a:bodyPr/>` without `anchor` means **top** (ECMA-376 default, unless the theme's `a:objectDefaults/a:spDef/a:bodyPr` says otherwise). Two consequences:
- Our own saved decks opened in PowerPoint and LibreOffice with every shape's text at the top. The engine sample's process slide ('Solar wind', 'Magnetosphere'…) showed it clearly.
- Files from other apps that omit the anchor drew centred here.

**Fix.**
- Writer: a non-placeholder, non-text-box shape with no anchor writes `anchor="ctr"`.
- Reader: such a shape's text takes the file's anchor, else the theme's spDef anchor (Office themes set `ctr`), else top. Middle is stored as unset (the model's default), so round trips stay equal. Placeholders, text boxes and tables keep inheriting as before.

Test `tests/anchor.rs`: the sample's centred shapes survive export/import; the same file with the anchors stripped reads as top; adding an Office-style spDef with `anchor="ctr"` reads as centred. `cargo xtask ci` passed (6/6). Checked by eye: re-rendered the corpus, and the sample's process slide (rendered from a deck saved before this fix) now anchors top exactly like LibreOffice's export of the same file. No other slide changed beyond noise.

title: Charts: draw axis titles
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by a LibreOffice comparison of a python-pptx chart deck: 11 slides covering column, line, area, stacked area, pie, doughnut, scatter, bar, 100 % stacked, markers, axis formats and titles, data labels and legends.

**Mismatch.** Axis titles (`c:catAx/c:title`, `c:valAx/c:title`) were read into `Chart::axis_titles` and written back, but never drawn. A chart with 'Revenue' and 'Month' titles showed neither.

title: Startup: fall back to Wayland when DISPLAY names no X server
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. This is a Linux startup failure I found during the startup-robustness sweep. The branch is fresh from main and independent of #644, #652 and #655.

## Summary
- **The failure:** `main` forces X11 whenever `DISPLAY` is set. A stale `DISPLAY` (left by an ended `ssh -X` session, or a desktop with Xwayland turned off) made startup fail with winit's "failed to open display", even though a Wayland compositor was running.
- **New `display::choose` (a pure function, unit-tested):**
  - A local `DISPLAY` (`:N`, `:N.S`, `unix:N`) whose `/tmp/.X11-unix/XN` socket is missing starts on Wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set.
  - Remote displays (`host:10.0`) and live X servers keep X11, as before.
- **`DECKCRAFT_WAYLAND`:** still forces Wayland, but only when a compositor is there. Without one it now keeps X11 instead of failing.
- **No display at all:** with neither variable set, the app prints a plain "needs a graphical session" message and logs it before winit's error.

## Test plan
- [x] `display::tests::a_stale_local_display_falls_back_to_wayland`
- [x] `display::tests::wayland_only_forced_and_no_display_at_all`
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)
- [ ] Manual, on a Wayland desktop: run with `DISPLAY=:9` set and confirm the window opens on Wayland. The box has no compositor, so I couldn't run this end to end.

Parity checklist: no feature rows. This is platform robustness only.

title: Render: don't lay out table cell text that lands off the slide
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Follow-up to the fuzz pass (#639, #651). A 200 × 200 table of long text took ~70 s to draw. Every cell's text was laid out twice: once to size its row and once to draw it, even for the thousands of rows far below the slide.

**Change:** `table::draw` skips the drawing layout for a cell whose rectangle, mapped to the render target and grown by a 64 px margin, lies wholly outside that target. Fills, borders and row heights are unchanged.

**Why it's safe:** the skip applies only where the text can't leave its cell, i.e. single-row cells with horizontal text whose row isn't at the 20,000 pt height cap. Rows grow to fit their text, so nothing overflows. Spanned rows, vertical text and capped rows are always drawn. The check uses the actual target size, so thumbnails, offscreen effect layers and zoomed views all cull against what they really draw into.

**Effect:** halves the text layout cost of huge tables (the row-height pass still measures every cell, which PowerPoint's own row sizing needs too).

**Test:** `table_rows_below_the_slide_are_not_laid_out_and_the_slide_looks_the_same`. It renders a 500-row table and checks that only on-slide cells were laid out (between 20 and 80, against 1000 before the fix; confirmed failing on main). It also checks the image is pixel-identical to a 30-row table that already runs past the slide's bottom.

Not stacked: from main. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Format: repair degenerate slide sizes on load
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. This continues the startup-robustness sweep: degenerate slide sizes in loaded files. The branch is fresh from main and doesn't depend on #644, #652, #655 or #661. I checked w4's claims and open PRs: none touch `repair`, the reader for `slideSize`/`notesSize`, or the size fields.

## Summary
- **`deckcraft_format::repair` and the new `sane_slide_size`:**
  - Each slide side is brought into 72–4032 pt (`SLIDE_SIDE`). That is PowerPoint's 1–56 in, the range Design › Slide Size already allows. Before, repair allowed 1–4000 pt.
  - A zero, negative or non-finite size becomes the 16:9 default.
  - A bad notes size gets the default.
- **Native reader:** a `slideSize`/`notesSize` that is null, a string or missing a side is read as NaN, and repair then replaces it.
  - Before, such a file failed to open with "damaged file: invalid type: null". DeckCraft itself writes null whenever a size is NaN or infinite.
- **Canvas and slide show fit:** both treat a zero or non-finite side as 1 pt, so a bad size set in memory can't make the layout infinite or NaN.

## Test plan

- [x] `format::tests::files_with_unreadable_slide_sizes_still_open`: null, string, missing side, null object, and a number

- [x] `slide_size_tests::the_canvas_fit_survives_a_zero_slide_size_in_memory`

Note: extreme aspect ratios that are still valid (for example 72×4000 pt) can still make textures larger than 2048 px in thumbnails. That case is #652's, so this PR's view test sticks to sizes that repair to moderate shapes.

title: Format: never save a .deckcraft that cannot be reopened over a NaN
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. A follow-up to #665: DeckCraft could save a `.deckcraft` file that it couldn't reopen. The branch is fresh from main. There is no w4 claim on the native format; w4's open claims are PPTX reader fuzz, duplicate shape ids and #631.

## Summary
- **The bug:** serde_json writes NaN and ±infinity as `null`, and `null` doesn't read back as a number. A single NaN in any number field that can't be empty (shape position, size, rotation, picture crop, ink width, group child space, and so on) made the saved file and its AutoRecover copy fail to open with "damaged file: invalid type: null, expected f64". Optional fields came back as unset, so they never failed.
- **Writer:** the new `finite::Finite` serializer adapter writes non-finite floats as 0 and passes everything else through unchanged. `save` uses it for `presentation.json`.
- **Loader:** files already written with those nulls now open. Each `null` where a number belongs reads as 0.
  - serde reports the exact position, except inside tagged enums such as picture crop and group child space, where it only reports the end of the enclosing object. There, candidate nulls are tried nearest first, and a patch is kept only when the parse gets further. That rule handles one null per such object.
  - Up to 256 fixes per file. Any other damage still fails as before.
- **`repair`** (runs after both native and PPTX loads) now also brings shape numbers into range:
  - positions and sizes: finite, within ±1e6 pt, sizes at least 0
  - rotation: 0–360°
  - picture crop: -10..1
  - font sizes: 1–4000 pt (PowerPoint's limit)
  - line widths: 0–1584 pt (PowerPoint's limit)
- **Animation timings** are `u32`, so they can't carry NaN. Nothing to fix there.

## Test plan
- [x] `finite::tests::non_finite_floats_are_written_as_zero_and_nothing_else_changes`: empty optionals stay `null`.
- [x] `tests::a_file_saved_with_non_finite_numbers_reopens`: NaN, infinity, huge and negative values across geometry, crop, line width, font sizes and a…

title: Show: a first animation set to With/After Previous plays when the slide appears
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #631

**Bug:** a slide whose first animation starts With or After Previous appeared fully built in the slide show.

**Cause:** `ShowState::enter` already starts an automatic step 0 (it sets `playing`). `Show::after_enter` then called `state.next()` again, which treats a playing step as a click and finishes it, so `step` jumped to 1.

**Fix:** as suggested in the issue. `after_enter` only starts the step's clock when `enter` already started the step. It calls `next()` only for autoplay previews, where an On Click first step hasn't started yet.

**Test:** `a_first_animation_after_or_with_previous_plays_when_the_slide_appears` (ui-egui show tests). It covers After Previous and With Previous, both when starting the show on the slide and when arriving from the slide before: the slide stays at step 0 with the step playing and its clock set. It also checks that On Click still waits. Confirmed failing on main (`(1, false)` instead of `(0, true)`).

Not stacked: from main. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: File: atomic, flushed saves that respect read-only files, links and permissions
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. This is data-loss-on-crash hardening for File › Save and AutoRecover. The branch is fresh from main. No other open PR touches `write_file` or `recovery::save`: #644 touches only `recovery::list` and `open`, and its `settings.rs` writes UI settings, not presentations.

## Summary
- **New `fsx::write_atomic`, used by every save to a path and by AutoRecover:**
  - Writes a temporary sibling, runs `sync_all` on it, renames it over the target, then syncs the folder (best effort).
  - Before, nothing was flushed: a power cut after the rename could leave the new name pointing at empty data.
  - A failed write now removes its temporary file. Before, `x.deckcraft.saving` was left behind.
- **Behaviour changes:**
  - **Read-only file:** refused with "the file is read-only; save a copy under another name", as PowerPoint does. Before, the rename silently replaced it.
  - **Symbolic link:** the save writes to the file the link points at, so the link stays a link. Before, it was replaced by a regular file.
  - **Permissions:** the new file keeps the old file's mode. Before, a private 0600 deck came back 0644.
  - **Error messages:** they say what happened (disk full, permission denied, the folder no longer exists, not a file) and that the file on disk was left as it was. The presentation stays unsaved and keeps its AutoRecover entry.
- **AutoRecover:**
  - The metadata file is written atomically too.
  - One presentation failing to write is logged and no longer stops the others. An error is returned only when nothing could be written.

## Test plan
- [x] `fsx::tests::replaces_the_file_keeping_its_permissions` (0600 stays 0600, no temporary file left)
- [x] `fsx::tests::a_read_only_file_is_refused_and_left_alone`

title: Merge Shapes: text merges as its letters, so a picture can fill them
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Closes #653

**Bug:** Merge Shapes between text and a picture left the letters unchanged and made the picture vanish. A text box counted as its whole rectangle, so the result was a box-shaped piece, and it kept the text box's formatting (no fill).

**Change** (`engine/src/cmd/merge.rs`, plus `render::text_outline`):
- **Text as letters:** a text box with no fill and no outline merges as its letters' outlines, laid out exactly as drawn (autofit, rotation, fake italic included), as in PowerPoint. A shape with a fill or outline still merges as its geometry.
- **Picture first:** the result is a picture cut to the letters. The crop is recomputed for the new box, so the picture stays where it was on the slide instead of stretching into the letters' bounds. This applies to upright, unflipped, stretched pictures; others keep their crop.
- **Text first:** the result is a shape filled with the text's colour, with no outline.
- **No text kept:** once letters became outlines, no piece keeps the text.

**Tests** (engine merge tests):
- `a_picture_intersected_with_text_fills_the_letters`: the result is one picture, without text, whose outline is the letters' area (within 5 %) inside the text box, and the picture is still in its original 400 × 200 place. Confirmed failing on main: the result was a box-sized piece, 8640 pt² against the letters' 76 pt².
- `text_merged_first_becomes_shapes_in_its_colour`.

I also rendered the merged slide to PNG and checked it: the letters show the picture.

Not stacked: from main. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Export: image exports keep the whole slide; partial failures say what was written
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. I reviewed the export and settings writers for atomicity and error handling, following up on #677. The branch is fresh from main. It doesn't need #677's write routine, so it isn't stacked on it.

## What the review found
- **PPTX save-as, PDF, PNG/JPEG and outline export:** all go through `cmd::file::write_file`, the same path as File › Save. #677 makes that path atomic and flushed, with read-only, link and permission handling. Nothing else is needed for those formats.
- **ODP export:** not on main yet; it's w3's #568, #576 and #581. Skipped.
- **Settings and recent files (`ui.json`, `prefs.json`):** main writes them with a plain `fs::write`. #644 already replaces that with a temp-file-then-rename write. Not repeated here.
- **Desktop `Services.write`:** a plain `fs::write`, but only the control protocol's screenshot and render-to-path use it, not user-facing saves. Left as is.

## Fixed here (real bugs)
- **Cropped exports:** `deckcraft_render` caps a picture at `MAX_SIDE` (16,000 px) by clipping the output size, not by lowering the scale. An image export whose slide × scale passed that limit, such as 4× of a 4032 pt slide, came out silently cropped to its top-left corner. `file.export` and `file.render` now go through `cmd::file::image_scale`, which keeps the scale within 0.01–16 (NaN becomes 1) and lowers it until the slide fits.
- **Partial exports:** exporting every slide as images stopped at the first file it couldn't write and gave no sign that earlier files existed. The error now says which slides were already written. Slide numbers are also checked before anything is written.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests::a_failed_all_slides_export_says_what_was_written`: the second output path is a folder; the first PNG is on disk and named in the error

title: Video: slides of any shape are drawn whole, letterboxed
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Stacked on #629, the tip of the video chain #608 → #616 → #622 → #628 → #629. The only new commit here is the last one. No issue: I checked this after #681's follow-up note.

## Summary
- **The bug:** video frames are limited to 1:10–10:1 and 8192 px wide, but Design › Slide Size allows 1:56. `render_opts` scaled the slide to the frame *height* alone, so:
  - **Very wide slides** were cropped: a 4032×72 pt slide rendered 56 frame-heights wide (clipped again at the renderer's 16,000 px), and `fit` copied only the left part into the frame.
  - **Very short slides** came out too small: the scale was capped at 16×, so the slide rendered smaller than the frame and sat in its top-left corner.
- **The fix:**
  - `render_opts` takes the frame size and scales the slide so all of it fits.
  - `fit` centres the picture, with black bars where the slide's shape differs from the frame's.
  - Normal shapes, where the frame follows the slide, render as before.

## Test plan
- [x] `video::tests::extreme_slide_shapes_are_letterboxed_whole`: 4032×72 and 72×4032 slides; both ends of the long side are in the frame, with bars on the other axis. With the fix reverted, it fails on "bars above and below" (the slide filled and overflowed the frame).
- [x] The existing `video::tests` still pass, including the frame-size and MP4 decode tests.

title: Media: damaged audio no longer hangs or panics
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by mutation fuzzing the media fixtures (embedded media in a deck goes through these paths).

- **Hang:** `decode_symphonia` retried on every demux `DecodeError`; damaged MP4/M4A files make symphonia's isomp4 demuxer return the same error forever, so decoding spun indefinitely (>120 s, never ending). It now gives up after 64 demux errors in a row.
- **Panic:** symphonia's Matroska reader panics on damaged files (`ebml.rs:343` "EBML header must be read before calling this function", `ebml.rs:317` position `assert_eq!`; both fire in release builds). Calls into symphonia (audio decode for Ogg/Matroska/other containers, and the probe) now run under `catch_unwind`, turning such panics into a corrupt-file error. Player threads are outside the engine's command guard, so this would otherwise end the app.

Test: `damaged_media_neither_panics_nor_hangs` with four fuzzed fixtures (CC0, derived from the existing ones; ATTRIBUTION.md updated). It fails on main and passes here. cargo xtask ci green.

Overlap: #498 rewrites the body of `decode_symphonia`; this PR only adds the error counter to its demux loop and wraps call sites, so a conflict should be small.

title: Media: damaged MP4 sample tables no longer abort the app
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found by mutation fuzzing the media fixtures. Symphonia 0.5.5's MP4 reader runs `Vec::with_capacity(entry_count)` on `stsc`/`stts`/`stsz`/`stco`/`co64` counts and reads each sample whole at its `stsz` size, with no check against the file. One flipped byte in an embedded `.m4a`/`.mp4` asks for 4 to 64 GB, and the process **aborts** (an allocation failure can't be caught, so the engine's panic guard doesn't help).

New `mp4guard::tables_fit` walks the box tree before audio decode/probe hand an MP4 to symphonia. Every box must fit inside its parent, every table's entries must fit inside its box, and every sample size must fit inside the file. Otherwise the file is `MediaError::Corrupt`. Valid fixtures still decode.

Test: `mp4_sample_tables_that_overrun_the_file_are_corrupt` with two fuzzed fixtures (CC0, from `tone.m4a`; ATTRIBUTION.md updated). It aborts with SIGABRT on main and passes here. cargo xtask ci green.

Not covered: symphonia does the same in other formats (FLAC picture lengths `symphonia-metadata flac.rs:53`, which the fuzzer hit at 1.7 GB; Vorbis comment lengths; Matroska block sizes; CAF packet tables). Moving to symphonia 0.6.x, or adding guards per container, would be follow-ups. Separate from #696 (decode-loop hang and symphonia panics). Both touch `audio::decode`, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.

title: PPTX: normalize literal line ends in XML so runs stay put on save
author: NikitkaRa
body:
Found with the PPTX → open → save .pptx → reopen model diff. In owasp.pptx one paragraph went from 14 runs to 19 because its `a:t` text holds a literal CR LF.

- **xml.rs:** text and CDATA now apply XML 1.0 §2.11 end-of-line handling, so a literal CR LF or a lone CR reads as LF. A `` character reference still reads as CR, as the spec says. Before this, the `\r` was kept in run text. On save it stayed in the text and the following LF was written as an extra `a:br`.
- **read/dml.rs:** a line feed inside run text is now read as a line break, the same as a vertical tab already was. That matches how text layout treats `\n` and how export writes it (`a:br`), so the model is the same before and after a save.
- **Tests:** `xml::tests::literal_cr_lf_and_lone_cr_read_as_lf_but_char_ref_stays` and `literal_line_ends_in_run_text_read_as_breaks_and_survive_save` in crates/pptx/tests/roundtrip.rs. The second one patches a raw `one\r\n   two\rthree` into a slide and checks the runs after import and after a further save and reopen. Both fail on main and pass with this change.
- Attribute value normalization (§3.3.3) is not changed here.

`cargo xtask ci` passes. No open issue or PR covers this, so there is no Closes line.

title: Undo: cap the history by memory as well as by steps
author: NikitkaRa
body:
No issue. This is a huge-deck robustness follow-up from the #695 investigation. The branch is fresh from main. No open PR touches `push_undo`, `History` or the undo limit.

## Summary
- **The problem:** undo kept up to 500 steps (`prefs.undo_limit`) regardless of their size. Steps share every slide, master and media item an edit didn't touch, so most cost little. But a deck-wide edit, such as resizing slides (which rescales every shape) or theme or master changes, keeps a copy of every slide. 500 of those on a 2000-slide deck could keep hundreds of full copies alive.
- **Cost estimate:** `push_undo` now estimates each step's cost when it is pushed. `undo_cost` counts the slides, masters and media data the step holds that the document after it doesn't share (by `Arc` pointer), using a structural size estimate per shape and the exact byte length for media.
- **The cap:** the oldest steps are dropped while the total passes `History::byte_limit`. The default is `UNDO_BYTE_BUDGET`, 256 MiB, used when the limit is 0. The newest step always stays, however big. The step-count limit still applies.
- **Cost map:** costs are kept in `History::costs`, keyed by the step's document pointer, and pruned as steps go.
- **Known approximation:** steps that undo or redo move between the stacks have no recorded cost, so they count as 0. The budget therefore under-counts and never drops steps early.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests::undo_history_is_capped_by_memory_as_well_as_steps`, written first and failing on main (30 of 30 deck-wide steps kept). Now:
  - 30 slide resizes on a 41-slide deck with a 10-copy budget keep 5–11 steps, and undo still works.
  - 120 small edits under the same budget keep all 120 steps.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.

Parity checklist: no new rows. PowerPoint also limits undo, by a step count.

title: PPTX: write Color Pulse emphasis as a colour change, not a scale

The default colour is the same dark red the player uses.

title: Add Simplified Chinese interface localization and disable unsupported languages
author: noorllpori
body:
DeckCraft's language controls previously appeared actionable without changing the interface. This adds an English/Simplified Chinese interface setting that applies immediately and is saved in desktop UI preferences. Unsupported interface languages and unimplemented text-language choices are disabled, with a link from the proofing dialog to interface preferences.

The Simplified Chinese catalog contains 1,655 entries and covers ribbon tools, shapes/transitions/animations/chart/table galleries, File and print/export pages, task panes, dialogs, context menus, command palette labels, slideshow/presenter controls, contributor views, native file-picker titles/filters, and common notices. Editor placeholder prompts are supplied through a renderer callback, and the canvas cache includes the interface language. Presentation contents, custom prompts, stored command/tab IDs, and API responses retain their existing semantics. Unrecognized strings and third-party diagnostic details fall back to English.

On Windows, the interface prefers the user's installed DengXian/等线 face, with the existing fallback chain when unavailable. No font asset is bundled, downloaded, or installed. The application remains named DeckCraft; the private installer, installer scripts, and local review artifacts are excluded from this PR.

title: Show: Presenter View only with a second display (fixes slide-show lag/freeze on one monitor)
author: melandur
body:
## Problem

Presenter View is on by default (`UiState::presenter_view: true`), and the slide show opens it whenever the setting is on, even with a single display. The presenter window then opens on the same screen as the full-screen show, so one of the two windows always ends up hidden behind the other.

All viewports are drawn on the same thread. The presenter window is an immediate viewport, drawn in the same frame as the show. A hidden window gets no frame callbacks from the compositor, so presenting to it blocks, and the whole app stalls with it: the show lags, key presses are lost, or the app freezes.

Which window ends up hidden depends on the window manager. On Hyprland with focus-follows-mouse (`input:follow_mouse = 1`, `misc:on_focus_under_fullscreen = 1`), the window under the pointer takes over full screen. So starting the show from **Play from Start** (top left) or from **Present** (top right) gave different results. Sometimes the Presenter View window took full screen and the show was hidden behind it.

## Repro

Linux, one monitor, Hyprland, Presenter View on (the default), a 35-slide deck. Start the show with **Present** and press → a few times.

Measured through the control server (`ui.key ArrowRight`, then poll `ui.inspect` until the slide changes):

| | Windows after start | Next-slide presses |
|---|---|---|
| Presenter View off | show (full screen) | 5 of 5, 19–43 ms each |
| Presenter View on, before | show + Presenter View | 3 of 5 went through; in another run the app stopped answering for >20 s |
| Presenter View on, after | show (full screen) | 6 of 6, 13–70 ms each |

## Fix

Like PowerPoint, Presenter View is used only when a second display is connected; with one display the show shows only the slides.

- `Services::displays`: a new optional host hook that returns the number of connected displays, or `None` when the host can't tell.
- `SlideApp::start_show` asks for Presenter View only when the setting is on **and** there is a second displa…

body:

title: CLI: convert and run refuse output formats DeckCraft can't write (#715)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #715

`deckcraft-cli convert IN OUT` chose the format with `format_for_path`, which falls back to native `.deckcraft` for any extension it doesn't recognise, so `out.odp`, `out.gif`, `out.svg` and `out.outline` were written as `.deckcraft` zips with exit status 0. `run --save` / `run --export` had the same problem.

## Change

- `deckcraft_engine::cmd::file::writable_format_for_path` (plus `WRITABLE_EXTENSIONS`): the format for a path, or `None` when its extension isn't one DeckCraft writes (`.deckcraft`, `.pptx/.potx/.ppsx`, `.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg/.jpeg`, `.txt/.md`).
- The CLI checks `convert`'s OUT and `run`'s `--save`/`--export` paths with it before opening or running anything, and fails without writing:

```
deckcraft-cli: out.odp: unsupported output format .odp (supported: .deckcraft, .pptx, .potx, .ppsx, .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .txt, .md)
```

The engine's `file.saveAs` / `file.export` keep their current fallback (the app's own save dialogs always give a known extension); only the CLI entry points are stricter. `.potx`/`.ppsx` content types (#210) are out of scope.

## Tests

- `apps/deckcraft-cli/tests/convert.rs` (new): convert to `.odp`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.outline` and an extension-less path fails, names the format and writes nothing; `.deckcraft` and `.txt` still convert; `run --save/--export deck.odp` fails before running. Both tests fail on `main`.
- Engine unit test for `writable_format_for_path`.
- `cargo xtask ci` steps fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `test --workspace`, assets and layers pass locally. The wasm step was not run: Gentoo's Rust ships no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` std. CI covers it.

title: PPTX: keep custom XML and custom document property parts on save
author: lhymes
body:
Opening a deck and saving it dropped `customXml/item*.xml` (with its `itemProps*.xml`) and `docProps/custom.xml`, because the reader skips parts the model has no place for. Those parts hold document-management metadata and custom document properties, so a plain open and save lost data the user never touched.

`Presentation` gains `kept_parts: Vec<KeptPart>`. The reader collects the custom-properties part reached from the package root, and each `customXml` part reached from the presentation together with its `customXmlProps` part. The writer emits them byte for byte with their content types and re-creates the relationships (root, presentation, and the per-item rels file). Other unknown parts are still skipped; this only widens the carried set to these two relationship kinds.

Found while round-tripping real-world files.

Test: `crates/pptx/tests/kept_parts.rs` builds a deck in code, adds the three parts and their relationships to the package, imports, exports, and checks the bytes, relationships and content types, and that a second round trip is stable.

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `deckcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon alsa-lib vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: deckcraft`;
  - `conflicts: deckcraft, deckcraft-bin, deckcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.deckcraft`, not `deckcraft`.** The AUR already has `deckcraft`, `deckcraft-bin` and `deckcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.6.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `deckcraft-0.6.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: GhostMitra
body:
## Description

Adds an opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (such as Nextcloud apps or other web containers) that frame DeckCraft web in an \<iframe>\, matching the clean-room convention established across craft sibling apps (\gridcraft\, \photocraft\, \pdfcraft\, \wordcraft\).

### Details
- **Opt-in activation**: When loaded with URL flag \?host=parent\, the web shell activates the bridge in \pps/deckcraft-web/src/host.rs\.
- **Same-origin security**: Only messages originating from the same origin as the app and sent from the immediate parent window (\window.parent\) are accepted and answered.
- **Protocol**:
  - \deckcraft:ready\ (to parent): sent when the app is initialized and ready to receive documents, carrying \{ version }\.
  - \deckcraft:open\ (from parent): accepts \{ name, bytes }\ (where \ ytes\ is an \ArrayBuffer\ or \Uint8Array\) and feeds the file through the inbox to open directly.
  - \deckcraft:save\ (to parent): intercepts saves and exports, transferring an \ArrayBuffer\ with \{ name, bytes }\ to the parent window for persistence.
  - \deckcraft:dirty\ (to parent): notifies the parent with \{ dirty }\ whenever unsaved document state changes.
  - \deckcraft:failed\ (to parent): notifies the parent with \{ error }\ if app startup fails.
- **Author parameter**: \&author=\ URL query parameter sets the user name for comments in host environments.
- **Workflow ergonomics**: In host mode, the initial sample deck is bypassed so the presentation loaded by the parent opens cleanly without intermediate UI noise. Leaving-page guard is deferred to the parent host.

### Quality gates
- Passed all quality gates locally (\cargo fmt\, \cargo clippy\, \cargo test\, \xtask assets\, \xtask layers\, wasm check).

title: Slide: a new slide's body goes into the layout's content placeholder
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #725

`slide.new` (MCP `add_slide`) put `body` into the first non-title placeholder in shape order. A layout with a small body placeholder ahead of its content placeholder (Keynote's "Title & Bullets": `type="body" sz="quarter" idx="21"` before `idx="1"`) got the body in the small box, and the content placeholder stayed empty.

The body now goes to the layout's main content placeholder, chosen by:

1. `idx="1"` (the content slot PowerPoint fills) first,
2. then a full-size placeholder over a `half`/`quarter` one,
3. then a text placeholder (body/obj/subTitle) over a picture/chart/table one,

with ties kept in shape order, so a layout with a single body placeholder behaves as before (title slides still put `body` in the subtitle, Two Content still uses the left box).

## Tests

- New `new_slide_body_goes_to_the_content_placeholder` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: Title and Content with an extra quarter-size body placeholder (`idx` 21) inserted before and after the content placeholder; the body must land in `idx` 1 and leave `idx` 21 empty. It fails on `main` (the "before" case) and passes with the fix.
- Checked end to end with the issue's python-pptx templates: `deckcraft-cli run --in tpl-before.pptx --cmd 'slide.new={"layout":"Title and Content","title":"T","body":"Line one\nLine two"}' --cmd 'slide.inspect={}'` now puts the body in `Content Placeholder 2` for both `tpl-before.pptx` and `tpl-after.pptx`.

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

DeckCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`, `alsa-lib`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

DeckCraft 0.6.1's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `deckcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.6.1 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `deckcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: Slide show: a first animation set After/With Previous plays when the slide appears (#631)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #631.

**What was wrong.** Entering a slide whose first step begins With/After Previous marked that step as playing (`enter` sets `playing = true` when `step_is_auto(0)`), and then the entry kick in `after_enter` advanced the state a second time — and `next()` on a playing state runs `step_done`, completing the step. The fade was over before its first frame: the slide appeared fully built, and the step clock (`Show.step_start`) had never been started. Exactly the reporter's table: After/With Previous shows the shape fully drawn at every sample; On Click fades correctly.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/show.rs`, `after_enter`): when the state already plays the auto first step, start the step's clock (`step_start = now`) instead of advancing. Two guard changes fall out of the entry matrix:

- advancing remains only for the play-all preview over a first step that waits for a click (`autoplay` + fresh step 0 + steps exist) — its `next()` can then only return `PlayStep`, so no action is dropped;
- Transition Preview still completes the entrance unseen (explicit `step_done` + early return, the old accidental behaviour now stated), so previews don't start waiting on entrance animations;
- back-navigation (lands on a slide fully built, `step == steps`) and "Show without animation" (no steps) stay put instead of being bounced forward by a stale advance — both mis-advances existed on main and are closed by the same gate.

**Tests:** kittest — a fade set After Previous (3 s) on the first shape, show started, five frames in: the step is still 0 and playing with both clocks set in the same frame. Fails on the old logic (`step` jumps to 1, `playing` false). The anim crate's own state machine is unchanged.

**Fidelity note, not addressed here:** PowerPoint starts a first After-Previous effect after the slide transition completes; ours starts it at entry, under the transition — consistent with the issue's intent ("plays as soon as the slide appears"). Worth a look during tr…

title: Fonts: falling back to the default face no longer deadlocks
author: xmaks82
body:
`FontDb::cascade` can hang the calling thread, and with it every thread that later loads a font.

The last fallback arm searched the loaded faces and, finding none that draws the cluster, called `first` while the search's `read_faces()` guard was still alive (a temporary in the match arm lives to the end of the `let f = match …;`). `first` looks up the default family. On a database where that family hasn't been looked up yet, `try_family` → `load_cataloged` → `add_fonts` takes `faces.write()`, even when there are no files to add. The thread waits on itself while holding `loading` and `loaded_families`, and every other lookup then queues behind it.

It depends on which caller reaches that path first, so it showed as a flaky hang. `cargo test -p deckcraft-text` at current main (2f6629c) hung in 4 of 10 parallel runs here. A stack dump of a hung run: one thread in `cascade → face → try_family → load_cataloged → load_family → add_fonts` waiting on the faces' write lock, the other test threads in `system_fallback` / `try_family` waiting on the loading mutexes. Single-threaded runs always pass.

The fix finishes the search before `first` runs. New test `falling_back_to_the_default_face_does_not_deadlock` takes that path on a fresh `FontDb` with system fallback off, in a thread with a 30 s timeout. It fails with a timeout on main and passes with the fix. With the fix: deckcraft-text 0 hangs in 15 parallel runs; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --release --workspace` passes. `cargo fmt --check` currently fails on main itself, in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (the `browsetheme_tests` module order), not in this change.

title: File › Settings › AI: bring your own model (any OpenAI-compatible server) and Draft slides from a prompt (#732)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
Hi again! This one answers #732 (bring your own AI model). Like my earlier PRs it's an experiment more than a finished proposal: take the whole thing, take only the parts you like, or close it. No hard feelings either way.

**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The code, the tests and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). I described what I wanted, made the design decisions and looked at the tab myself on Windows 11. **It has not been tested with a real AI model at all** (see Testing).

**It builds on #534 (File › Settings).** The AI tab lives on the Settings page that #534 adds, so this branch contains #534's commits. Please look at #534 first. The 2 commits on top are what this PR adds. Once #534 is merged (or changed), I'll rebase this so only those 2 commits are left.

## What it does

File › Settings gets an **AI** tab, between Keyboard Shortcuts and Backup and Reset:

- **Server:** Ollama, LM Studio and OpenAI buttons fill in the address and a starting model. Any other server that speaks the OpenAI chat completions API works too (LocalAI, vLLM, a company proxy…): type its address.
- **Address, Model, API key:** the key box is a password field. No key is needed for a model running on your own computer.
- **Test connection:** sends a tiny request and says whether the server, key and model answered.
- **Draft slides:** describe a talk ("Five slides introducing the solar system to a school class") and the model writes a Markdown outline. DeckCraft builds it with the existing `slide.fromOutline` command, after the current slide. They're ordinary slides, and one Undo takes them all away.

Ollama on this computer is the default, so out of the box nothing leaves your machine.

## How it's built

title: Centre anchorCtr text on zero-width boxes instead of running off slide
author: Silvertree2010
body:

## Cause
A box with zero width was still laid out as wrapping text, so each word or letter broke onto its own line. When anchorCtr text was wider than the box, the centring offset was clamped to zero, so the line started at the box edge and ran past the slide.

## Fix
Text in a zero-width box is now laid out on one line per paragraph. When anchorCtr text is wider than its box, the layout is redone on a rect grown symmetrically around the box, so the block is centred and lines align within it.
