title: Fix add overflow panic in table.columnWidth for a huge column index
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:540 (column_width)` (no existing issue): table.columnWidth panics (add overflow) when `col` is a huge index.

## Cause
`column_width` computed the right-neighbour column with a plain `c + 1`. With `col` = usize::MAX this overflows, which panics in debug builds and is reported as an Internal error. In release builds it wraps to 0.

## Fix
Both uses of `c + 1` in `column_width` (the `get` and the `get_mut` in the keepTotal branch) now use `c.saturating_add(1)`, as the insert commands already do. A huge column index finds no column, so the command succeeds and changes nothing.

## Verified
- Regression test `table_column_width_of_a_huge_column_is_ignored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p deckcraft-engine --lib table_column_width_of_a_huge_column_is_ignored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests::east_asian_vertical_text_stands_ideographs_upright`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The other table commands and the insert variants, which already saturate. A huge `col` is still ignored with Ok and not turned into a bad-params error.

title: Text: links take the hyperlink colour over the run's colour, unless ahyp:hlinkClr keeps it
author: xmaks82
body:
`resolve::run` kept a colour set on a hyperlinked run. The comment above it says PowerPoint 2019 and later honour that colour. I measured this on Windows and both versions draw such a run in the theme's hyperlink colour instead.

**Measured.** One slide with four runs, saved as PDF by PowerPoint through COM:

| run | PowerPoint 2016 (16.0.16327) | Microsoft 365 (16.0.17932) | `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `solidFill FF0000` + `hlinkClick` | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue | red |
| `solidFill FF0000` + `hlinkClick` with `ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` | red | red | red |
| no fill + `hlinkClick` | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue | hyperlink blue |
| `solidFill FF0000`, no link | red | red | red |

`ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` (`{A12FA001-AC4F-418D-AE19-62706E023703}`) is the extension PowerPoint writes when a user gives a link a colour of their own. Files without it, such as Google Slides exports, which put `srgbClr 000000` on every link run, open in PowerPoint with blue links. `main` showed them black.

**Change**
- `RunProps::link_keeps_color` is read from `a:hlinkClick/a:extLst/…/ahyp:hlinkClr val="tx"` and written back. Inside `hlinkClick` it goes after `a:snd`, in schema order.
- `resolve::run` paints a link in `hlink` unless the run (or the `defRPr` that carries the link) keeps its colour. In that case the inherited text colour applies, which is what `tx` means. Underline handling is unchanged.
- Tests: `hyperlinks_draw_in_the_hyperlink_colour_underlined` and `hyperlinked_runs_take_the_theme_hyperlink_look` now pin the measured rule, and `a_link_that_keeps_its_text_colour_survives_a_round_trip` is new.

**Checked**
- 31 real decks compared slide by slide with PDFs from PowerPoint 2016: 8 slides closer, none worse.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: Text: a word doesn't break after ?, !, } or + (URLs wrap as in PowerPoint)
author: xmaks82
body:
`break_opportunities` follows Unicode line breaking, which allows a break after `?`, `!`, `}` and `+` inside a word. A long URL therefore broke after its `?` and after each `+` of the query, and the rest of the line stayed empty. PowerPoint fills the line instead.

**Measured in PowerPoint 2016 for Windows** (16.0.16327, `latinLnBrk` off, which is its default). Text boxes held words joined by each of `? ! ) ] } ; : , » / . _ % = & + -`, plus a Yandex search URL, and were saved as PDF through COM. None of `?`, `!`, `}` or `+` is a break opportunity inside a word: the word fills the line and breaks where it no longer fits, as `main` already does after `/` and `\`. The other characters already matched.

| Yandex search URL in a 3-inch box, Arial 14 | first line |
|---|---|
| PowerPoint | `https://yandex.ru/search/?text=%` |
| `main` | `https://yandex.ru/search/?` |
| this branch | `https://yandex.ru/search/?text=%` |

On the synthetic slide every line now matches PowerPoint's PDF, where `main` differed on 9 lines. Across 31 real decks compared with PowerPoint PDFs, the slide of search links gets closer by 1.5 and one slide moves by 0.1 of rasterization noise; that slide's text lines are identical to PowerPoint's.

`a_word_does_not_break_after_a_slash_or_backslash` now also covers `?`, `!`, `}` and `+`. The `deckcraft-text` tests pass and clippy is clean.

Open question, left alone here: PowerPoint seems to allow a break *before* `)` and `}` inside a word, while this PR only removes the breaks *after* them. I can probe that separately if useful.

title: Header & Footer: the automatic date takes a format
author: Hamza0101
body:
Header & Footer's automatic date was always the short date, with no way to choose a format — and a `dateFormat` parameter was accepted and silently dropped.

## What was wrong

`HeaderFooter::date_format` exists in the model, documented as "`datetime1`…`datetime13` format for automatic dates". Nothing ever read it, wrote it or set it: `grep` finds exactly one hit, the field's own declaration. The placeholder was hardcoded:

```rust
PhType::Date if hf.date_text.is_empty() => TextBody {
    ... kind: RunKind::Field { field: "datetime1".into() } ...
```

Measured on `main` @ 1dc6972:

```
design.headerFooter {date: true, dateText: ""}                      -> "10/17/2026"  datetime1
design.headerFooter {date: true, dateFormat: "datetime5"}           -> "10/17/2026"  datetime1
                                                                       hf.date_format stayed ""
```

The second line is the worse half: the command returned `Ok`, so a caller had no way to tell the format had been ignored.

Everything else was already in place — `datetime::field_text` renders all thirteen types, and Insert ▸ Date & Time already offers them. Only the wiring from a choice to the placeholder was missing.

## The change

- `design.headerFooter` takes `dateFormat`, **refuses** anything outside the thirteen types rather than ignoring it, and stores it.
- A Date placeholder is created with that field type and its saved text.
- An existing Date placeholder follows a format that changed, the same way it already followed a changed `dateText`.
- `datetime::DATE_KINDS` is the canonical list, and `dialogs.rs` now uses it instead of keeping a second copy of the same thirteen strings.
- The Header & Footer dialog gains a **Format** dropdown, listing each type by what it would show right now (the same samples as Insert ▸ Date & Time), enabled while the date is automatic — a fixed date is the text as typed, so a format would mean nothing there.

title: Export: PDFs store each slide backdrop once (#845)
author: FabPei
body:
Opening this 438-slide deck as a PDF produced a 226 MB file where LibreOffice writes 4 MB (#845). Every slide repeats the same background design — the master and layout graphics, a water-texture frame in this deck — but the export rasterized each slide as one full-page bitmap at print resolution and embedded that bitmap per page, so the repeated artwork was stored once per slide instead of once.

The export now draws each slide as two rasters: the backdrop (background fill with the master and layout graphics) and the slide's own shapes over it. `deckcraft_render::render_slide_part` already splits the two this way for slide transitions, and the split is exact — the full renderer composes the same two passes. Equal backdrops become equal images, and the writer stores each one once through its content-addressed image cache, so a deck's shared design now costs one raster however many slides use it. The slide's own shapes keep their transparency: the renderer's premultiplied pixels are converted to straight RGBA for the PDF's colour channel and alpha mask.

What changed:
- `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` — `Exporter::slide` renders `SlidePart::Backdrop` and `SlidePart::Content` and draws them as two images; new `backdrop` (composite onto white) and `straight` (premultiplied to straight RGBA) helpers.
- `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs` — new regression test.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#845

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The regression test `slides_share_one_backdrop_raster_and_keep_their_pixels` exports slides with different text and asserts the PDF has one backdrop object drawn by every page, that the stored backdrop is byte-for-byte what the renderer draws, and that a slide's content raster keeps straight RGBA plus its alpha mask — without this change the pages store full-page rasters that share nothing. title: Theme: light-mode controls stand out on dialogs (#826)
author: FabPei
body:
The Preferences checkbox and the Interface size slider were invisible in light mode (#826): their fills come from the `field_bg` token, which was pure white, on a dialog that is also white and draws no border around its controls — white-on-white. The dark theme already used a `field_bg` slightly off its card colour, which is why only light mode looked broken. The reporter's suggested fix is exactly this: make the background colour of those controls darker.

What changed:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` — light `field_bg` is `0xE3E3E3` (the palette's card-border grey) instead of white, so checkbox fills, slider troughs and field backgrounds stand out on the white card and the chrome.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` — new regression test `field_backgrounds_stand_out_on_dialogs` checks the effective egui visuals after `apply`: control fills must differ from the dialog background by a visible margin in both themes.

Note on the ticket title: the relay title says "text appears black in dark mode in some menus", which we could not reproduce — deterministic pixel sampling of the dark-mode Preferences dialog found no black text (175,000 samples, minimum luminance equal to the dialog background). The reporter's body describes the light-mode control backgrounds, and that is what this fixes.

Fixes storytold/deckcraft#826

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering, assets, wasm). The regression test `field_backgrounds_stand_out_on_dialogs` is proven red-green (it fails on white-on-white before this change). Verified in the running app: the light-mode Preferences dialog now shows the checkbox and slider clearly against the dialog.

title: Format: Asian typography paragraph options (禁則処理・句読点のぶら下げ) in the dialog and as commands
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

DeckCraft already modelled, read, wrote and (for two of them) honoured PowerPoint's East Asian paragraph properties — `a:pPr/@eaLnBrk`, `@hangingPunct`, `@latinLnBrk` — but **nothing could set them**: no command, no UI. A Japanese user could not turn 禁則処理 or 句読点のぶら下げ on or off, which PowerPoint exposes in Paragraph ▸ アジア言語の文字体裁.

- **Commands** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`), each `{"on"?: bool}` toggling the selected paragraphs' property and `enabled` like the other paragraph commands:

| id | label | property |
|---|---|---|
| `format.eastAsianLineBreak` | East Asian Line Breaking (禁則処理) | `east_asian_line_break` → `@eaLnBrk` |
| `format.hangingPunctuation` | Hang Punctuation (句読点のぶら下げ) | `hanging_punct` → `@hangingPunct` |
| `format.latinLineBreak` | Allow Latin Text to Wrap Mid-word (英単語の途中で改行を許可) | `latin_line_break` → `@latinLnBrk` |

- **Paragraph dialog**: a bold **Asian Typography** section with the three checkboxes, applied with the dialog's other paragraph edits in one *Paragraph…* undo step; `format.paragraphDialog` takes `eastAsianLineBreak?`, `hangingPunctuation?`, `latinLineBreak?` (a present non-bool is rejected without editing; absent leaves the property alone).
- **The line breaker now honours `eaLnBrk`**: Unicode's line-break data offers no break before a small kana or the prolonged sound mark at all, so relaxing 禁則 means *adding* that opportunity, not keeping one — with the property off, a line may start with one (Word's 禁則処理なし). Absent still means on (PowerPoint's default), so the default layout is unchanged, and closing brackets and closing punctuation keep following the Unicode rule (they are protected by the Unicode classes, not by a deckcraft list — a follow-up if the maintainer wants them relaxed too).
- `latin_line_break` and `hanging_punct` were already honoured by the line breaker and are unchanged.

title: Dark appearance: follow the system setting (#41)
author: JeremyYao
body:
Fixes #41.

## Problem

DeckCraft never read the operating system's appearance. On Windows 11 with dark mode on, it still opened light, because `UiState.brightness` defaulted to Light and nothing compared it with the system. Preferences ▸ Dark appearance was a checkbox, so it couldn't say "follow the system" either.

## What this changes

**Preferences ▸ General ▸ Dark appearance** is now a dropdown with three choices:

| Choice | Appearance |
|---|---|
| **Use system setting** (default) | Dark while the system is dark, light while it is light. Follows changes made while DeckCraft runs, including macOS Auto. |
| **On** | Always dark |
| **Off** | Always light |

- **File ▸ Account ▸ Appearance** shows the same dropdown. It replaces the Light/Dark one that was there.
- When the system's setting can't be read, Use system setting falls back to **light**.
- The View ribbon's **Dark Mode** button and the title-bar **Light/Dark appearance** toggle are still one-click switches. They now switch to whichever of On or Off isn't showing. They don't offer the three-way choice that #41's first acceptance criterion asks for, because a dropdown didn't fit a one-click button. That is easy to add if you want it.
- **Command:** `view.dark` takes `{mode: "system"|"on"|"off"}` or `{on: bool}`, and toggles when given neither.
- **Saved state:** `darkMode` in `ui.json`. An older file with `"brightness": "dark"` loads as On. One with `"brightness": "light"`, which was the default before, loads as Use system setting, because a saved light value doesn't show whether the user picked it. #41 lists the default as a maintainer decision; this PR makes it Use system setting, as requested by the person filing this change.
- egui's style is now pinned to the appearance DeckCraft picks, through `ctx.set_theme`. Before, egui switched to its own unstyled light or dark style whenever the system theme changed. That also gives the native title bar the matching appearance.

title: Close the control port on the first line that isn't a request
author: skylartaylor
body:
# Close the control port on the first line that isn't a request

The control port closes the connection on the first line that isn't a request, rather than skipping
bad lines and continuing to read. An HTTP request line or the HTTP/2 preface ends the connection
before anything after it is dispatched.

across every app in this family. I have only opened the pull request, because they were unreachable
and the team was ready to build. Thank you for the work, and for the care taken over the test
coverage in particular.

title: Fonts: the CJK fallback path prefers faces matching the run's bold/italic (#892)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #892.

**What was wrong.** Bold Chinese, Japanese and Korean text was drawn in regular weight when the run's font had no CJK glyphs (Calibri, Aptos, Arial — the usual case). The CJK fallback path (`FontDb::cascade` → `fallback_for`) never received the run's style: the fallback sort always preferred `weight = 400, italic = false`, so a regular CJK face beat a bold one every time.

**The fix** (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs` + `fallback.rs`, ~25 lines): `fallback_for_styled` and `loaded_fallback_styled` sort candidates by `(fallback_family, italic_match, weight_match)` where `italic_match` and `weight_match` compare the face against the requested style's italic and weight (via the existing `style_italic`/`style_weight` helpers). `cascade` passes the run's `style` through to the styled variant. Regular text gets the identical sort as before (`style_weight("Regular")` = 400, `style_italic("Regular")` = false), so non-CJK fallbacks are unchanged.

**Tests:** a fonts-crate test verifying that `fallback_for_styled` returns a face whose weight matches the requested style for a CJK character the default font doesn't cover. Verified visually with the issue's exact python-pptx repro: the bold copies of the Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Cyrillic and Thai lines are all visibly heavier than the regular ones. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Header & Footer: an automatic date's format comes back on import
author: Hamza0101
body:
The read-side half I said I would send separately in #927. **Stacked on #927** — it needs `datetime::DATE_KINDS` from it, so please take that one first; the diff here is the top commit only.

## What was wrong

`header_footer()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs` looked at a Date placeholder and recorded its *text* only when it held no field. It never looked at the field, so an automatic date's format was dropped on import: `date_format` came back empty whatever the deck used.

## Why it is not cosmetic

With #927's Format dropdown, opening a deck whose dates are `datetime5` showed **datetime1** selected, because that is what an empty `date_format` falls back to. Pressing Apply then sent `datetime1` back and reformatted the deck's dates — a silent change to a file the user had only opened to look at. That is the part that moved this from "nice to have" to worth sending.

## The change

The reader remembers which of the thirteen formats the field is, so the dialog opens on the deck's own choice.

- An unknown spelling is deliberately **not** recorded. `datetime` and `datetimeFigureOut` both render as the short date, but the command only accepts the thirteen and would refuse them, so claiming one as "the choice" would make Apply fail. They come back as no choice, exactly as before.
- A **fixed** date still comes back as its text, unchanged.

`crates/pptx` takes a dependency on `crates/text` for `DATE_KINDS` rather than keeping a second copy of the same thirteen strings. pptx is layer 3 and text is layer 2, so that direction is allowed; `cargo xtask layers` passes (28 crates, no violations).

## Tests

`crates/pptx/tests/header_footer_date.rs`, a real round trip through `export` then `import`:

| deck | `date_format` after import | `date_text` |
|---|---|---|
| `dateFormat: datetime5` | `datetime5` | empty |
| `dateFormat: datetime11` | `datetime11` | empty |
| no format asked for | `datetime1` (the placeholder's own field) | empty |
| `dateText: "4 July 1776"` | empty —…

title: Canvas: a shape in front of edited text takes the click (#931)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
Fixes #931.

**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), which reproduced the bug in the desktop app on Windows 11 and checked the fix there too.

## The bug

On a Title and Content slide, put a shape on top of the content placeholder, click the placeholder's edge, then click the shape: the placeholder stays selected and the shape can't be reached until you click somewhere else first.

Clicking an empty placeholder starts editing its text (as in PowerPoint). From then on, `Session::pointer` sent every click inside that text box to `place_caret`, which runs before the hit test, so a shape in front of the text never got the click.

## The fix

`place_caret` (crates/engine/src/tools.rs) now first walks the shapes in front of the one holding the text, topmost first, and leaves the click to the normal hit test when one of them is under the pointer. A click on the text where nothing is in front still moves the caret, and grouped text works the same way (the walk stops at the group that holds the edited shape). 9 lines, no other behaviour changes.

## Testing

- New engine test `a_shape_in_front_of_edited_text_takes_the_click`: the reporter's steps with pointer events. Without the fix it fails (the placeholder stays selected); with it, it passes. It also checks that a click on the text away from the shape keeps editing it.
- Reproduced in the desktop app over the control channel before the fix, and checked after.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress-log line.

title: Media: fuzz the AV1, VP9 and HEVC decoders at the bitstream level, with AV1 film grain clips
author: braiinz94
body:
Found while reviewing test coverage of the hand-written video decoders (no existing issue).

## What was missing

The AV1, VP9 and HEVC decoders read files from strangers, but their crates have few tests for their size (`av1`: 10 tests for ~20k lines) and none fuzz them. `damaged_media_neither_panics_nor_hangs` damages whole files, so most mutations stop in the container and never reach a decoder. AV1 film grain synthesis (`crates/av1/src/grain.rs`) was barely reached (14 % of its lines), because no fixture carries grain.

## What this adds

- **`crates/media/tests/codec_mutation.rs`.** It demuxes the fixture clips the way `video.rs` does, then damages the compressed samples themselves before they reach the decoder: truncate, flip bits, overwrite a run, set a byte, drop, repeat or reorder samples, and sometimes the `av1C` / `hvcC` record. Every mutation must give an error or pictures, never a panic or a hang (10 s per decode). It is seeded and deterministic: `DECKCRAFT_MUTATION_ITERS` (default 200 per clip) runs it longer, `DECKCRAFT_MUTATION_SEED` replays another seed, and a failure prints clip, seed, iteration and mutation.
- **`harness_reports_panics_and_hangs`.** A fuzzer that finds nothing proves nothing until it is seen to catch something, so this checks that the harness reports a panic (with its location) and a hang.
- **`clip-av1-grain-{4,6,15}.mkv`** (2–3 KB each). The same `make.sh` gradient, encoded with libaom's built-in film grain test vectors (`film-grain-test=N`), so they are contributor-original and CC0 like the other clips. `make.sh` regenerates them and `ATTRIBUTION.md` lists them. Measured clip by clip with `cargo-llvm-cov`, these three reach every line of `grain.rs` that all 16 vectors reach.
- **`av1_grain_fixtures_carry_film_grain`.** The sequence header has `film_grain_params_present`, and decoding with `apply_film_grain` changes all 6 pictures of each clip compared with decoding without it.

No `Cargo.toml` change, no new dependency.

title: Thumbnails: navigating slides scrolls the pane to keep the current slide visible (#917)
author: albayazid
body:
Fixes #917.

**What was wrong.** Navigating slides with the arrow keys never scrolled the thumbnail pane: past a screenful of slides, the current slide's thumbnail left the viewport and the pane gave no hint where you were.

**The fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/thumbs.rs`): when the current slide changes, the pane scrolls its thumbnail into view — minimally, and only once it has left the viewport, as in PowerPoint. A thumbnail that is already on screen never moves the pane, so the user's own scrolling stands, and opening a document never scrolls (the first frame only records the slide). `ui.scroll_to_rect(rect, None)` gives exactly that: egui scrolls only when the rect is outside the clip rect. An `Align::Center` would have re-centred the pane — animated — on every keystroke.

`show()` also records the pane's scroll offset in `UiState.thumbs_scroll` (`#[serde(skip)]`, so it is not persisted). This is the same pattern as `slide_rect`/`canvas_scale` and flows into the control channel's `inspect` output automatically, so the pane is observable from end-to-end automation too.

**Tests:** `thumbs::tests::navigating_slides_keeps_the_current_thumbnail_visible` builds a 31-slide deck, jumps to the last slide and asserts the pane scrolled, then steps one slide up — already on screen — and asserts the pane held still. Verified red without the fix (the offset stayed 0).

**Gate:** fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm all green locally. One pre-existing Windows-only failure in the workspace test run (`replacefonts_tests::ribbon_button_opens_the_dialog_and_replaces`) also fails on clean `main` on this machine; Linux CI is unaffected. ROADMAP progress-log row added.

title: Edit Points: turning a shape into a freeform is one undo step
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this bug while break-testing DeckCraft (random command sequences, then Undo all the way back, which should restore the deck exactly), on Windows 11.

## The bug

Right-click a shape (a star, an arrow…) → **Edit Points**, then press Ctrl+Z: the shape stays a freeform. Edit Points turns a preset into custom geometry, but `shape.editPoints` was a `noundo` command, so that conversion never became an undo step, and the first Ctrl+Z took back whatever came *before* it instead (in the test, the insertion of the shape itself).

## The fix

- `shape.editPoints` is an ordinary undoable command now. `Session::execute` only records a step when the document actually changed, so entering Edit Points on a shape that is already a freeform, or leaving Edit Points, still adds nothing; only the conversion is a step ("Edit Points").
- `ToolState::editing_points` only counts a shape that is a freeform, so when Undo turns it back into a preset, Edit Points ends instead of showing a point editor with no points.

## Testing

- New engine test `edit_points_conversion_is_one_undo_step`: convert, leave, Undo (the star is back), Redo (freeform again), Undo while still editing (Edit Points ends), and re-entering on a freeform adds no step. Without the fix it fails: Ctrl+Z removes the inserted shape instead.
- The existing Edit Points tests still pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress-log line.

title: Open: cap absurd effect sizes from a file (a huge glow made rendering ask for 34 GB)
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this while break-testing DeckCraft on Windows 11: damaged copies of the sample deck saved as .pptx, opened, rendered and saved again.

## The bug

A `.pptx` (or `.deckcraft`) can give an effect any size. Format Shape and `shape.effects` keep a glow to 150 pt, but a file is read as is, so a slide with `<a:glow rad="99999999999999999999">` reached the renderer with a glow of ~7.9 × 10^15 pt:

- at some sizes `vello_common` panics (`flatten_simd.rs:581`, range end index 8 out of range for slice of length 6). The command guard catches it, but the slide doesn't draw
- at others (a glow of 10^18 pt) rendering asked for **34 GB** in one allocation and the process aborted, which no guard can catch, so the app closes and unsaved work is lost

One bad file is enough.

## The fix

`deckcraft_format::sane_numbers`, which `repair` already runs on every opened file (`.pptx` and `.deckcraft`), now also caps effect sizes at what Format Shape allows, the way it already caps line widths and font sizes: glow 150 pt, soft edges 100 pt, shadow blur and distance 200 pt, reflection blur and distance 100 pt. Shadow scale and skew are kept to ±1000% and ±89°, and anything that isn't a number becomes 0. This covers shape effects and run effects in text and in table cells.

## Testing

- New engine test `opening_a_file_caps_absurd_effect_sizes`: a deck with every effect at 10^18 pt or NaN (shape, text and table-cell text), saved as `.deckcraft` and as `.pptx` and opened again. Every size comes back within the limits, and only then is the slide rendered, so the test can't trigger the huge allocation even when the cap is missing. Without the fix it fails on the first check (a shadow of 10^18 pt survives the load).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress-lo…

title: Open: give shapes that repeat an id in a .deckcraft file fresh ones
author: Zetenypapp
body:
**Upfront about how this was made:** I'm not a programmer. The fix, the test and this description were written by Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). It found this while break-testing DeckCraft on Windows 11: the sample deck saved as `.deckcraft`, with its numbers changed one kind at a time, then opened, rendered and saved again.

## The bug

A `.deckcraft` file whose shapes repeat an id (hand-edited, written by another tool, or damaged) opens as is, and the deck fails its own `Presentation::validate` ("slide N: duplicate shape id M"). Everything that finds a shape by id (selection, `id`/`ids` command params, the Selection Pane, the control channel and MCP) then gets the first of the shapes that share it, so the others can't be reached or edited by id. `repair` already gives repeated *slide* ids fresh ones, but not repeated shape ids. A `.pptx` isn't affected: its importer assigns ids itself.

## The fix

`repair` (run on every opened file) now gives each shape that repeats an id already used on its slide, layout or master, groups included, a fresh id from the deck's counter. The first shape keeps its id, and with it whatever animations and connectors point at. Decks without repeats aren't copied or changed. An exhausted id space leaves the rest as they are, as `repair` already does for slides (#407).

## Testing

- New engine test `opening_a_file_gives_repeated_shape_ids_fresh_ones`: a group of four shapes and an ellipse, all given the same id, saved as `.deckcraft` and opened again. The deck validates, all six shapes are there, the first keeps its id, the new ids come from the deck's counter, and the last shape can be selected by its own id. Without the fix it fails: five "duplicate shape id" problems.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes locally on Windows 11: fmt, pdf-deps, clippy, tests, assets, layers and wasm.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress-log line.
